knowledge_statements.scope_note: Real-valued measurable functions on a Lebesgue-measurable set $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $\Omega\in\mathcal B_n$. For $1\leq p<\infty$, set $\|u\|_{L^p(\Omega)}:=\left(\int_\Omega|u(x)|^p\,dx\right)^{1/p}$, and set $\|u\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)}:=\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{x\in\Omega}|u(x)|:=\inf\{\alpha\geq0:\mu(\{|u|>\alpha\})=0\}$. Let $\mathcal L^p(\Omega)$ consist of measurable functions with finite seminorm. Under $u\sim v\iff\|u-v\|_{L^p(\Omega)}=0\iff u=v$ almost everywhere, define $L^p(\Omega):=\mathcal L^p(\Omega)/\!\sim$ with the induced norm. Define $\mathcal L^p_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega):=\{u:u\text{ is measurable and }u\in\mathcal L^p(K)\text{ for every compact }K\subset\Omega\}$ and $L^p_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega):=\mathcal L^p_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)/\!\sim$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite integral or essential-supremum seminorm defines the measurable-function classes. Quotienting by almost-everywhere equality yields the normed $L^p$ spaces. Local $L^p$ membership requires finite $L^p$ size on every compact subset, followed by the same almost-everywhere quotient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L^p(\Omega)=\mathcal L^p(\Omega)/\!\sim,\quad u\sim v\iff u=v\ \text{a.e.};\qquad L^p_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)=\mathcal L^p_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)/\!\sim

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition of integration for simple and Bochner-integrable functions taking values in an ambient Banach space X.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let X be the ambient Banach space. For a simple function s(t)=\sum_{i=1}^m\mathbf 1_{E_i}(t)y_i, define \int_0^T s(t)\,dt:=\sum_{i=1}^m y_i\mu(E_i). A function f:[0,T]\to X is Bochner-integrable if there is a sequence of simple functions s_k such that s_k(t)\to f(t) almost everywhere and \int_0^T\|s_k(t)-f(t)\|_X\,dt\to0. In that case, define \int_0^T f(t)\,dt:=\lim_{k\to\infty}\int_0^T s_k(t)\,dt.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The integral of a simple vector-valued function is the measure-weighted sum of its component vectors. A function is Bochner-integrable when simple functions approximate it almost everywhere and in L1 norm; its integral is the limit of their integrals.
assumptions_latex: X\text{ is the ambient Banach space}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \int_0^T s(t)\,dt=\sum_{i=1}^m y_i\mu(E_i),\qquad \int_0^T f(t)\,dt=\lim_{k\to\infty}\int_0^T s_k(t)\,dt.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dunford–Pettis and de la Vallée-Poussin criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent weak sequential compactness, equi-integrability, uniform absolute continuity, and superlinear-gauge conditions in the ambient measure-space setting of the source.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\mathcal F\subset L^1(\Omega)\), the following are equivalent: \(\mathrm{(a)}\) every sequence in \(\mathcal F\) has a subsequence weakly convergent in \(L^1(\Omega)\); \(\mathrm{(b)}\) for every \(\varepsilon>0\) there exists \(\lambda>0\) such that \(\int_{\{|u|\geq\lambda\}}|u(x)|\,dx\leq\varepsilon\) for every \(u\in\mathcal F\); \(\mathrm{(c)}\) for every \(\varepsilon>0\) there exists \(\delta>0\) such that \(\int_B|u(x)|\,dx\leq\varepsilon\) for every \(u\in\mathcal F\) and every measurable \(B\) with measure at most \(\delta\); \(\mathrm{(d)}\) there exists a positive Borel function \(\Phi:[0,\infty)\to\overline{\mathbb R}_+\) such that \(\Phi(t)/t\to+\infty\) as \(t\to\infty\) and \(\sup_{u\in\mathcal F}\int_\Omega\Phi(|u(x)|)\,dx<+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a family in L1, sequential relative weak compactness, equi-integrable tails, uniform absolute continuity of its integrals, and a uniform superlinear-gauge bound are equivalent in the source's ambient measure-space setting.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathrm{(a)}\Longleftrightarrow\mathrm{(b)}\Longleftrightarrow\mathrm{(c)}\Longleftrightarrow\mathrm{(d)}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extended-real-valued scalar functions on Euclidean space and measurable subsets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A function $f:\mathbb R^n\to[-\infty,\infty]$ is Lebesgue measurable if $\{x\in\mathbb R^n:f(x)>\alpha\}\in\mathcal B_n$ for every $\alpha\in\mathbb R$. If $A\in\mathcal B_n$ and $f:A\to[-\infty,\infty]$, then $f$ is Lebesgue measurable on $A$ if its zero extension $\widetilde f$, defined by $\widetilde f=f$ on $A$ and $\widetilde f=0$ outside $A$, is Lebesgue measurable on $\mathbb R^n$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An extended-real function on Euclidean space is Lebesgue measurable when every strict superlevel set is measurable. Measurability on a measurable subset is defined using the zero extension.
assumptions_latex: A\in\mathcal B_n\text{ and }f:A\to[-\infty,\infty]\text{ in the subset case}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\text{ is measurable}\iff\{x:f(x)>\alpha\}\in\mathcal B_n\ \forall\alpha\in\mathbb R;\qquad f\text{ is measurable on }A\iff\widetilde f\text{ is measurable on }\mathbb R^n

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-$L^p$ measurable functions on a Lebesgue-measurable domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $\Omega\in\mathcal B_n$ and $p\in[1,\infty]$. For all $u,v\in\mathcal L^p(\Omega)$, $\|u-v\|_{L^p(\Omega)}=0$ if and only if $u=v$ almost everywhere on $\Omega$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two measurable functions in the finite-$L^p$ class have zero $L^p$ distance exactly when they agree almost everywhere.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|u-v\|_{L^p(\Omega)}=0\iff u=v\quad\text{a.e. on }\Omega

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonnegative Elementary Functions and Their Integral
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite nonnegative combinations of indicators of pairwise disjoint Lebesgue-measurable sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define $E_+(\mathbb R^n):=\left\{\sum_{k=1}^m\alpha_k1_{A_k}:m\in\mathbb N,\ A_k\in\mathcal B_n\text{ pairwise disjoint},\ \alpha_k\geq0\right\}$. For $f=\sum_{k=1}^m\alpha_k1_{A_k}\in E_+(\mathbb R^n)$, define $\int_{\mathbb R^n}f\,d\mu:=\sum_{k=1}^m\alpha_k\mu(A_k)$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative elementary function is a finite nonnegative combination of indicators of pairwise disjoint measurable sets. Its integral is the corresponding weighted sum of their measures.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: E_+(\mathbb R^n)=\left\{\sum_{k=1}^m\alpha_k1_{A_k}\right\},\qquad \int_{\mathbb R^n}\sum_{k=1}^m\alpha_k1_{A_k}\,d\mu=\sum_{k=1}^m\alpha_k\mu(A_k)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Simple and Strongly Measurable Vector-Valued Functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Measurability foundations for functions from a finite time interval into a vector space X.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A function s:[0,T]\to X is simple if s(t)=\sum_{i=1}^m\mathbf 1_{E_i}(t)y_i for Lebesgue-measurable sets E_i\subset[0,T] and points y_i\in X. A function f:[0,T]\to X is strongly measurable if there exist simple functions s_k:[0,T]\to X such that s_k(t)\to f(t) for almost every t\in[0,T].
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A vector-valued function is simple when it is a finite sum of fixed vectors multiplied by indicators of measurable sets. It is strongly measurable when it is an almost-everywhere pointwise limit of simple functions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: s(t)=\sum_{i=1}^m\mathbf 1_{E_i}(t)y_i\text{ is simple, and }f\text{ is strongly measurable}\iff\exists(s_k)\text{ simple with }s_k(t)\to f(t)\text{ a.e.}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonnegative and signed extended-real measurable functions on $\mathbb R^n$, and integration over measurable subsets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For measurable $f:\mathbb R^n\to[0,\infty]$ and a nondecreasing sequence $(f_k)\subset E_+(\mathbb R^n)$ satisfying $f=\sup_k f_k$, define $\int_{\mathbb R^n}f\,d\mu:=\sup_k\int_{\mathbb R^n}f_k\,d\mu$. For measurable $f:\mathbb R^n\to[-\infty,\infty]$, let $f^+=\max(f,0)$ and $f^-=\max(-f,0)$ and define $\int f\,d\mu:=\int f^+\,d\mu-\int f^-\,d\mu$ when at least one of the two terms is finite; the source calls $f$ integrable in this case. If $A\in\mathcal B_n$ and the zero extension $f1_A$ is integrable in this sense, define $\int_Af\,d\mu:=\int_{\mathbb R^n}f1_A\,d\mu$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The integral of a nonnegative measurable function is defined through an increasing elementary approximation. The signed integral is the positive-part integral minus the negative-part integral when the difference is defined, and integration over a measurable subset uses the zero extension. The source uses “integrable” whenever at least one part integral is finite.
assumptions_latex: f:\mathbb R^n\to[0,\infty]\text{ is measurable and }f_k\in E_+(\mathbb R^n),\ f_k\uparrow f
f:\mathbb R^n\to[-\infty,\infty]\text{ is measurable in the signed case}
A\in\mathcal B_n\text{ and }f1_A\text{ is integrable in the subset case}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \int f\,d\mu=\sup_k\int f_k\,d\mu;\qquad \int f\,d\mu=\int f^+\,d\mu-\int f^-\,d\mu;\qquad \int_Af\,d\mu=\int_{\mathbb R^n}f1_A\,d\mu

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Measurability under Lattice Limits and Elementary Approximation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lebesgue-measurable extended-real functions on $\mathbb R^n$.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If $(f_k)$ is any sequence of Lebesgue-measurable functions on $\mathbb R^n$, then $\sup_k f_k$, $\inf_k f_k$, $\limsup_{k\to\infty}f_k$, and $\liminf_{k\to\infty}f_k$ are Lebesgue measurable. If $f\geq0$ is Lebesgue measurable, then there exists a nondecreasing sequence $(g_k)_{k\in\mathbb N}\subset E_+(\mathbb R^n)$ such that $f=\sup_k g_k$ pointwise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Countable suprema, infima, upper limits, and lower limits of measurable functions are measurable. Every nonnegative measurable function is the pointwise supremum of an increasing sequence of nonnegative elementary functions.

f:\mathbb R^n\to[0,\infty]\text{ is Lebesgue measurable for the approximation assertion}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Measurability under Countable Set Operations and Limits
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stability of closed-valued measurable multifunctions under pointwise countable operations and set limits.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Gamma_j:I\rightrightarrows\mathbb R^n\), \(j\geq1\), be closed-valued and \(\mathcal L\)-measurable. The multifunction \(\Gamma\) is closed-valued and \(\mathcal L\)-measurable when defined pointwise by any of \(\Gamma(t)=\overline{\bigcup_{j\geq1}\Gamma_j(t)}\), \(\Gamma(t)=\bigcap_{j\geq1}\Gamma_j(t)\), \(\Gamma(t)=\limsup_{j\to\infty}\Gamma_j(t)\), or \(\Gamma(t)=\liminf_{j\to\infty}\Gamma_j(t)\). In particular, if the set limit \(\lim_{j\to\infty}\Gamma_j\) exists, it is measurable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Closed-valued measurable multifunctions remain closed-valued and measurable under closed countable union, countable intersection, set limsup, and set liminf. An existing set limit is therefore measurable.
assumptions_latex: \Gamma_j:I\rightrightarrows\mathbb R^n\text{ is closed-valued and }\mathcal L\text{-measurable for every }j\geq1
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \overline{\bigcup_{j\geq1}\Gamma_j},\ \bigcap_{j\geq1}\Gamma_j,\ \limsup_{j\to\infty}\Gamma_j,\ \liminf_{j\to\infty}\Gamma_j\text{ are closed-valued and }\mathcal L\text{-measurable}

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $V\subset\mathbb{R}^k$ be measurable and let $\Gamma:V\rightrightarrows\mathbb{R}^l$. The multifunction $\Gamma$ is measurable if it is closed-valued and, for every closed set $C\subset\mathbb{R}^l$, the hit preimage $\Gamma^{-1}(C):=\{x\in V:\Gamma(x)\cap C\neq\varnothing\}$ is measurable. knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equivalent Weak Convergences and Compactness for Range-Bounded Maps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Includes scalar maps and the stated finite-dimensional vector extension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: D\subset\mathbb R^N\text{ bounded open},\ K\subset\mathbb R\text{ bounded},\ \mathcal K:=\{k:D\to\mathbb R:k\text{ measurable},\ k(x)\in K\text{ a.e.}\}.\ \forall q\in[1,\infty),\ \forall\{k_n\}\subset\mathcal K:\quad k_n\overset{*}{\rightharpoonup}\text{ in }L^\infty(D)\iff k_n\rightharpoonup\text{ in }L^q(D)\iff k_n\to\text{ in }\mathcal D'(D).\ \text{If }K\text{ is also closed and convex, then }\mathcal K\text{ is convex and compact in each of these topologies.}
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For measurable functions on a bounded open set whose values lie almost everywhere in a fixed bounded set, convergence in the L-infinity weak-star topology, weak convergence in any finite Lq space, and distributional convergence are equivalent. If the range set is also closed and convex, the function class is convex and compact in these topologies. The assertions extend to maps taking values in a bounded subset of a finite-dimensional Euclidean space, with closedness and convexity required for the compactness conclusion.
assumptions_latex: D\subset\mathbb R^N\text{ is bounded and open}
\mathcal K=\{k:D\to\mathbb R:k\text{ measurable and }k(x)\in K\text{ a.e.}\}
K\text{ is closed and convex for the convexity and compactness conclusion}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: k_n\overset{*}{\rightharpoonup}_{L^\infty}k\iff k_n\rightharpoonup_{L^q}k\iff k_n\to k\text{ in }\mathcal D'(D);\quad K\text{ bounded, closed, convex}\Rightarrow\mathcal K\text{ convex and compact in all three topologies}.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two composition rules, respectively using inner semicontinuity and measurable graphs with outer semicontinuity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: (a) If \(S:T\rightrightarrows\mathbb R^n\) is measurable and \(M:\mathbb R^n\rightrightarrows\mathbb R^m\) is inner semicontinuous, then \((M\circ S)(t)=M(S(t))\) is measurable. (b) If \(S\) is closed-valued and measurable, each \(M(t,\cdot):\mathbb R^n\rightrightarrows\mathbb R^m\) is outer semicontinuous, and \(t\mapsto\operatorname{gph}M(t,\cdot)\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\) is measurable, then \(t\mapsto M(t,S(t))\) is measurable. The graph hypothesis holds in particular when \(M(t,\cdot)\) is independent of \(t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Composing a measurable multifunction with an inner-semicontinuous multifunction preserves measurability. A parameter-dependent outer-semicontinuous composition is also measurable when the inner multifunction is closed-valued and measurable and the outer mapping has a measurably varying graph.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Preservation of closed-valued measurability under substitution of a measurable trajectory, using the source's sequential set-limit continuity condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:I\times\mathbb R^n\rightrightarrows\mathbb R^k\) and let \(\bar x:I\to\mathbb R^n\) be Lebesgue measurable. knowledge_statements.statement_title: Measurability under intersections, unions, sums, and products
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Preservation rules for measurable set-valued mappings, with countability, closed-value, and finiteness conditions retained.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S_j:T\rightrightarrows\mathbb R^n\) be measurable for every \(j\in J\). Then: (a) if \(J\) is countable and every \(S_j\) is closed-valued, \(t\mapsto\bigcap_{j\in J}S_j(t)\) is measurable; (b) if \(J\) is countable, \(t\mapsto\bigcup_{j\in J}S_j(t)\) is measurable; (c) if \(J\) is finite, then for arbitrary \(\lambda_j\in\mathbb R\), \(t\mapsto\sum_{j\in J}\lambda_jS_j(t)\) is measurable. If \(J=\{1,\ldots,r\}\) and \(S_j:T\rightrightarrows\mathbb R^{n_j}\), then (d) \(t\mapsto S_1(t)\times\cdots\times S_r(t)\) is measurable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Countable unions of measurable multifunctions remain measurable; countable intersections do so when all values are closed. Finite scalar-weighted sums and finite Cartesian products of measurable multifunctions are also measurable.
assumptions_latex: \(S_j:T\rightrightarrows\mathbb R^n\text{ is measurable for every }j\in J\)
\(J\text{ is countable and each }S_j\text{ is closed-valued for intersections}\)
\(J\text{ is finite and }\lambda_j\in\mathbb R\text{ for sums}\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bigcap_jS_j(\cdot),\ \bigcup_jS_j(\cdot),\ \sum_j\lambda_jS_j(\cdot),\text{ and }\prod_{j=1}^rS_j(\cdot)\text{ are measurable under their respective assumptions.}\)

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterization of closed-valued multifunctions on a Lebesgue-measurable interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Gamma:I\rightrightarrows\mathbb R^n\) be closed-valued and let \(D=\{t\in I:\Gamma(t)\neq\varnothing\}\). The following are equivalent: (a) \(\Gamma\) is \(\mathcal L\)-measurable; (b) \(\operatorname{Gr}\Gamma\in\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal B(\mathbb R^n)\); (c) \(D\) is Lebesgue measurable and there exist Lebesgue-measurable functions \(\gamma_k:D\to\mathbb R^n\), \(k\geq1\), such that \(\Gamma(t)=\overline{\bigcup_{k=1}^{\infty}\{\gamma_k(t)\}}\) for every \(t\in D\). The representation in (c) is called a Castaing representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a closed-valued multifunction, measurability, product measurability of its graph, and existence of a countable measurable family dense in each nonempty value are equivalent. The last characterization is a Castaing representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (a)\Longleftrightarrow(b)\Longleftrightarrow(c)

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition by inverse images of open sets, with elementary measurable constructions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((T,\mathcal A)\) be a measurable space and define \(S^{-1}(O)=\{t\in T\mid S(t)\cap O\ne\varnothing\}\). A mapping \(S:T\rightrightarrows\mathbb R^n\) is measurable when \(S^{-1}(O)\in\mathcal A\) for every open \(O\subset\mathbb R^n\). Consequently, \(\operatorname{dom}S=S^{-1}(\mathbb R^n)\in\mathcal A\). For single-valued \(S\), this is ordinary measurability. Constant multifunctions and multifunctions constant on a finite or countable measurable partition are measurable; so are \(S(t)=D+a(t)\) and \(S(t)=\lambda(t)D\) when \(D\subset\mathbb R^n\) is fixed and \(a\) or \(\lambda\), respectively, is measurable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A set-valued map is measurable when the set of parameters whose value intersects any given open set is measurable. Its domain is then measurable. This agrees with ordinary measurability for single-valued maps and includes constant maps, measurable step maps, and measurable translations or scalar rescalings of a fixed set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S\text{ is measurable}\iff \forall O\subset\mathbb R^n\text{ open},\ S^{-1}(O)\in\mathcal A;\qquad \operatorname{dom}S\in\mathcal A.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Metric-Valued Measurability, Convergence in Measure, and Lp Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definitions and basic structural properties for measurable maps into separable metric or Hilbert spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $X,Y_1,\ldots,Y_k$ be separable metric spaces, $\mathbf Y=\prod_{i=1}^kY_i$, and $\mu\in\mathcal P(X)$. A product map $\mathbf r=(\mathbf r_1,\ldots,\mathbf r_k):X\to\mathbf Y$ is Borel (respectively, $\mu$-measurable) iff every component $\mathbf r_i$ is so; consequently $d_Y(\mathbf r(\cdot),\mathbf s(\cdot))$ is measurable for measurable $\mathbf r,\mathbf s:X\to Y$. One has $\mathbf r_n\to\mathbf r$ in measure iff $\mu(\{x:d_Y(\mathbf r_n(x),\mathbf r(x))>\varepsilon\})\to0$ for every $\varepsilon>0$. For $1\le p<\infty$, $L^p(\mu;Y)$ consists, modulo $\mu$-a.e. equality, of measurable $\mathbf r$ satisfying $\int_Xd_Y^p(\mathbf r(x),\bar y)\,d\mu(x)<\infty$ for some, equivalently every, $\bar y\in Y$, with distance $d_{L^p}(\mathbf r,\mathbf s)=(\int_Xd_Y^p(\mathbf r(x),\mathbf s(x))\,d\mu)^{1/p}$. This space is complete iff $Y$ is complete. If $Y$ is a separable Hilbert space, this metric is induced by the usual $L^p$ norm; every $\mathbf r\in L^1(\mu;Y)$ has a vector integral characterized by duality, and every proper convex lower-semicontinuous $\phi:Y\to(-\infty,+\infty]$ satisfies $\phi(\int_X\mathbf r\,d\mu)\le\int_X\phi(\mathbf r)\,d\mu$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite product of maps into separable metric spaces is measurable exactly when all its components are measurable. Convergence in measure is defined through the measure of sets on which the pointwise distance exceeds each positive tolerance. Metric-valued Lp spaces consist of maps having finite p-distance from one, hence every, reference point; their natural metric is complete exactly when the target is complete. For a separable Hilbert target, the metric comes from the usual Lp norm, and L1 maps admit vector integrals satisfying duality and Jensen's inequality.
assumptions_latex: Y\text{ is a separable Hilbert space for the norm, vector-integral, and Jensen assertions}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbf r\text{ is measurable}\iff(\forall i)\,\mathbf r_i\text{ is measurable};\quad \mathbf r_n\to\mathbf r\text{ in measure}\iff(\forall\varepsilon>0)\,\mu\{d_Y(\mathbf r_n,\mathbf r)>\varepsilon\}\to0;\quad L^p(\mu;Y)\text{ is complete}\iff Y\text{ is complete, with the stated Hilbert-valued integration properties.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Integrably Bounded Multifunction and Aumann Integral
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definitions for multifunctions on a compact real interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Gamma:[a,b]\rightrightarrows\mathbb{R}^n\). It is integrably bounded if there exists an integrable function \(\phi\) such that \(\|z\|\leq\phi(t)\) for every \(t\in[a,b]\) and every \(z\in\Gamma(t)\). Define \((\operatorname{co}\Gamma)(t):=\operatorname{co}(\Gamma(t))\). Its Aumann integral is \[\int\Gamma:=\left\{\int_a^b\gamma(t)\,dt:\gamma(\cdot)\text{ is a measurable selection of }\Gamma\right\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multifunction on an interval is integrably bounded when all its values are dominated in norm by one integrable function. Its convexification is defined pointwise, and its Aumann integral is the set of integrals of its measurable selections.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (\operatorname{co}\Gamma)(t)=\operatorname{co}(\Gamma(t)),\qquad \int\Gamma=\left\{\int_a^b\gamma(t)\,dt:\gamma\text{ is a measurable selection of }\Gamma\right\}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Regularity properties of a multifunction support Hamiltonian
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States three conditional properties of the support Hamiltonian: boundedness and Lipschitz continuity, upper semicontinuity along state-costate sequences, and measurability along measurable arguments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:[S,T]\times\mathbb R^n\rightrightarrows\mathbb R^n\) have closed values, and let \(H(t,x,p)=\sup_{v\in F(t,x)}\langle p,v\rangle\). (a) If \((t,x)\in\operatorname{dom}F\) and \(F(t,x)\subset cB\) for some \(c\ge 0\), then \(|H(t,x,p)|\le c\lVert p\rVert\) for every \(p\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(p\mapsto H(t,x,p)\) is Lipschitz with constant \(c\). (b) Fix \(t\in[S,T]\). If \(x_i\to x\), \(p_i\to p\), \((t,x_i)\in\operatorname{dom}F\), \(F(t,x_i)\subset cB\) for all \(i\), and \(\operatorname{Gr}F(t,\cdot)\) is closed, then \(\limsup_{i\to\infty}H(t,x_i,p_i)\le H(t,x,p)\). (c) If \(x:[S,T]\to\mathbb R^n\) and \(p:[S,T]\to\mathbb R^n\) are measurable, \((t,x(t))\in\operatorname{dom}F\) for all \(t\), and \(F\) is \(\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal B^n\)-measurable, then \(t\mapsto H(t,x(t),p(t))\) is measurable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the support Hamiltonian of a closed-valued multifunction, bounded value sets give a dual-variable bound and Lipschitz continuity. A uniformly bounded closed-graph condition gives upper semicontinuity along convergent state-costate sequences, while multifunction measurability gives measurability along measurable arguments.
assumptions_latex: F:[S,T]\times\mathbb R^n\rightrightarrows\mathbb R^n\text{ has closed values}
\text{Each conclusion is subject to its respective hypotheses in (a), (b), or (c)}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Under the respective hypotheses, }H\text{ satisfies the bound and Lipschitz property in (a), the limsup inequality in (b), and measurability in (c).}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Measurability of Parametric Infima and Attaining Selections
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Measurability of a marginal infimum, its attainment set, and an almost-everywhere measurable minimizing selection under Carathéodory and closed-valued measurability assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g:I\times\mathbb{R}^k\to\mathbb{R}\) be a Carathéodory function and let \(\Gamma:I\rightrightarrows\mathbb{R}^k\) be closed-valued, nonempty-valued, and measurable. Define \(\eta(t)=\inf_{\gamma\in\Gamma(t)}g(t,\gamma)\in\mathbb{R}\cup\{-\infty\}\). Then \(\eta\) is Lebesgue measurable. Let \(I'=\{t\in I:\inf_{\gamma'\in\Gamma(t)}g(t,\gamma')=g(t,\gamma)\text{ for some }\gamma\in\Gamma(t)\}\). Then \(I'\) is Lebesgue measurable, and there exists a measurable \(\gamma:I'\to\mathbb{R}^k\) such that \(\eta(t)=g(t,\gamma(t))\) for almost every \(t\in I'\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a Carathéodory integrand minimized over a closed, nonempty-valued measurable multifunction, the marginal infimum and its attainment set are measurable, and an attaining point can be selected measurably almost everywhere on that set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\eta\) and \(I'\) are Lebesgue measurable, and there exists measurable \(\gamma:I'\to\mathbb{R}^k\) such that \(\eta(t)=g(t,\gamma(t))\) for a.e. \(t\in I'\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential compactness and trajectory closure for uniformly controlled approximate solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Gamma\) be \(\mathcal L\times\mathcal B\)-measurable, and let \(x_j\) be arcs on \([a,b]\) such that \(x_j(t)\in X(t)\) and \(|\dot x_j(t)|\le \phi(t)\) for almost every \(t\). Suppose \(\dot x_j(t)\in\Gamma(t,x_j(t)+y_j(t))+r_j(t)B\) for \(t\in A_j\), where the measurable functions \(y_j,r_j\) converge uniformly to zero, the measurable sets \(A_j\subseteq[a,b]\) satisfy \(m(A_j)\to b-a\), and \(\{x_j(a)\}\) is bounded. Then some subsequence converges uniformly to an arc \(x\) that is a trajectory of \(\Gamma\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For measurable dynamics, arcs with a common almost-everywhere velocity bound, bounded initial values, vanishing state and velocity perturbations, and inclusion validity on sets whose measures approach the full interval possess a uniformly convergent subsequence whose limit is a genuine trajectory.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\,j_k\text{ and an arc }x\text{ such that }x_{j_k}\to x\text{ uniformly and }x\text{ is a trajectory of }\Gamma.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a Euclidean-valued multifunction, allowing empty values, and the associated notion of an almost-everywhere measurable selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^m\), a multifunction \(\Gamma:\Omega\rightrightarrows\mathbb R^n\) assigns to every \(x\in\Omega\) a possibly empty set \(\Gamma(x)\subseteq\mathbb R^n\). A measurable selection of \(\Gamma\) is a measurable function \(\gamma:\Omega\to\mathbb R^n\) such that \(\gamma(x)\in\Gamma(x)\) for almost every \(x\in\Omega\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multifunction assigns each point a possibly empty subset of the range space. A measurable selection is a measurable single-valued function that belongs to the assigned set almost everywhere.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \gamma\text{ is a measurable selection of }\Gamma\iff \gamma:\Omega\to\mathbb R^n\text{ is measurable and }\gamma(x)\in\Gamma(x)\text{ for a.e. }x\in\Omega.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dunford–Pettis weak compactness criterion on a finite interval
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes relative weak sequential compactness of a bounded family in finite-dimensional-valued L1 by uniform integrability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal S\subset L^1([S,T];\mathbb R^n)\) be bounded. The following are equivalent: (i) every sequence in \(\mathcal S\) has a subsequence converging weakly in \(L^1\) to an \(L^1\) function; (ii) for every \(\varepsilon>0\) there is \(\delta>0\) such that, for every measurable \(D\subset[S,T]\) with \(\operatorname{meas}(D)<\delta\) and every \(x\in\mathcal S\), \(\int_D\|x(t)\|\,dt<\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bounded family of integrable vector-valued functions is relatively weakly sequentially compact exactly when its integrals are uniformly small on measurable sets of sufficiently small measure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Weak sequential relative compactness of }\mathcal S\iff\mathcal S\text{ is uniformly integrable}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Measurability and Lipschitz Bound for the Multifunction Residual
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual properties associated with a measurably Lipschitz multifunction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If F is measurably Lipschitz on \Omega with rank function k, then for every x,v\in\mathbb{R}^n, the map t\mapsto\rho(t,x,v) is measurable. For every (t,x_1),(t,x_2)\in\Omega and v_1,v_2\in\mathbb{R}^n, \[|\rho(t,x_1,v_1)-\rho(t,x_2,v_2)|\le k(t)|x_1-x_2|+|v_1-v_2|.\] If F is closed and nonempty on \Omega, these two properties are also equivalent to F being measurably Lipschitz.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A measurably Lipschitz multifunction has a time-measurable residual that is Lipschitz in state and velocity. When the multifunction is closed and nonempty on the tube, these residual properties characterize measurable Lipschitzness.
assumptions_latex: F\text{ is measurably Lipschitz on }\Omega\text{ with rank function }k
F\text{ is closed and nonempty on }\Omega\text{ for the converse}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: t\mapsto\rho(t,x,v)\text{ is measurable},\quad |\rho(t,x_1,v_1)-\rho(t,x_2,v_2)|\le k(t)|x_1-x_2|+|v_1-v_2|,\text{ with equivalence under closedness and nonemptiness}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Regularity and Measurability of the Multifunction Residual
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives velocity Lipschitz continuity, joint state-velocity control, and measurable composition for distance to a multifunction value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $\rho_F(t,x,v):=\inf_{\eta\in F(t,x)}|\eta-v|$. For every $(t,x)\in\operatorname{dom}F$, $|\rho_F(t,x,v)-\rho_F(t,x,v')|\le|v-v'|$. If $\bar x+\epsilon B\subset\operatorname{dom}F$ and $F(t,x)\subset F(t,x')+k|x-x'|B$ for all $x,x'\in\bar x+\epsilon B$, then $|\rho_F(t,x,v)-\rho_F(t,x',v')|\le|v-v'|+k|x-x'|$. If $F$ is $\mathcal L\times\mathcal B^n$-measurable and measurable functions $y,v$ satisfy $\operatorname{Gr}y\subset\operatorname{dom}F$, then $t\mapsto\rho_F(t,y(t),v(t))$ is Lebesgue measurable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Distance to a multifunction value is 1-Lipschitz in the velocity. A Lipschitz inclusion condition on the values gives a joint state-velocity estimate, while measurability of the multifunction makes the residual measurable along measurable state and velocity functions.
assumptions_latex: F(t,x)\subset F(t,x')+k|x-x'|B\quad\forall x,x'\in\bar x+\epsilon B\text{ for the joint estimate}
F\text{ is }\mathcal L\times\mathcal B^n\text{-measurable and }y,v\text{ are measurable with }\operatorname{Gr}y\subset\operatorname{dom}F\text{ for measurable composition}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |\rho_F(t,x,v)-\rho_F(t,x,v')|\le|v-v'|;\quad |\rho_F(t,x,v)-\rho_F(t,x',v')|\le|v-v'|+k|x-x'|\text{ under the stated inclusion condition};\quad t\mapsto\rho_F(t,y(t),v(t))\text{ is measurable under the stated measurability hypotheses}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Aumann integral is invariant under pointwise convexification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-valued integration of measurable multifunctions on a finite interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $\Gamma:[S,T]\rightrightarrows\mathbb{R}^n$ be Lebesgue measurable with nonempty closed values. Suppose there exists $c\in L^1([S,T])$ such that $\Gamma(t)\subseteq c(t)B$ for every $t\in[S,T]$. Then
\[
\int_S^T\Gamma(s)\,ds=\int_S^T\operatorname{co}\Gamma(s)\,ds,
\]
where, for $A=\Gamma$ and $A=\operatorname{co}\Gamma$,
\[
\int_S^T A(s)\,ds:=\left\{\int_S^T\gamma(s)\,ds:\gamma\text{ is a Lebesgue-measurable selection of }A\right\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonempty closed-valued, Lebesgue-measurable, integrably bounded multifunction, taking the pointwise convex hull does not change the set of integrals of measurable selections.
assumptions_latex: \Gamma:[S,T]\rightrightarrows\mathbb{R}^n\text{ is Lebesgue measurable with nonempty closed values}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \int_S^T\Gamma(s)\,ds=\int_S^T\operatorname{co}\Gamma(s)\,ds

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Effective Domain of a Measurable Multifunction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the effective domain and records its measurability and invariance under null-set modification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\Gamma:\Omega\rightrightarrows\mathbb R^n\), define \(\operatorname{dom}\Gamma:=\{x\in\Omega:\Gamma(x)\neq\varnothing\}\). If \(\Omega\) is measurable and \(\Gamma\) is measurable, then \(\operatorname{dom}\Gamma=\Gamma^{-1}(\mathbb R^n)\) is measurable. Redefining \(\Gamma\) on a Lebesgue-null subset of \(\Omega\) does not change its measurability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The effective domain is the set of points where the multifunction has a nonempty value. For a measurable multifunction it is measurable, and changing the multifunction on a null set preserves measurability.
assumptions_latex: \Omega\text{ is Lebesgue measurable and }\Gamma\text{ is measurable for the measurability conclusions}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{dom}\Gamma=\{x\in\Omega:\Gamma(x)\neq\varnothing\}=\Gamma^{-1}(\mathbb R^n)\text{ is measurable};\qquad \widetilde\Gamma=\Gamma\text{ a.e.}\Rightarrow\bigl(\widetilde\Gamma\text{ is measurable}\iff\Gamma\text{ is measurable}\bigr).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-valued mappings, pointwise value properties, and hit-measurability on a Euclidean domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A multifunction \(\Gamma:\mathbb{R}^m\rightrightarrows\mathbb{R}^n\) assigns to each \(x\in\mathbb{R}^m\) a possibly empty set \(\Gamma(x)\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\). It is closed, compact, convex, or nonempty on \(S\subseteq\mathbb{R}^m\) when every value \(\Gamma(x)\), \(x\in S\), has the corresponding property. A multifunction \(\Gamma:S\rightrightarrows\mathbb{R}^n\) is measurable if \(\{x\in S:\Gamma(x)\cap C\neq\varnothing\}\) is Lebesgue measurable for every open \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\); equivalently, it suffices to require this for every closed \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multifunction assigns a possibly empty set to each point. A value property holds on S when every value over S has that property. Measurability means that the points whose values meet any open set form a Lebesgue-measurable set; equivalently, closed test sets may be used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Gamma\text{ is measurable}\iff \{x\in S:\Gamma(x)\cap C\neq\varnothing\}\text{ is Lebesgue measurable for every open, equivalently every closed, }C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Measurability Is Preserved by Pointwise Convexification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex-hull construction for measurable closed-valued multifunctions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G:\Omega\rightrightarrows\mathbb{R}^n\) be measurable and closed-valued, and define \(\Gamma(x):=\operatorname{co}G(x)\). Then \(\Gamma\) is measurable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The pointwise convex hull of a measurable closed-valued multifunction into Euclidean space is measurable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Gamma\text{ is measurable}

children.title: Graph-Inverse-Image Measurability Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Equivalent and regime-dependent descriptions of multifunction measurability.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Graph and inverse-image characterizations of multifunction measurability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Implications and equivalences among measurability, graph measurability, and Borel inverse-image measurability, including the completeness and nonclosed-valued regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let S:T\rightrightarrows\mathbb{R}^n be closed-valued. Write (a) for measurability of S, (b) for \operatorname{gph}S\in\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal B(\mathbb R^n), and (c) for S^{-1}(D)\in\mathcal A for every D\in\mathcal B(\mathbb R^n). Then (c)\Rightarrow(a)\Rightarrow(b). If (T,\mathcal A,\mu) is complete, (a), (b), and (c) are equivalent. In the complete case, (b)\Rightarrow(c)\Rightarrow(a) remains valid without assuming that S is closed-valued.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a closed-valued multifunction into Euclidean space, Borel inverse-image measurability implies multifunction measurability, which implies measurability of its graph. On a complete measure space, all three properties are equivalent; moreover, graph measurability still implies Borel inverse-image measurability and hence multifunction measurability even without closed-valuedness.
assumptions_latex: S(t)\text{ is closed for every }t\in T\text{ for the general chain }(c)\Rightarrow(a)\Rightarrow(b)
\mathcal B(\mathbb R^n)\text{ is the range Borel field}
(T,\mathcal A,\mu)\text{ is complete for the equivalence and nonclosed-valued conclusions}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (c)\Rightarrow(a)\Rightarrow(b);\qquad (T,\mathcal A,\mu)\text{ complete}\Rightarrow[(a)\Leftrightarrow(b)\Leftrightarrow(c)],\text{ with }(b)\Rightarrow(c)\Rightarrow(a)\text{ even when }S\text{ is not closed-valued}.

children.title: Graph Measurability
children.top_down_role: Measurability expressed through the graph of a multifunction.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Section consequence intrinsic to graph measurability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\operatorname{gph}F\in\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal B(Y)\), then for every fixed \(y\in Y\), \[\{\omega:y\in F(\omega)\}=\{\omega:(\omega,y)\in\operatorname{gph}F\}\in\mathcal A.\] Equivalently, \(\omega\mapsto\delta_{F(\omega)}(y)\) is measurable for each fixed \(y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A measurable graph has measurable membership sections for every fixed range point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{\omega:y\in F(\omega)\}\in\mathcal A\).

notation.meaning: Extended-real indicator of the value set

knowledge_statements.title: Measurability of Fixed-Value Membership Sections

assumptions_latex: \((Y,\mathcal B(Y))\) is a measurable space with its Borel sigma-algebra.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{gph}F\in\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal B(Y)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Product-sigma-algebra definition for a multifunction into a Borel space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a multifunction \(F:\Omega\rightrightarrows Y\), define its graph by \[\operatorname{gph}F:=\{(\omega,y)\in\Omega\times Y:y\in F(\omega)\}.\] The multifunction is graph measurable when \(\operatorname{gph}F\) belongs to the product sigma-algebra \(\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal B(Y)\). This property concerns joint measurability of membership pairs and does not, without additional hypotheses, assert measurability of projections of the graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multifunction is graph measurable when the set of parameter-value pairs belonging to its values is measurable in the product sigma-algebra.
knowledge_statements.title: Graph Measurability

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and content kind fit the Graph Measurability leaf, and the statement is mathematically precise, but no inspectable citation or authoritative locator is supplied.

children.title: Inverse-Image Measurability
children.top_down_role: Measurability expressed through inverse images of range-space sets.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed-valued separable-metric characterization of Effros measurability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y\) be separable metric and let \(F:\Omega\rightrightarrows Y\) have nonempty closed values. Then \(F\) is Effros measurable if and only if, for every \(y\in Y\), the function \[\omega\mapsto d(y,F(\omega))\] is \(\mathcal A\)-measurable. It is enough to test \(y\) in a fixed countable dense subset of \(Y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For nonempty closed values in a separable metric space, hit measurability is equivalent to measurability of point-to-value-set distance functions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\text{ is Effros measurable}\iff d(y,F(\cdot))\text{ is measurable for every }y\in Y\).

notation.meaning: Distance from a point to the multifunction value

knowledge_statements.title: Distance Characterization of Hit Measurability

assumptions_latex: \(Y\) is a topological space equipped with \(\mathcal B(Y)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F^{-}(O)\in\mathcal A\) for every open set \(O\subset Y\).

notation.meaning: Hit inverse image of a set

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effros, or hit, measurability; this is not ordinary inverse-image notation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a multifunction \(F:\Omega\rightrightarrows Y\) and a set \(B\subset Y\), its hit inverse image is \[F^{-}(B):=\{\omega\in\Omega:F(\omega)\cap B\neq\varnothing\}.\] The multifunction is inverse-image measurable, also called Effros measurable, when \(F^{-}(O)\in\mathcal A\) for every open set \(O\subset Y\). If \(Y\) is second countable, it suffices to verify this condition on a countable base of its topology.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multifunction is inverse-image measurable when the parameters whose values meet any open set form a measurable set.
knowledge_statements.title: Inverse-Image Measurability

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The hit-inverse-image definition, countable-base observation, and definition content kind fit the leaf, but the record has no source with a specific locator.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: States the closed-set definition, the equivalent compact-set test, and the failure of open-set hit measurability to characterize this notion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) be measurable and define \(\Gamma^{-1}(V):=\{x\in\Omega:\Gamma(x)\cap V\neq\varnothing\}\). The multifunction \(\Gamma:\Omega\rightrightarrows\mathbb R^n\) is measurable if \(\Gamma^{-1}(V)\) is Lebesgue measurable for every closed set \(V\subseteq\mathbb R^n\). Equivalently, it suffices to require this for every compact set \(V\). Such measurability implies that \(\Gamma^{-1}(U)\) is measurable for every open set \(U\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), but the open-set property alone does not characterize measurability in this definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multifunction is measurable when every closed-set hit inverse image is measurable. Compact sets provide an equivalent test. Open-set hit inverse images are then measurable, but that property alone is not sufficient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigl[\forall V\subseteq\mathbb R^n\text{ closed},\ \Gamma^{-1}(V)\text{ is measurable}\bigr]\iff\bigl[\forall K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\text{ compact},\ \Gamma^{-1}(K)\text{ is measurable}\bigr],\qquad \Gamma\text{ measurable}\Rightarrow\Gamma^{-1}(U)\text{ measurable for every open }U,\text{ without a converse in general}.

children.title: Representation Equivalence Regimes
children.top_down_role: Range-space and value-set settings where the two representations coincide.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Borel Graphs Give Universally Measurable Hit Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Graph-to-hit implication after universal completion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) and \(Y\) be standard Borel spaces and let \(B=\operatorname{gph}F\subset S\times Y\) be Borel. For every Borel set \(C\subset Y\), \[F^{-}(C)=\operatorname{proj}_S\bigl(B\cap(S\times C)\bigr)\] is analytic and therefore universally measurable. Consequently, relative to the universal completion of \(\mathcal B(S)\), every Borel-graph multifunction is hit measurable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Borel graph has analytic hit projections, so graph measurability implies hit measurability after universal completion of the domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F^{-}(C)\) is universally measurable for every Borel \(C\subset Y\).

notation.meaning: Hit inverse image of the set

knowledge_statements.title: Borel Graphs Give Universally Measurable Hit Sets

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Closed-Valued Hit Measurability Implies Graph Measurability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hit-to-graph implication for a Polish range.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\Omega,\mathcal A)\) be a measurable space, let \(Y\) be Polish, and let \(F:\Omega\rightrightarrows Y\) have nonempty closed values. If \(F\) is Effros measurable, then \[\operatorname{gph}F\in\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal B(Y).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonempty closed-valued Effros-measurable multifunction into a Polish space has a measurable graph.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is nonempty closed-valued and Effros measurable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{gph}F\in\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal B(Y)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Closed-Valued Hit Measurability Implies Graph Measurability

assumptions_latex: \(S\) is a standard Borel space and \(\mathcal A\) is the completion of its Borel sigma-algebra under a probability measure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\) is Effros measurable if and only if \(\operatorname{gph}F\in\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal B(Y)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Completed standard-Borel regime with a Polish range and closed fibers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) be standard Borel, let \(\mathcal A\) be the completion of \(\mathcal B(S)\) under a probability measure, and let \(Y\) be Polish. For every nonempty closed-valued multifunction \(F:S\rightrightarrows Y\), the following are equivalent: \(F^{-}(O)\in\mathcal A\) for every open \(O\subset Y\), and \(\operatorname{gph}F\in\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal B(Y)\). The closed-fiber and completed standard-Borel hypotheses ensure that the relevant graph sections and projections remain measurable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For closed-valued multifunctions on a completed standard Borel probability space with Polish range, graph and hit measurability coincide.
knowledge_statements.title: Representation Equivalence Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A theorem is the appropriate content kind for this equivalence-regime leaf. However, the exact equivalence involving a completed domain sigma-algebra and the product sigma-algebra depends delicately on the stated measurable-space hypotheses and requires an authoritative theorem locator before the version can be accepted.

children.title: Representation Separation Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Settings where graph-based and inverse-image criteria require distinct treatment.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Hit Measurability Does Not Control Nonclosed Graphs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hit-to-graph separation caused by dense nonclosed values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Omega=\{0,1\}\) carry the trivial sigma-algebra \(\{\varnothing,\Omega\}\), let \(Y=\mathbb R\), and choose \(a\in\mathbb R\setminus\mathbb Q\). Define \(F(0)=\mathbb Q\) and \(F(1)=\mathbb Q\cup\{a\}\). Every nonempty open set meets both values, so \(F^{-}(O)=\Omega\) for every nonempty open \(O\), and \(F\) is Effros measurable. However, \(\{\omega:a\in F(\omega)\}=\{1\}\notin\mathcal A\); hence \(\operatorname{gph}F\notin\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal B(\mathbb R)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dense nonclosed values can make all open hit sets trivial while hiding a nonmeasurable membership section, so hit measurability need not imply graph measurability.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\) is Effros measurable but not graph measurable.

notation.meaning: Fixed irrational point distinguishing the two values

knowledge_statements.title: Hit Measurability Does Not Control Nonclosed Graphs

assumptions_latex: \(S=Y=\mathbb N^{\mathbb N}\) carry their standard Borel sigma-algebras.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Graph measurability need not imply inverse-image measurability when fiber regularity or completion assumptions are absent.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection obstruction on an uncompleted standard Borel space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: There exists a Borel set \(B\subset S\times Y\), with \(S=Y=\mathbb N^{\mathbb N}\), whose projection \(\operatorname{proj}_S B\) is analytic but not Borel. Define \(F(s):=B_s=\{y:(s,y)\in B\}\). Then \(\operatorname{gph}F=B\) is Borel measurable, whereas \[F^{-}(Y)=\{s:F(s)\neq\varnothing\}=\operatorname{proj}_S B\] is not Borel. Thus graph measurability alone does not imply inverse-image measurability; closed fibers, suitable projection hypotheses, or completion of the domain sigma-algebra are substantive requirements.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Borel graph can have a non-Borel projection, so graph measurability alone need not yield hit measurability.
knowledge_statements.title: Representation Separation Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The projection counterexample correctly expresses a representation-separation boundary, and failure_boundary is the correct content kind. The existence of the specified Borel set with analytic non-Borel projection is the essential nontrivial claim and has no cited source.

children.title: Closed-Valued Measurable Mappings
children.top_down_role: Measurable multifunctions whose values are closed sets.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonemptiness and range-regularity boundaries of the standard selection theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Closed-valuedness permits empty fibers, which preclude a selection. Open-hit measurability and nonempty closed values in an arbitrary topological range do not by themselves fall under the Kuratowski–Ryll-Nardzewski theorem; Polish or an appropriate standard-Borel range hypothesis is substantive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Empty fibers prevent selection, and the standard measurable-selection theorem requires descriptive regularity of the range.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F(\omega)=\varnothing\Rightarrow\nexists f(\omega)\in F(\omega).
knowledge_statements.title: Selection Hypotheses Are Substantive

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Measurable selection for nonempty closed-valued Effros-measurable mappings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(Y\) is Polish and \(F:\Omega\rightrightarrows Y\) is Effros measurable with nonempty closed values, then there is an \(\mathcal A/\mathcal B(Y)\)-measurable map \(f:\Omega\to Y\) such that \(f(\omega)\in F(\omega)\) for every \(\omega\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonempty closed-valued Effros-measurable multifunction into a Polish space has a measurable selection.
assumptions_latex: \(F(\omega)\) is nonempty and closed for every \(\omega\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists f:\Omega\to Y\text{ measurable with }f(\omega)\in F(\omega)\ \forall\omega.
knowledge_statements.title: Kuratowski–Ryll-Nardzewski Selection Theorem

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent tests for nonempty closed-valued multifunctions in a Polish range.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y\) be Polish and let \(F:\Omega\rightrightarrows Y\) have nonempty closed values. Effros measurability of \(F\) is equivalent to measurability of \(\omega\mapsto d(y,F(\omega))\) for every \(y\in Y\), and also to the existence of measurable selections \((f_n)_{n\ge1}\) satisfying \(F(\omega)=\overline{\{f_n(\omega):n\ge1\}}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For nonempty closed values in a Polish space, open-hit measurability, measurable distance functions, and a Castaing representation are equivalent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\text{ is Effros measurable}\iff d(y,F(\cdot))\text{ is measurable for every }y\iff F\text{ admits a Castaing representation}.

notation.meaning: Distance from y to the fiber

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(\omega)\) is closed for every \(\omega\), and \(F^{-}(O)\in\mathcal A\) for every open \(O\subset Y\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equivalent Tests for Closed-Valued Multifunction Measurability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inverse-image, containment, countable-ball, and distance-function criteria under closed-valuedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S:T\rightrightarrows\mathbb R^n\) be closed-valued. The following are equivalent: \(S\) is measurable; \(S^{-1}(C)\in\mathcal A\) for every closed set \(C\), every compact set \(C\), every closed ball, or every rational closed ball; \(S^{-1}(O)\in\mathcal A\) for every open ball or every rational open ball; \(\{t\mid S(t)\subset O\}\in\mathcal A\) for every open \(O\); \(\{t\mid S(t)\subset C\}\in\mathcal A\) for every closed \(C\); and, for every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), \(t\mapsto d(x,S(t))\) is measurable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a closed-valued multifunction, measurability can equivalently be tested using inverse images of closed or compact sets, open or closed balls—including only rational balls—containment in open or closed sets, or measurability of every point-to-value distance function.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Conditions (a)--(j), including measurability of }S\text{ and of every }t\mapsto d(x,S(t)),\text{ are equivalent}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Measurability of Tangent and Normal Cone Mappings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Measurability of tangent, regular tangent, normal, regular normal, and normal-graph mappings induced by a closed-valued measurable multifunction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let S:T\rightrightarrows\mathbb{R}^n be closed-valued and measurable, and let x:T\to\mathbb{R}^n be measurable with x(t)\in S(t) for every t. Then the mappings
\[
t\mapsto T_{S(t)}(x(t)),\quad t\mapsto\widehat T_{S(t)}(x(t)),\quad t\mapsto N_{S(t)}(x(t)),\quad t\mapsto\widehat N_{S(t)}(x(t))
\]
are closed-valued and measurable. Moreover,
\[
t\mapsto\operatorname{gph}N_{S(t)}=\{(y,v)\mid y\in S(t),\ v\in N_{S(t)}(y)\}
\]
is closed-valued and measurable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a closed-valued measurable multifunction and a measurable selection, its tangent, regular tangent, normal, and regular normal cone mappings along that selection are closed-valued and measurable. The mapping assigning the graph of the normal-cone mapping is also closed-valued and measurable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: t\mapsto T_{S(t)}(x(t)),\ t\mapsto\widehat T_{S(t)}(x(t)),\ t\mapsto N_{S(t)}(x(t)),\ t\mapsto\widehat N_{S(t)}(x(t)),\text{ and }t\mapsto\operatorname{gph}N_{S(t)}\text{ are closed-valued and measurable}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Weak Closure of Approximate Multifunction Selections
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak L1 closure under almost-everywhere parameter convergence, integrable domination, vanishing inclusion errors, and exceptional sets of vanishing measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let I=[a,b], let Q\subset I\times\mathbb R^\ell be closed, and let \Gamma:Q\rightrightarrows\mathbb R^n have closed convex values. For each t\in I, suppose G(t)=\{(u,z):(t,u)\in Q,\ z\in\Gamma(t,u)\} is closed and nonempty. Suppose t\mapsto H_{\Gamma(t,u(t))}(p) is measurable for every measurable admissible u and every p\in\mathbb R^n, and \Gamma(t,u)\subset B(0,k(t)) for some summable k and every (t,u)\in Q. Let u_i be measurable and admissible almost everywhere, with u_i\to u_* almost everywhere. Let |z_i(t)|\le k(t) almost everywhere and let the components of z_i converge weakly in L^1(I) to those of z_*. If measurable sets \Omega_i\subset I satisfy \operatorname{meas}(\Omega_i)\to b-a and z_i(t)\in\Gamma(t,u_i(t))+B(0,r_i(t)) for almost every t\in\Omega_i, where r_i\ge0 and r_i\to0 in L^1(I), then z_*(t)\in\Gamma(t,u_*(t)) for almost every t\in I.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the stated graph-closedness, support-function measurability, and integrable-boundedness assumptions, approximate selections remain feasible when their parameters converge almost everywhere, the selections converge weakly in L1, the inclusion errors vanish in L1, and the exceptional sets have vanishing measure.
assumptions_latex: I=[a,b],\quad Q\subset I\times\mathbb R^\ell\text{ is closed},\quad \Gamma(t,u)\text{ is closed and convex}.
G(t)=\{(u,z):(t,u)\in Q,\ z\in\Gamma(t,u)\}\text{ is closed and nonempty for every }t\in I.
t\mapsto H_{\Gamma(t,u(t))}(p)\text{ is measurable for every measurable admissible }u\text{ and every }p\in\mathbb R^n.
k\in L^1(I),\quad \Gamma(t,u)\subset B(0,k(t))\text{ for every }(t,u)\in Q.
(t,u_i(t))\in Q\text{ a.e.},\quad u_i\to u_*\text{ a.e.},\quad |z_i(t)|\le k(t)\text{ a.e.},\quad z_i\rightharpoonup z_*\text{ componentwise in }L^1(I).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: z_*(t)\in\Gamma(t,u_*(t))\quad\text{for a.e. }t\in[a,b].

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lusin-type characterizations of closed-valued measurable multifunctions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence of measurability with near-continuity, near-outer-semicontinuity, and almost-everywhere agreement with a Borel-graph representative.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let T\in\mathcal B(\mathbb R^d), let \mathcal A=\mathcal L(T), let \mu be d-dimensional Lebesgue measure restricted to \mathcal A, and let S:T\rightrightarrows\mathbb R^n be closed-valued. Then S is measurable if and only if each of the following equivalent conditions holds: (i) for every \varepsilon>0 there is a closed T_\varepsilon\subset T with \mu(T\setminus T_\varepsilon)<\varepsilon such that S|_{T_\varepsilon} is continuous; (ii) the same assertion holds with outer semicontinuity in place of continuity; (iii) there is a closed-valued R:T\rightrightarrows\mathbb R^n with \operatorname{gph}R\in\mathcal B(T\times\mathbb R^n) such that R=S on some T'\in\mathcal A satisfying \mu(T\setminus T')=0. If \mu(T)<\infty, the sets T_\varepsilon in (i) and (ii) may be chosen compact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed-valued multifunction on a Borel subset of Euclidean space is Lebesgue measurable exactly when, outside sets of arbitrarily small measure, it is continuous; equivalently, it is outer semicontinuous there. This is also equivalent to agreeing almost everywhere with a closed-valued multifunction having a Borel graph. When the domain has finite measure, the large closed subsets may be chosen compact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S\text{ measurable}\Longleftrightarrow(i)\Longleftrightarrow(ii)\Longleftrightarrow(iii),\qquad \mu(T)<\infty\Rightarrow T_\varepsilon\text{ may be chosen compact}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Closed Noncompact Fibers Need Not Give Attainment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of continuous maximum attainment without compactness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(C=[0,\infty)\) and \(g(x)=1-e^{-x}\), the set \(C\) is closed and \(g\) is continuous, but \(\sup_{x\in C}g(x)=1\) is not attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuous objective need not attain its supremum on a closed noncompact fiber.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sup_{x\in[0,\infty)}(1-e^{-x})=1\text{ and }1-e^{-x}<1\ \forall x.
knowledge_statements.title: Closed Noncompact Fibers Need Not Give Attainment

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise distance attainment and measurable nearest-point selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(F(\omega)\) is nonempty compact in a metric space, then \(d(y,F(\omega))=\min_{z\in F(\omega)}d(y,z)\), and the nearest-point set is nonempty compact. If the range is Polish and \(F\) is measurable, this nearest-point multifunction is measurable and admits a measurable selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Distance to a nonempty compact fiber is attained, and under Polish measurable data a nearest point can be selected measurably.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) has nonempty compact values in a metric space.
For the measurable conclusion, the range is Polish and \(F\) is measurable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname*{argmin}_{z\in F(\omega)}d(y,z)\ne\varnothing,\text{ with a measurable selection under the additional hypotheses}.
knowledge_statements.title: Compact-Fiber Distance Attainment

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Measurable Maximum Theorem for Compact Fibers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Measurable values and optimizers for Carathéodory objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y\) be Polish, let \(F:\Omega\rightrightarrows Y\) be nonempty compact-valued and Effros measurable, and let \(g:\Omega\times Y\to\mathbb R\) be Carathéodory. Then \(v(\omega)=\max_{y\in F(\omega)}g(\omega,y)\) is measurable, the argmax mapping is nonempty compact-valued and measurable, and it admits a measurable selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Carathéodory objective over nonempty compact measurable fibers has a measurable maximum value and a measurable maximizer.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is nonempty compact-valued and Effros measurable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: v\text{ is measurable and }\operatorname*{argmax}_{y\in F(\omega)}g(\omega,y)\text{ admits a measurable selection}.
knowledge_statements.title: Measurable Maximum Theorem for Compact Fibers

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(\omega)\) is compact for every \(\omega\), and \(F^{-}(O)\in\mathcal A\) for every open \(O\subset Y\).

children.title: Value-Set Regime Transitions
children.top_down_role: Changes in measurability and selection behavior across value-set compactness regimes.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Boundedness Does Not Replace Total Boundedness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Infinite-dimensional obstruction to the finite-dimensional compactness upgrade.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In every infinite-dimensional normed space \(X\), the closed unit ball \(\overline B_X\) is closed and bounded but not norm compact. Hence boundedness cannot replace total boundedness in the closed-to-compact transition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Closed bounded fibers need not be norm compact in infinite-dimensional spaces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \overline B_X\text{ is closed and bounded but not norm compact}.
knowledge_statements.title: Boundedness Does Not Replace Total Boundedness

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact metric threshold upgrading closed fibers to compact fibers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In a complete metric space, a set is compact if and only if it is closed and totally bounded. Consequently, if every fiber of \(F\) is closed, then \(F\) is compact-valued exactly when every fiber is totally bounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In a complete metric range, total boundedness is exactly the additional fiber condition needed to upgrade closed values to compact values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F(\omega)\text{ is compact}\iff F(\omega)\text{ is totally bounded}\quad\forall\omega.
knowledge_statements.title: Complete-Metric Compactness Transition

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fiberwise weak compactness alternative in reflexive Banach spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(X\) is reflexive, every norm-closed bounded convex subset of \(X\) is weakly compact. Thus norm-closed bounded convex fibers are compact in the weak topology, although they need not be norm compact. This fiberwise conclusion alone makes no assertion that norm-Effros measurability is equivalent to weak-Effros measurability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reflexivity upgrades closed bounded convex fibers to weak compactness, but neither to norm compactness nor automatically to weak measurability.
assumptions_latex: Each fiber is norm closed, bounded, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F(\omega)\text{ is weakly compact for every }\omega.
knowledge_statements.title: Weak-Topology Compactness Upgrade

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Compact-valuedness implies closed-valuedness; the converse generally fails, but holds for closed bounded fibers in finite-dimensional normed spaces.

notation.meaning: Closed unit ball of a normed space

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transition between compact and closed fiber regimes.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 5. Set-Valued Mappings p. 148

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(Y\) is Hausdorff, every compact-valued measurable multifunction is closed-valued measurable. For \(Y=\mathbb R^d\), a closed-valued multifunction whose fibers are bounded is compact-valued by finite-dimensional compactness. This transition fails in an infinite-dimensional normed space \(X\): the constant multifunction \(F(\omega)=\overline B_X\) is measurable and has closed bounded values, while \(\overline B_X\) is not compact when \(X\) is infinite-dimensional.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compact fibers are closed in Hausdorff spaces; closed bounded fibers become compact in finite dimensions, but not in infinite-dimensional normed spaces.
knowledge_statements.title: Value-Set Regime Transitions

children.title: Measurable Selection Principles
children.top_down_role: Selection theorem families connecting measurable sets with measurable decisions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Countable-selector representation of closed-valued measurable multifunctions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y\) be Polish and let \(F:\Omega\rightrightarrows Y\) have nonempty closed values. Then \(F\) is Effros measurable if and only if there exist measurable selections \(f_n:\Omega\to Y\) such that \[F(\omega)=\overline{\{f_n(\omega):n\in\mathbb N\}}\qquad(\omega\in\Omega).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonempty closed-valued multifunction into a Polish space is Effros measurable exactly when it is pointwise generated densely by countably many measurable selections.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\text{ is Effros measurable}\iff F(\omega)=\overline{\{f_n(\omega):n\in\mathbb N\}}\) for measurable selections \(f_n\).
knowledge_statements.title: Castaing Representation Theorem

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selection principle for parameterized normal-integrand minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((T,\mathcal A,\mu)\) be complete and sigma-finite, let \(X\) be Polish, and let \(h:T\times X\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) be a normal integrand. Put \(m(t)=\inf_x h(t,x)\). For every measurable \(\varepsilon:T\to(0,\infty)\), on the measurable set where \(m(t)\in\mathbb R\) there exists a measurable \(x_\varepsilon(t)\) satisfying \[h(t,x_\varepsilon(t))<m(t)+\varepsilon(t).\] If the argmin multifunction is nonempty, closed-valued, and Effros measurable, it admits a measurable exact minimizer selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normal-integrand minimization admits measurable strict epsilon-minimizers, and measurable nonempty closed argmin sets admit exact measurable minimizers.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is Polish and \(h\) is a normal integrand.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists x_\varepsilon\text{ measurable}:h(t,x_\varepsilon(t))<m(t)+\varepsilon(t)\) wherever \(m(t)\in\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.title: Measurable Epsilon-Minimizer Selection

assumptions_latex: \(F:\Omega\rightrightarrows Y\) is Effros measurable with nonempty closed values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exists an \(\mathcal A/\mathcal B(Y)\)-measurable map \(f\) satisfying \(f(\omega)\in F(\omega)\) for every \(\omega\in\Omega\).

notation.meaning: A measurable selection of the multifunction

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Kuratowski–Ryll-Nardzewski closed-valued selection theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\Omega,\mathcal A)\) be a measurable space, let \(Y\) be Polish, and let \(F:\Omega\rightrightarrows Y\) have nonempty closed values. If \(F^{-}(O)\in\mathcal A\) for every open set \(O\subset Y\), then there exists an \(\mathcal A/\mathcal B(Y)\)-measurable map \(f:\Omega\to Y\) such that \[f(\omega)\in F(\omega)\qquad\text{for every }\omega\in\Omega.\] Such a map is called a measurable selection of \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every nonempty closed-valued Effros-measurable multifunction into a Polish space admits a measurable selection.
knowledge_statements.title: Measurable Selection Principles

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The statement is the Kuratowski-Ryll-Nardzewski measurable selection theorem with appropriate hypotheses, and theorem is the correct content kind for the topic. No authoritative theorem or page locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Measurable Finite-Mixture Attainment of the Pointwise Biconjugate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The second displayed identity contains an apparent coefficient-symbol extraction error. It is normalized to \(\ell_i\), consistently with the measurable weight vector introduced in the proposition and the preceding identity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every measurable mapping \(p:\Omega\to\mathbb R^m\), there exist a measurable mapping \(\widetilde\ell=(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_{m+1}):\Omega\to E_{m+1}\) and measurable mappings \(q_i:\Omega\to\mathbb R^m\), \(i=1,\ldots,m+1\), such that for almost every \(x\in\Omega\), \[f^{**}(x;p(x))=\sum_{i=1}^{m+1}\ell_i(x)f(x,q_i(x)),\qquad \sum_{i=1}^{m+1}\ell_i(x)q_i(x)=p(x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every measurable field p has measurable mixture weights and measurable component fields that attain the pointwise biconjugate value and reproduce p as their barycenter almost everywhere.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\,\widetilde\ell:\Omega\to E_{m+1},\ q_i:\Omega\to\mathbb R^m\text{ measurable such that the two displayed identities hold almost everywhere.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Measurability of Optimal Values and Solutions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Allows empty minimizer sets and extended-real optimal values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a normal integrand \(f:T\times\mathbb{R}^n\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}\), define \(p(t)=\inf_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}f(t,x)\) and \(P(t)=\operatorname{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}f(t,x)\). Then \(p:T\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}\) is measurable and \(P:T\rightrightarrows\mathbb{R}^n\) is closed-valued and measurable. Consequently, \(A=\{t\mid P(t)\neq\varnothing\}\) is measurable, and there exists a measurable function \(x:A\to\mathbb{R}^n\) such that \(x(t)\in P(t)\) for every \(t\in A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a normal integrand, the parametric infimum is measurable and the argmin mapping is closed-valued and measurable. The parameters at which a minimizer exists form a measurable set, on which a measurable minimizing selection exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p\text{ is measurable},\quad P\text{ is closed-valued and measurable},\quad \{t\mid P(t)\neq\varnothing\}\text{ is measurable and admits a measurable minimizing selection}.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Measurable selection of parameterized feasible points for a Carathéodory constraint system.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definitions for measurable integrands on products of Polish spaces, with continuity or lower semicontinuity required only for almost every parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let X_1,X_2 be Polish spaces, let \mu\in\mathcal P(X_1), and let \mathcal L be the \sigma-algebra of \mu-measurable subsets of X_1. An \mathcal L\otimes\mathcal B(X_2)-measurable function f:X_1\times X_2\to\mathbb R is called a Carathéodory integrand when x_2\mapsto f(x_1,x_2) is continuous for \mu-almost every x_1. An \mathcal L\otimes\mathcal B(X_2)-measurable function f:X_1\times X_2\to[0,+\infty] is called a normal integrand when x_2\mapsto f(x_1,x_2) is lower semicontinuous for \mu-almost every x_1.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A jointly measurable real-valued integrand is called Carathéodory when its second-variable sections are continuous for almost every first-variable parameter. A jointly measurable nonnegative extended-real-valued integrand is called normal when those sections are lower semicontinuous almost everywhere.
assumptions_latex: f:X_1\times X_2\to\mathbb R\text{ is }\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal B(X_2)\text{-measurable in the Carathéodory case}
f:X_1\times X_2\to[0,+\infty]\text{ is }\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal B(X_2)\text{-measurable in the normal case}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\text{ is called Carathéodory when }f(x_1,\cdot)\text{ is continuous for }\mu\text{-a.e. }x_1;\quad f\text{ is called normal when }f(x_1,\cdot)\text{ is l.s.c. for }\mu\text{-a.e. }x_1.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Joint Measurability Criterion for Normal Integrands
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Forward implication is unconditional in the stated framework; the converse requires completeness of the parameter measurable space with respect to a measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(f:T\times\mathbb{R}^n\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}\) is a normal integrand, then \((t,x)\mapsto f(t,x)\) is \(\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal B(\mathbb{R}^n)\)-measurable and \(x\mapsto f(t,x)\) is lower semicontinuous for every \(t\). Conversely, if these two properties hold and \((T,\mathcal A)\) is complete with respect to some measure \(\mu\), then \(f\) is a normal integrand; in particular, this applies to \(T=\mathbb{R}^d\) with \(\mathcal A=\mathcal L(\mathbb{R}^d)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A normal integrand is jointly measurable and lower semicontinuous in its state variable. Under completeness of the parameter measurable space, joint measurability together with statewise lower semicontinuity also implies normality.
assumptions_latex: (T,\mathcal A)\text{ is complete with respect to some measure }\mu\text{ for the converse}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\text{ normal}\Rightarrow f\text{ is }\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal B(\mathbb{R}^n)\text{-measurable and }f(t,\cdot)\text{ is lsc};\quad \text{under completeness, the converse holds}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Normal integrand and measurable substitution property
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the extract's Borel-representative definition and records its measurable-section and measurable-substitution consequences together with the stated failure boundary. Corrupted closure formulas are excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $B\subset\mathbb R^p$ be Borel. A mapping $f:\Omega\times B\to\overline{\mathbb R}$ is a normal integrand if $f(x,\cdot)$ is lower semicontinuous on $B$ for almost every $x\in\Omega$ and there exists a Borel function $\widetilde f:\Omega\times B\to\overline{\mathbb R}$ such that $\widetilde f(x,\cdot)=f(x,\cdot)$ for almost every $x$. Then $f(\cdot,a)$ is measurable for every $a\in B$, and $x\mapsto f(x,u(x))$ is measurable for every measurable $u:\Omega\to B$. Measurability in $x$ and lower semicontinuity in $a$ alone do not guarantee the measurable-substitution property.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A normal integrand has almost-everywhere lower-semicontinuous fibers and an almost-everywhere equal jointly Borel representative. Its fixed-state sections and its substitutions along measurable mappings are measurable. Separate measurability in the parameter and lower semicontinuity in the state alone do not ensure measurable substitution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\text{ normal}\Longrightarrow \bigl(\forall a\in B,\ f(\cdot,a)\text{ measurable}\bigr)\land\bigl(\forall u:\Omega\to B\text{ measurable},\ x\mapsto f(x,u(x))\text{ measurable}\bigr)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Scorza–Dragoni Approximation for Carathéodory and Normal Integrands
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The exceptional parameter set consists of those first-variable values for which equality fails at at least one second-variable value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let X_1,X_2 be Polish spaces and \mu\in\mathcal P(X_1). If f:X_1\times X_2\to\mathbb R is a Carathéodory integrand, then for every \varepsilon>0 there exists a continuous function f_\varepsilon such that \mu\!\left(\left\{x_1\in X_1:\exists x_2\in X_2,\ f(x_1,x_2)\ne f_\varepsilon(x_1,x_2)\right\}\right)\le\varepsilon. If f:X_1\times X_2\to[0,+\infty] is instead a normal integrand, then f_\varepsilon may be chosen lower semicontinuous and pointwise bounded above by f, with the same exceptional-set bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For every positive tolerance, a Carathéodory integrand agrees for every state value with a continuous function outside a parameter set of measure at most that tolerance. A normal integrand likewise agrees there with a lower-semicontinuous function that is everywhere no larger than the original integrand.
assumptions_latex: f:X_1\times X_2\to\mathbb R\text{ is a Carathéodory integrand, or }f:X_1\times X_2\to[0,+\infty]\text{ is a normal integrand}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists f_\varepsilon:\ \mu\!\left(\left\{x_1\in X_1:\exists x_2\in X_2,\ f(x_1,x_2)\ne f_\varepsilon(x_1,x_2)\right\}\right)\le\varepsilon,\quad f_\varepsilon\text{ is continuous in the Carathéodory case, and l.s.c. with }f_\varepsilon\le f\text{ in the normal case}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Integral Lower-Limit Inequality under Almost-Everywhere Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lower semicontinuity of an integral generated by a nonnegative normal integrand along almost-everywhere convergent measurable mappings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\Omega\times\mathbb{R}^p\to[0,+\infty]\) be a normal integrand. Let \((u_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}\) be measurable mappings \(\Omega\to\mathbb{R}^p\) such that \(u_n(x)\to\bar u(x)\) for almost every \(x\). Then
\[
\int_\Omega f(x,\bar u(x))\,dx\leq\lim_{n\to\infty}\int_\Omega f(x,u_n(x))\,dx,
\]
whenever the displayed extended-real limit on the right exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonnegative normal integrand, almost-everywhere convergence of measurable mappings gives an integral lower-limit inequality, provided the stated limit of the integrals exists.
assumptions_latex: \lim_{n\to\infty}\int_\Omega f(x,u_n(x))\,dx\text{ exists in the extended reals}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \int_\Omega f(x,\bar u(x))\,dx\leq\lim_{n\to\infty}\int_\Omega f(x,u_n(x))\,dx

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniform Lusin characterization of normal integrands
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The extract's first occurrence of $K_\varepsilon$ is an evident symbol corruption and is read as a compact set $K$; the theorem remains subject to the chapter's ambient measure-topology assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $B\subset\mathbb R^p$ be Borel and let $f:\Omega\times B\to\overline{\mathbb R}$.
