knowledge_statements.statement_title: Banach and Hilbert Structure of Sobolev Spaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Completeness for all permitted exponents and Hilbert structure in the quadratic case.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n\) be open, \(k\in\mathbb N_0\), and \(p\in[1,\infty]\). Then \(W^{k,p}(\Omega)\) is a Banach space. Moreover, \(H^k(\Omega):=W^{k,2}(\Omega)\) is a Hilbert space with inner product \[\langle u,v\rangle_{H^k(\Omega)}:=\sum_{|\alpha|\le k}\langle D^\alpha u,D^\alpha v\rangle_{L^2(\Omega)}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every integer-order Sobolev space W^{k,p}(Ω), including the p equals infinity case, is complete. For p equal to two it is the Hilbert space H^k(Ω), whose inner product is the sum of the L² inner products of all weak derivatives through order k.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: W^{k,p}(\Omega)\text{ is Banach, and }H^k(\Omega)=W^{k,2}(\Omega)\text{ is Hilbert with }\langle u,v\rangle_{H^k}=\sum_{|\alpha|\le k}\langle D^\alpha u,D^\alpha v\rangle_{L^2}.

children.title: BV Integral Representation
children.top_down_role: Bulk, jump, and singular representation regimes on BV spaces.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional bulk, jump, and Cantor Radon–Nikodym decomposition without identifying the Cantor density as a recession function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(u\in BV(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)\), and let \(\mu_u\) be a positive Radon measure such that \[\mu_u\ll\lambda_u:=\mathcal L^n+\mathcal H^{n-1}\mathbin{\vrule height 1.4ex depth -0.3ex width 0.07ex\vrule height 0.07ex depth -0.02ex width 0.8ex}J_u+|D^cu|.\] The three measures in \(\lambda_u\) are mutually singular, so there are unique nonnegative densities \(f_u,g_u,h_u\), up to the corresponding null sets, such that for every Borel set \(A\subset\Omega\), \[\mu_u(A)=\int_A f_u\,dx+\int_{A\cap J_u}g_u\,d\mathcal H^{n-1}+\int_A h_u\,d|D^cu|.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A BV energy measure dominated by the bulk, jump, and Cantor reference measures has a unique three-part Radon–Nikodym decomposition.
assumptions_latex: \mu_u\ll\mathcal L^n+\mathcal H^{n-1}\mathbin{\vrule height 1.4ex depth -0.3ex width 0.07ex\vrule height 0.07ex depth -0.02ex width 0.8ex}J_u+|D^cu|
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mu_u=f_u\mathcal L^n+g_u(\mathcal H^{n-1}\mathbin{\vrule height 1.4ex depth -0.3ex width 0.07ex\vrule height 0.07ex depth -0.02ex width 0.8ex}J_u)+h_u|D^cu|\text{ uniquely up to null sets}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Measure Decomposition Does Not Identify the Cantor Density
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical separation between a three-measure decomposition and structural identification of its Cantor density.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the local measure-valued functional
\[
F(u,A):=|D^cu|(A),\qquad u\in BV(\Omega).
\]
For every affine \(u\), \(D^cu=0\), so the density detected from affine bulk states is \(f\equiv0\), with \(f^\infty\equiv0\). Nevertheless, \(F(u,A)>0\) whenever \(|D^cu|(A)>0\). Thus locality and a Radon–Nikodym decomposition alone do not force the Cantor density to equal the recession function of the bulk density.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A functional charging only the Cantor derivative has zero affine bulk density but a nonzero Cantor density, so measure decomposition alone cannot identify the latter as a bulk recession function.
assumptions_latex: No lower-semicontinuity or relaxation theorem is asserted for this example.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\equiv0,\qquad f^\infty\equiv0,\qquad F(u,A)=|D^cu|(A),

notation.meaning: Cantor part of the distributional derivative.

knowledge_statements.title: Measure Decomposition Does Not Identify the Cantor Density

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical derivative decomposition furnishing the three reference measures used in BV integral representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(u\in BV(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)\),
\[
Du=\nabla u\,\mathcal L^n+(u^+-u^-)\otimes\nu_u\,\mathcal H^{n-1}\mathbin{\vrule height 1.4ex depth -0.3ex width 0.07ex\vrule height 0.07ex depth -0.02ex width 0.8ex}J_u+D^cu.
\]
The absolutely continuous, jump, and Cantor measures in this decomposition are mutually singular.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every BV derivative splits uniquely into mutually singular absolutely continuous, jump, and Cantor parts.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Du=\nabla u\,\mathcal L^n+(u^+-u^-)\otimes\nu_u\,\mathcal H^{n-1}\mathbin{\vrule height 1.4ex depth -0.3ex width 0.07ex\vrule height 0.07ex depth -0.02ex width 0.8ex}J_u+D^cu.

knowledge_statements.title: Canonical BV Derivative Decomposition

assumptions_latex: \(u\in BV(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)\), with \(Du=\nabla u\,\mathcal L^n+D^j u+D^c u\).
\(F\) is local, lower semicontinuous, measure-valued in the open-set argument, and has linear growth.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[F(u,A)=\int_A f(x,u,\nabla u)\,dx+\int_{J_u\cap A}g(x,u^+,u^-,\nu_u)\,d\mathcal H^{n-1}+\int_A f^\infty\!\left(x,u,\frac{dD^c u}{d|D^c u|}\right)d|D^c u|.\]

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bulk, jump, and Cantor decomposition of local BV functionals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under the standard coercivity, locality, and continuity hypotheses ensuring BV integral representation, there are a bulk density \(f\), a surface density \(g\), and an appropriate recession density \(f^\infty\) such that, for every open \(A\subset\Omega\),
\[F(u,A)=\int_A f(x,u,\nabla u)\,dx+\int_{J_u\cap A}g(x,u^+,u^-,\nu_u)\,d\mathcal H^{n-1}+\int_A f^\infty\!\left(x,u,\frac{dD^c u}{d|D^c u|}\right)d|D^c u|.\]
The three terms respectively charge the absolutely continuous, jump, and Cantor regimes of \(Du\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A suitable local BV functional decomposes into bulk, jump-surface, and Cantor contributions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Here P(E_t) denotes the perimeter in D of the strict sublevel set E_t.

Let $D\subset\mathbb{R}^N$ be open and let $f\in BV(D)$. For each $t\in\mathbb{R}$ define $E_t=\{x\in D:f(x)<t\}$. Then

\]

children.title: Functional Locality
children.top_down_role: Dependence of a functional on local agreement of admissible states.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent factorization of a local functional through the almost-everywhere restriction class on each open set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each open \(A\subset\Omega\), write \(u\sim_Av\) when \(u=v\) almost everywhere on \(A\). A functional \(F:X\times\mathcal A(\Omega)\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is local exactly when, for every open \(A\), there is a map \(\Phi_A:X/{\sim_A}\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) satisfying \[F(u,A)=\Phi_A([u]_{\sim_A})\qquad(u\in X).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Functional locality is equivalent to factorization through the almost-everywhere restriction class on each localized open set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\text{ is local}\iff \forall A\ \exists\Phi_A\text{ with }F(u,A)=\Phi_A([u]_{\sim_A}).

notation.meaning: Almost-everywhere agreement on the open set A.
Factor map on local restriction classes.

knowledge_statements.title: Restriction-Class Factorization of Functional Locality

assumptions_latex: \(F:X\times\mathcal A(\Omega)\to(-\infty,\infty]\), where elements of \(X\) are measurable maps on \(\Omega\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[u=v\ \text{a.e. on }A\quad\Longrightarrow\quad F(u,A)=F(v,A).\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Locality with respect to almost-everywhere agreement on the localized set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The functional \(F\) is local if, for every \(A\in\mathcal A(\Omega)\) and every \(u,v\in X\), agreement \(u=v\) almost everywhere on \(A\) implies
\[F(u,A)=F(v,A).\]
Thus the value assigned to \(A\) depends only on the equivalence class of the restriction of the function to \(A\), not on values outside \(A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A localized functional is local when its value on a set depends only on the function inside that set.

children.title: Measure Representation Properties
children.top_down_role: Measure-theoretic structure of localized functional values.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absolute-continuity threshold for representing the localized measure by a Lebesgue density.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(u,A)=\mu_u(A)\) for open \(A\subset\Omega\), where \(\mu_u\) is a finite Radon measure. Then \[\mu_u\ll\mathcal L^n\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \exists g_u\in L^1(\Omega):\ F(u,A)=\int_A g_u\,dx\quad\forall A\in\mathcal A(\Omega).\] The density \(g_u=d\mu_u/d\mathcal L^n\) is unique almost everywhere and, for almost every \(x\in\Omega\), \[g_u(x)=\lim_{r\downarrow0,\,B_r(x)\subset\Omega}\frac{F(u,B_r(x))}{|B_r(x)|}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A measure-valued localization has a Lebesgue density exactly when its representing measure is absolutely continuous, and that density is recovered almost everywhere by measure differentiation.
assumptions_latex: \(\mu_u\) is a finite Radon measure representing \(A\mapsto F(u,A)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mu_u\ll\mathcal L^n\) is equivalent to representation by the unique density \(d\mu_u/d\mathcal L^n\), recoverable by ball ratios almost everywhere.

notation.meaning: Radon–Nikodym density of the representing measure.

knowledge_statements.title: Radon–Nikodym Density Criterion

assumptions_latex: For each fixed \(u\in X\), the set function \(A\mapsto F(u,A)\) is the restriction of a finite Radon measure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For each \(u\), there is a unique finite Radon measure \(\mu_u\) satisfying \(F(u,A)=\mu_u(A)\) for every open \(A\subset\Omega\).

notation.meaning: Representing Radon measure associated with the function.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Radon-measure structure of the localized set function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every fixed \(u\in X\), measure representation means that there is a finite Radon measure \(\mu_u\) on \(\Omega\) such that
\[F(u,A)=\mu_u(A)\qquad\text{for every open }A\subset\Omega.\]
Consequently the localized functional is monotone in \(A\), countably additive on disjoint Borel sets after extension, inner regular on open sets, and outer regular on Borel sets. The representing measure is unique because open sets determine a Radon measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For each function, the localized energy extends uniquely to a Radon measure and inherits its additivity and regularity properties.
knowledge_statements.title: Measure Representation Properties

children.title: Localization Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Compatibility between locality, restriction, and measure representation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Agreement Gives Consistent Measure Restrictions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility between functional locality and restriction of localized energy measures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(F\) is local and, for every \(u\in X\), \(F(u,\cdot)\) is the restriction to open sets of a Radon measure \(\mu_u\). If \(u=v\) almost everywhere on an open set \(A\subset\Omega\), then for every open \(B\subset A\), \[\mu_u(B)=F(u,B)=F(v,B)=\mu_v(B).\] Consequently \(\mu_u\mathbin{\vrule height 1.4ex depth -0.3ex width 0.07ex\vrule height 0.07ex depth -0.02ex width 0.8ex}A=\mu_v\mathbin{\vrule height 1.4ex depth -0.3ex width 0.07ex\vrule height 0.07ex depth -0.02ex width 0.8ex}A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: States agreeing locally induce identical restrictions of their representing energy measures on that region.
assumptions_latex: u=v\text{ a.e. on the open set }A
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mu_u\mathbin{\vrule height 1.4ex depth -0.3ex width 0.07ex\vrule height 0.07ex depth -0.02ex width 0.8ex}A=\mu_v\mathbin{\vrule height 1.4ex depth -0.3ex width 0.07ex\vrule height 0.07ex depth -0.02ex width 0.8ex}A.

notation.meaning: Radon measure representing the localized values of F at u.

knowledge_statements.title: Local Agreement Gives Consistent Measure Restrictions

assumptions_latex: \(F(u,\cdot)=\mu_u\) is represented by a Radon measure on \(\Omega\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[F(u,A)=\sup_{U\Subset A}F(u,U),\qquad F(u,A\cup B)=F(u,A)+F(u,B)\ \text{if }A\cap B=\varnothing.\]

notation.meaning: Compact containment of one open set in another.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility of restriction, exhaustion, and disjoint localization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(F(u,\cdot)=\mu_u\) for a Radon measure \(\mu_u\), then restriction to an open subset is compatible with further localization: for open \(B\subset A\subset\Omega\), the restriction of \(F(u,\cdot)\) from \(A\) to \(B\) equals \(F(u,B)\). Moreover,
\[F(u,A)=\sup_{U\Subset A}F(u,U),\]
and for disjoint open sets \(A,B\subset\Omega\),
\[F(u,A\cup B)=F(u,A)+F(u,B).\]
These identities permit densities to be recovered from arbitrarily small neighborhoods.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Measure-valued localization commutes with restriction, compact exhaustion, and addition over disjoint open sets.
knowledge_statements.title: Localization Compatibility

children.title: Nonlocality Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Obstructions to local integral representation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of the measure property despite dependence only on values inside the localized set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For scalar \(u\in L^1(\Omega)\), define \[H(u,A)=\left|\int_Au(x)\,dx\right|^2.\] For disjoint open \(A,B\subset\Omega\), \[H(u,A\cup B)=H(u,A)+H(u,B)+2\left(\int_Au\right)\left(\int_Bu\right),\] so whenever the cross term is nonzero, \(A\mapsto H(u,A)\) is not finitely additive. It therefore cannot be a representing measure or equal \(\int_A h(x,j^ku(x))\,dx\) for every open \(A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Squaring an integral creates cross terms between disjoint regions, preventing measure representation even though the functional uses only values inside the localized set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The localization \(A\mapsto H(u,A)\) is generally nonadditive and has no measure or local-density representation.

notation.meaning: Squared integral of the field over the localized set.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonadditive Localization Obstruction
Nonlocality Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pairwise interactions across the boundary of a localized open set obstruct local jet-based representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n\) be bounded and open, let \(A\subset\Omega\) be open, and let \(K\in L^\infty(\Omega\times\Omega;[0,\infty))\) be positive on a subset of \(A\times(\Omega\setminus A)\) having positive product measure. For \(u\in L^\infty(\Omega)\), define \[G(u,A)=\int_A\int_\Omega K(x,y)|u(x)-u(y)|^2\,dy\,dx.\] Then there exist \(u,v\in L^\infty(\Omega)\) such that \(u=v\) almost everywhere on \(A\) but \(G(u,A)\ne G(v,A)\). Thus \(G\) is not local and cannot, for every open localization, be represented by a density depending only on a pointwise local jet.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pairwise interaction that couples an open set to its complement can distinguish functions that agree inside the set, so it is nonlocal and has no purely local jet representation on every localization.
assumptions_latex: \(\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n\) is bounded and open, and \(A\subset\Omega\) is open.
\(K\in L^\infty(\Omega\times\Omega;[0,\infty))\) is positive on a subset of \(A\times(\Omega\setminus A)\) of positive product measure.
\(G\) is defined on \(L^\infty(\Omega)\times\mathcal A(\Omega)\) by the displayed interaction integral.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\exists u,v\in L^\infty(\Omega):\ u=v\ \text{a.e. on }A\ \text{and}\ G(u,A)\ne G(v,A).\]

notation.meaning: The pairwise interaction energy localized in its first integration variable to A.
A nonnegative interaction kernel coupling points x and y.

children.title: Blow-Up Localization
children.top_down_role: Rescaling families used to localize variational functionals.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Common rescaling architecture for volume and codimension-one measure components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the dilation \(T_{x_0,r}(y)=x_0+ry\), Lebesgue measure satisfies \(\mathcal L^d(T_{x_0,r}(A))=r^d\mathcal L^d(A)\), while \((d-1)\)-dimensional Hausdorff measure on a rectifiable interface scales by \(r^{d-1}\). Consequently, volume-density blow-ups use \(r^{-d}\) normalization and surface-density blow-ups use \(r^{-(d-1)}\) normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The normalization in a blow-up is determined by the dimension of the reference measure whose density is being recovered.
assumptions_latex: The localized component is absolutely continuous with respect to \(\mathcal L^d\) or to \(\mathcal H^{d-1}\) on a rectifiable interface.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: r^{-d}\text{ is the volume normalization, whereas }r^{-(d-1)}\text{ is the codimension-one normalization.}

knowledge_statements.title: Dimension-Dependent Blow-Up Normalization
Blow-Up Localization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovery of the absolutely continuous density of a localized energy measure by shrinking-ball normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(u,A)=\mu_u(A)\) for open \(A\subset\Omega\), where \(\mu_u\) is a finite Radon measure with Lebesgue decomposition \(\mu_u=h_u\mathcal L^n+\mu_u^s\). Then, for \(\mathcal L^n\)-almost every \(x_0\in\Omega\), \[h_u(x_0)=\frac{d\mu_u}{d\mathcal L^n}(x_0)=\lim_{r\downarrow0}\frac{F(u,B_r(x_0))}{|B_r(x_0)|}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At almost every point, normalized energy on shrinking balls recovers the absolutely continuous density of the localized energy measure.
assumptions_latex: \(\mu_u\) is a finite Radon measure with \(\mu_u=h_u\mathcal L^n+\mu_u^s\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[h_u(x_0)=\frac{d\mu_u}{d\mathcal L^n}(x_0)=\lim_{r\downarrow0}\frac{F(u,B_r(x_0))}{|B_r(x_0)|}\quad\text{for }\mathcal L^n\text{-a.e. }x_0\in\Omega.\]

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Almost-Everywhere Uniqueness of the Represented Bulk Density
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniqueness along a fixed Sobolev field from equality of all localized bulk energies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(u\in W^{1,1}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)\). If \(h_1,h_2\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)\) satisfy \[\int_A h_1(x)\,dx=\int_A h_2(x)\,dx\] for every relatively compact open set \(A\subset\Omega\), then \(h_1=h_2\) \(\mathcal L^n\)-almost everywhere. Thus a represented bulk density evaluated along \((u,\nabla u)\) is determined almost everywhere by the localized functional.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Localized energies determine the represented bulk density along a fixed Sobolev field uniquely up to a null set.
assumptions_latex: \(\int_A h_1\,dx=\int_A h_2\,dx\) for every relatively compact open \(A\subset\Omega\).

knowledge_statements.title: Almost-Everywhere Uniqueness of the Represented Bulk Density
Bulk-Density Identification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise recovery of a represented bulk density from normalized local energies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \(F(u,A)=\int_A f(x,u(x),

children.title: Recession-Density Identification
children.top_down_role: Localization of densities associated with singular growth.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence and structural properties of the recession function for a finite convex integrand.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(z\mapsto f(x,z)\) is finite and convex, then for every \(z_0,z\) the quotient \[t\mapsto\frac{f(x,z_0+tz)-f(x,z_0)}{t}\] is nondecreasing on \((0,\infty)\). Its limit as \(t\to\infty\) is independent of \(z_0\) and defines \(f^\infty(x,z)\). The function \(f^\infty(x,\cdot)\) is convex and positively one-homogeneous; an upper linear-growth bound makes it finite-valued.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convexity makes the recession limit base-point independent, convex, and positively homogeneous.
assumptions_latex: An upper linear-growth bound is assumed when finiteness of \(f^\infty\) is asserted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f^\infty(x,\lambda z)=\lambda f^\infty(x,z)\quad(\lambda\ge0),\qquad f^\infty(x,\cdot)\text{ is convex}.

notation.meaning: Arbitrary finite base point in the recession quotient.

knowledge_statements.title: Convex Recession Function Properties

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Measure-theoretic localization of an already represented singular energy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(\mu_u^s=f^\infty(x,\theta_u(x))\,|D^su|\), where \(\theta_u=dD^su/d|D^su|\). Then for \(|D^su|\)-almost every \(x_0\), \[f^\infty(x_0,\theta_u(x_0))=\frac{d\mu_u^s}{d|D^su|}(x_0)=\lim_{r\downarrow0}\frac{\mu_u^s(B_r(x_0))}{|D^su|(B_r(x_0))}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The represented recession density is recovered by differentiating singular energy with respect to the total variation of the singular derivative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f^\infty(x_0,\theta_u(x_0))=\lim_{r\downarrow0}\frac{\mu_u^s(B_r(x_0))}{|D^su|(B_r(x_0))}\quad\text{for }|D^su|\text{-a.e. }x_0.

Polar density of the singular derivative.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Linear Growth Does Not Ensure a Recession Limit
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of the ordinary recession quotient for a continuous nonconvex integrand with linear growth.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(f:\mathbb R\to[0,\infty)\) by \[f(z)=|z|\bigl(2+\sin(\log(1+|z|))\bigr).\] Then \(|z|\le f(z)\le3|z|\), but for \(z=1\), \[\frac{f(tz)-f(0)}{t}=2+\sin(\log(1+t))\] has no limit as \(t\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Continuity and linear growth alone do not ensure existence of the ordinary recession limit for a nonconvex integrand.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lim_{t\to\infty}\frac{f(t)-f(0)}{t}\text{ does not exist}.
knowledge_statements.title: Linear Growth Does Not Ensure a Recession Limit

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonconvex upper-recession object used when the ordinary recession limit need not exist.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For fixed \(x\), define
\[
f^{\#}(x,z):=\limsup_{\substack{t\to+\infty\\z'\to z}}\frac{f(x,tz')}{t}.
\]
A uniform upper linear-growth bound makes \(f^{\#}(x,\cdot)\) finite. If the ordinary recession quotient converges locally uniformly with respect to directions near \(z\), then \(f^{\#}(x,z)=f^\infty(x,z)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A joint limsup in scale and direction defines an upper recession function even when a nonconvex integrand has no ordinary recession limit.
assumptions_latex: A uniform upper linear-growth bound is assumed when finiteness is asserted.
Equality with \(f^\infty\) requires stability of the ordinary recession limit under directional perturbations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f^{\#}(x,z)=\limsup_{\substack{t\to+\infty\\z'\to z}}\frac{f(x,tz')}{t}.

notation.meaning: Directional perturbation in the joint limsup.

knowledge_statements.title: Generalized Upper Recession Function

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Autonomous convex linear-growth relaxation identifying the singular density by the ordinary recession function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d\) be bounded and open and let \(f:\mathbb R^{m\times d}\to[0,+\infty)\) be finite and convex, with \(c|z|\le f(z)\le C(1+|z|)\). If \(I(v)=\int_\Omega f(\nabla v)\,dx\) on \(W^{1,1}(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)\), then its sequential strong-\(L^1\) lower-semicontinuous envelope on \(BV(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)\) is
\[
\overline I(u)=\int_\Omega f(\nabla u)\,dx+\int_\Omega f^\infty\!\left(\frac{dD^su}{d|D^su|}\right)d|D^su|,
\qquad f^\infty(z)=\lim_{t\to\infty}\frac{f(tz)}t.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an autonomous convex integrand with linear growth, relaxation from W1,1 to BV evaluates the ordinary recession function on the polar of the singular derivative.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is finite and convex and satisfies \(c|z|\le f(z)\le C(1+|z|)\).
The envelope is taken for sequential strong \(L^1\) convergence from \(W^{1,1}\) to \(BV\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \overline I(u)=\int_\Omega f(\nabla u)\,dx+\int_\Omega f^\infty\!\left(\frac{dD^su}{d|D^su|}\right)d|D^su|.

notation.meaning: Part of Du singular with respect to Lebesgue measure.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Conjugate-Domain Representation of the Convex Recession Function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual representation of a closed proper convex integrand's recession density.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix \(x\) and let \(g(z)=f(x,z)\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex. Then
\[
g^\infty(z)=\sigma_{\operatorname{dom}g^*}(z)=\sup_{p\in\operatorname{dom}g^*}\langle p,z\rangle.
\]
An upper bound \(g(z)\le C(1+|z|)\) gives \(\operatorname{dom}g^*\subset C\mathbb B\), while \(g(z)\ge c|z|-C\) gives \(c\mathbb B\subset\operatorname{dom}g^*\) and hence \(g^\infty(z)\ge c|z|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed convex recession density is the support function of the effective domain of the convex conjugate.
assumptions_latex: \(g=f(x,\cdot)\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
The displayed growth assumptions are imposed only for their corresponding domain conclusions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: g^\infty=\sigma_{\operatorname{dom}g^*}.

notation.meaning: Convex conjugate of the fixed-x integrand.
Support function of the set C.

assumptions_latex: \(\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d\) is open and \(f:\Omega\times\mathbb R^{m\times d}\to[0,\infty)\) is convex in its second argument.
\(f\) has linear growth and sufficient continuity in \(x\) for the standard \(BV\)-relaxation formula.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The singular derivative contributes \(f^\infty(x,dD^su/d|D^su|)\) per unit \(|D^su|\).

notation.meaning: Recession function of the integrand in its gradient variable.
Part of the distributional derivative singular with respect to Lebesgue measure.
Polar density of the singular derivative with respect to its total variation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex linear-growth relaxation on \(BV\), with the recession function identifying singular energy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(x\in\Omega\) and \(z\in\mathbb R^{m\times d}\), define
\[
f^\infty(x,z):=\lim_{t\to\infty}\frac{f(x,tz)-f(x,0)}{t},
\]
whenever the stated hypotheses guarantee this limit. If \(u\in BV(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)\) and \(Du=\nabla u\,\mathcal L^d+D^su\), then the relaxed functional has singular part
\[
\int_\Omega f^\infty\!\left(x,\frac{dD^su}{d|D^su|}(x)\right)d|D^su|(x).
\]
Thus blow-up along amplitudes diverging at rate \(t\) identifies the density carried by the singular derivative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The recession function, evaluated at the polar of the singular derivative, gives the relaxed energy density on the singular part.
knowledge_statements.title: Recession-Density Identification

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation role and recession-density formula are standard, but “sufficient continuity” does not state the hypotheses needed for the claimed BV relaxation formula. A specific source is required.

children.title: Direct-Method Compactness
children.top_down_role: Compactness architecture for minimizing sequences and admissible limits.

children.top_down_role: Growth and normalization structures preventing escape of minimizing sequences.

children.title: Superlinear-Growth Regimes
children.top_down_role: Growth regimes supporting reflexive-space bounds.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Endpoint separating the reflexive superlinear route from linear-growth compactness mechanisms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(1<p<\infty\), \(L^p(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)\) and \(W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)\) are reflexive, and their bounded sequences are weakly relatively compact. At \(p=1\), these spaces are generally nonreflexive, so boundedness alone does not provide weak sequential compactness; uniform-integrability, BV, or measure compactness hypotheses are then needed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The reflexive compactness route applies above linear growth and generally fails at the exponent one endpoint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(1<p<\infty\) gives reflexive weak compactness, whereas \(p=1\) does not in general.
knowledge_statements.title: Reflexivity Threshold for Power Growth

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every finite-energy sublevel of \(F\) is bounded in \(W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)\), hence weakly relatively compact.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: p-growth coercivity and reflexivity are standard direct-method facts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A coercive \(p\)-growth regime with \(p>1\), yielding reflexive Sobolev compactness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \(c\in\mathbb R\) and every \(u\) satisfying \(F(u)\leq c\), coercive growth gives
\[
\alpha\bigl(\|u\|_{L^p}^p+\|\nabla u\|_{L^p}^p\bigr)\leq c+\|\beta\|_{L^1}.
\]
Hence the sublevel \(\{u:F(u)\leq c\}\) is bounded in \(W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)\). Since \(1<p<\infty\), this Sobolev space is reflexive, so each sequence in the sublevel has a weakly convergent subsequence. The same conclusion holds when the \(L^p\)-term is replaced by a normalization and an applicable Poincare inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coercive growth of order greater than one bounds Sobolev sublevels and supplies weakly convergent subsequences through reflexivity.
knowledge_statements.title: Superlinear-Growth Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property correctly describes the superlinear coercive regime and reflexive compactness, but no inspectable source locator is supplied.

children.title: Linear-Growth Regimes
children.top_down_role: Growth regimes requiring BV or measure compactness.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-dimensional derivative concentration explaining the need for BV or measure compactness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \((0,1)\), define \[u_j(x)=\min\{jx,1\}.\] Then \((u_j)\) is bounded in \(W^{1,1}(0,1)\), since \(u_j'=j\mathbf1_{(0,1/j)}\) and \(\|u_j'\|_{L^1}=1\). The derivatives are not uniformly integrable and hence are not weakly relatively compact in \(L^1(0,1)\). Viewed as measures on \([0,1]\), \[u_j'\,\mathcal L^1\stackrel{*}{\rightharpoonup}\delta_0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bounded amount of gradient mass can concentrate into a measure, preventing weak L1 compactness despite bounded total variation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The sequence is bounded in W^{1,1}, but its gradients are not weakly relatively compact in L^1.
knowledge_statements.title: Concentration Obstructs Weak W11 Compactness

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Normalization Converts Linear Derivative Growth into BV Coercivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Energy-to-BV boundedness after additive constants are controlled.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(F(u)\ge \alpha |Du|(\Omega)-C\), where \(\alpha>0\), and the admissible class has prescribed mean, an appropriate prescribed trace, or an independent coercive \(L^1\) term. Then every finite sublevel of \(F\) is bounded in \(BV(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)\). Without such normalization, derivative growth alone does not control additions of constants.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linear derivative growth yields BV-bounded sublevels after constants are fixed or separately controlled.
assumptions_latex: A BV Poincare normalization holds, or the energy separately controls \(\|u\|_{L^1}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F(u)\le c\Rightarrow \|u\|_{L^1}+|Du|(\Omega)\le C_c.
knowledge_statements.title: Normalization Converts Linear Derivative Growth into BV Coercivity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: BV Compactness in the Linear-Growth Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compactness under uniform mass and total-variation bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d\) be bounded with Lipschitz boundary. If \((u_j)\subset BV(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)\) satisfies
\[
\sup_j\bigl(\|u_j\|_{L^1(\Omega)}+|Du_j|(\Omega)\bigr)<\infty,
\]
then a subsequence and \(u\in BV(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)\) satisfy \(u_j\to u\) in \(L^1\) and \(Du_j\stackrel{*}{\rightharpoonup}Du\) as vector-valued Radon measures.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform mass and total variation give strong L1 compactness and weak-star compactness of derivative measures.
assumptions_latex: The sequence has uniformly bounded \(L^1\) norm and total variation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: u_j\to u\text{ in }L^1,\qquad Du_j\stackrel{*}{\rightharpoonup}Du\text{ along a subsequence}.

notation.meaning: Total variation of the distributional derivative

knowledge_statements.title: BV Compactness in the Linear-Growth Regime

assumptions_latex: \(\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d\) is bounded and has Lipschitz boundary.
\(F\) is defined on \(W^{1,1}(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)\) and satisfies \(F(u)\geq\alpha(\|u\|_{L^1}+\|\nabla u\|_{L^1})-C\), with \(\alpha>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Energy-bounded sequences are bounded in \(BV\), relatively compact in \(L^1\), and have weak-star convergent derivative measures along a subsequence.

notation.meaning: Distributional derivative, regarded as a vector-valued Radon measure.
Total variation of the derivative measure on the domain.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: linear growth naturally yields BV rather than reflexive Sobolev compactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear growth provides \(BV\) and measure compactness, generally not weak compactness in \(W^{1,1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(F(u_j)\leq c\), then
\[
\sup_j\bigl(\|u_j\|_{L^1(\Omega)}+|Du_j|(\Omega)\bigr)<\infty,
\]
where \(Du_j=\nabla u_j\,\mathcal L^d\) for \(u_j\in W^{1,1}\). Consequently there exist \(u\in BV(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)\) and a subsequence such that \(u_j\to u\) in \(L^1(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)\) and \(Du_j\stackrel{*}{\rightharpoonup}Du\) as Radon measures. Thus a direct method for linear growth normally uses the relaxed \(BV\) domain, because bounded subsets of \(W^{1,1}\) need not be weakly relatively compact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linear energy growth bounds total variation, so compactness occurs in BV and in derivative measures rather than through reflexivity of W1,1.
knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Growth Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property fits the linear-growth leaf and correctly distinguishes BV compactness from W^{1,1} reflexivity, but it lacks a source locator.

children.title: Coercivity Modulo Invariances
children.top_down_role: Compactness after normalization by translations, constants, or other null directions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Functional inequality certifying coercivity after removal of null directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(N\subset X\) be the invariant null space and suppose \[\operatorname{dist}(x,N)\le C(1+E(x)),\qquad F(x)\ge aE(x)-b,\quad a>0.\] Then every finite sublevel of \(F\) has bounded image in \(X/N\); equivalently, \(F\) is coercive modulo \(N\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Poincare-type estimate controlling distance to the null space by an energy dominated by the objective certifies quotient coercivity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\text{ is coercive modulo }N.

notation.meaning: energy controlling displacement transverse to the invariant directions

knowledge_statements.title: Poincare-Type Quotient Coercivity Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of ambient coercivity despite quotient control.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(H^1(0,1)\), let \[F(u)=\int_0^1|u'(x)|^2\,dx.\] Then \(F(u+c)=F(u)\), and \(u_j\equiv j\) satisfies \(F(u_j)=0\) while \(\|u_j\|_{H^1}\to\infty\). Thus ambient sublevels are unbounded. After imposing \(\int_0^1u=0\), Poincare's inequality bounds the normalized representatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Derivative energy cannot control additive constants; mean normalization removes the escaping null direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\text{ is not ambiently coercive but is coercive modulo constants}.
knowledge_statements.title: Unnormalized Escape Along Null Directions

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounded normalized representatives for invariant functionals on a complemented quotient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=N\oplus Z\) with bounded projection \(P_N:X\to N\), and suppose \(F(x+n)=F(x)\) for every \(n\in N\). If \(F\) is coercive modulo \(N\), then every energy-bounded sequence \((x_j)\) has normalized representatives \[z_j=x_j-P_Nx_j\in Z,\qquad F(z_j)=F(x_j),\] bounded in \(X\). Conversely, boundedness in \(Z\) of every normalized finite sublevel implies coercivity modulo \(N\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the null space is complemented, subtracting its component converts quotient coercivity into boundedness of normalized representatives.
assumptions_latex: \(N\) is a closed complemented subspace of \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Quotient coercivity is equivalent to boundedness of normalized sublevels in the fixed complement.

notation.meaning: bounded projection onto the invariant subspace

knowledge_statements.title: Complemented-Kernel Normalization Principle

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a normed space and \(N\subset X\) is a closed subspace representing null directions.
\(F:X\to(-\infty,\infty]\) is invariant under \(N\): \(F(x+n)=F(x)\) for all \(n\in N\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Coercivity modulo \(N\) is ordinary coercivity of the induced functional on \(X/N\), equivalently boundedness of quotient sublevels.

notation.meaning: Distance from an element to the invariant subspace.
Quotient map from X to the space of equivalence classes modulo N.
Functional induced by F on the quotient.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: quotient coercivity is the canonical formulation of coercivity modulo null directions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coercivity after quotienting additive null directions such as constants, translations, or finite-dimensional kernels.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The functional \(F\) is coercive modulo \(N\) when
\[
\operatorname{dist}(x,N)\to\infty\quad\Longrightarrow\quad F(x)\to\infty.
\]
Invariance makes \(\bar F(\pi x):=F(x)\) well defined on \(X/N\), whose norm is \(\|\pi x\|_{X/N}=\operatorname{dist}(x,N)\). Hence coercivity modulo \(N\) is precisely coercivity of \(\bar F\). Equivalently, for every \(c\in\mathbb R\), the quotient sublevel \(\pi(\{x:F(x)\leq c\})\) is bounded. If bounded representatives can be selected, normalized minimizing sequences are bounded in \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A functional is coercive modulo its null directions when its sublevels become bounded after passage to the corresponding quotient space.
knowledge_statements.title: Coercivity Modulo Invariances

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition correctly formulates coercivity modulo an invariant closed subspace through the quotient norm, but no source is cited.

children.title: Sublevel-Set Boundedness
children.top_down_role: Boundedness properties of functional sublevel families in relevant topologies.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a normed space and \(F:X\to(-\infty,\infty]\) is an extended-real functional.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Level-boundedness means \(\{x\in X:F(x)\leq c\}\) is bounded for every finite \(c\).

notation.meaning: Sublevel set of F at height c.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundedness of all finite sublevels in the ambient norm.

source_refs.locator: 9.1.5 Boundedness of level sets p. 826
source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(c\in\mathbb R\), define the finite sublevel set
\[
L_c(F):=\{x\in X:F(x)\leq c\}.
\]
The functional \(F\) is level-bounded if \(L_c(F)\) is bounded in \(X\) for every \(c\in\mathbb R\). Equivalently, for each \(c\) there exists \(R_c<\infty\) such that \(F(x)\leq c\) implies \(\|x\|\leq R_c\). Empty sublevels are bounded by convention. This definition concerns boundedness only and does not itself require lower semicontinuity, compactness, or attainment of the infimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A functional is level-bounded when every sublevel below a finite height is bounded in the ambient norm.
knowledge_statements.title: Sublevel-Set Boundedness

source_witnesses.locator: 9.1.5 Boundedness of level sets p. 826
source_witnesses.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Immediate boundedness consequence of level-boundedness before any topology-specific compactness argument.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be level-bounded on a normed space and let \(m:=\inf_XF\in\mathbb R\). Every sequence \((x_k)\) satisfying \(F(x_k)\to m\) is norm bounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every minimizing sequence of a level-bounded functional with finite infimum is norm bounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_k\|x_k\|<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.title: Boundedness of Minimizing Sequences

children.title: Coercivity–Level-Boundedness Equivalence Regimes
children.top_down_role: Settings where coercivity and level boundedness coincide or diverge.

knowledge_statements.title: Coercivity–Level-Boundedness Equivalence Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential coercivity versus level-boundedness on an arbitrary normed space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The following conditions are equivalent:
\[
\|x_j\|\to\infty\quad\Longrightarrow\quad F(x_j)\to\infty
\]
for every sequence \((x_j)\subset X\), and
\[
L_c(F):=\{x\in X:F(x)\leq c\}\text{ is bounded for every }c\in\mathbb R.
\]
Equivalently, the first condition may be written as \(\lim_{\|x\|\to\infty}F(x)=\infty\). No finite-dimensionality or lower semicontinuity is required for this equivalence. Compactness of sublevels, however, requires additional topological hypotheses, such as finite dimensionality together with closedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A functional diverges along every norm-divergent sequence exactly when each of its finite sublevel sets is bounded.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a normed space and \(F:X\to(-\infty,\infty]\) is an extended-real functional.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The sequential coercivity condition \(\|x_j\|\to\infty\Rightarrow F(x_j)\to\infty\) is equivalent to boundedness of every finite sublevel.

notation.meaning: Sublevel set of F at height c.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bounded Sublevels Need Not Be Norm Compact
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Infinite-dimensional boundary of the coercivity-to-compactness implication.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be an infinite-dimensional Banach space and define \[F(x)=\begin{cases}0,&\|x\|\le1,\\+\infty,&\|x\|>1.\end{cases}\] Every finite nonempty sublevel is the closed unit ball, so \(F\) is coercive in the extended-real sequential sense and norm lower semicontinuous. Nevertheless, its finite sublevel is not norm compact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The indicator of the closed unit ball is coercive and lower semicontinuous but lacks norm-compact sublevels in infinite dimensions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Coercivity plus norm lower semicontinuity does not imply norm-compact sublevels.
knowledge_statements.title: Bounded Sublevels Need Not Be Norm Compact

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Topological upgrades of the accepted coercivity-level-boundedness equivalence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be coercive. If \(X\) is finite-dimensional and \(F\) is lower semicontinuous, every finite sublevel is norm compact. If \(X\) is reflexive and \(F\) is weakly lower semicontinuous, every finite sublevel is weakly compact. In either regime, a proper \(F\) with finite infimum attains its infimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coercivity gives bounded sublevels; suitable lower semicontinuity and ambient compactness upgrade them to compact sublevels and existence.
assumptions_latex: Either \(X\) is finite-dimensional and \(F\) is lower semicontinuous, or \(X\) is reflexive and \(F\) is weakly lower semicontinuous.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Finite sublevels are compact in the corresponding topology, and a proper finite-infimum functional attains its minimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Compact-Sublevel Regimes Beyond Boundedness

children.title: Reflexive Weak Compactness
children.top_down_role: Compactness in reflexive Sobolev and Lebesgue spaces.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundedness alone need not imply weak subsequential compactness outside reflexive spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In \(\ell^1\), the unit vectors \(e_n\) satisfy \(\|e_n\|_1=1\) but have no weakly convergent subsequence. Thus boundedness alone cannot replace reflexivity or a separate weak-compactness criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The bounded unit-vector sequence in l1 has no weakly convergent subsequence, showing the necessity of an additional compactness hypothesis.
assumptions_latex: \((e_n)\) is the canonical unit-vector sequence in \(\ell^1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((e_n)\) is norm bounded but not relatively weakly sequentially compact in \(\ell^1\).

notation.meaning: The nth canonical unit vector in l1.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonreflexive Boundedness Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical characterizations of the reflexive compactness mechanism.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a Banach space \(X\), the following are equivalent: \(X\) is reflexive; its closed unit ball \(B_X\) is weakly compact; every bounded sequence in \(X\) has a weakly convergent subsequence. The sequential equivalence uses the Eberlein–Šmulian theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Banach space is reflexive exactly when its unit ball is weakly compact, equivalently when every bounded sequence has a weakly convergent subsequence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: X\text{ reflexive}\iff B_X\text{ weakly compact}\iff\text{every bounded sequence has a weakly convergent subsequence}.
knowledge_statements.title: Reflexivity–Weak Compactness Equivalences

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There are a subsequence \((x_{j_k})\) and \(x\in X\) such that \(x_{j_k}\rightharpoonup x\).

notation.meaning: Weak convergence in the Banach space X.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: bounded-sequence weak compactness in reflexive Banach spaces is classical
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential weak compactness of bounded sets in reflexive Banach spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Every bounded sequence \((x_j)\) in a reflexive Banach space \(X\) possesses a subsequence \((x_{j_k})\) and an element \(x\in X\) such that
\[
x_{j_k}\rightharpoonup x,
\qquad
\ell(x_{j_k})\to\ell(x)\quad\text{for every }\ell\in X^*.
\]
In particular, bounded sublevels of a functional on \(L^p\) or \(W^{1,p}\), with \(1<p<\infty\), are weakly relatively sequentially compact. If the sublevel is also weakly closed, then it is weakly sequentially compact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every bounded sequence in a reflexive Banach space has a weakly convergent subsequence; weakly closed bounded sublevels are therefore weakly compact.
knowledge_statements.title: Reflexive Weak Compactness

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Canonical isometric embedding into the bidual
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the canonical evaluation map and records its norm-preserving property.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a normed space \(X\), define \(J:X\to X^{**}\) by \(\langle Jx,\zeta\rangle=\langle\zeta,x\rangle\) for every \(x\in X\) and \(\zeta\in X^*\). Then \(J\) is linear and \(\|Jx\|_{X^{**}}=\|x\|_X\) for every \(x\in X\); hence \(J\) is a continuous isometry of \(X\) onto the subspace \(J(X)\subseteq X^{**}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every normed space has a canonical linear evaluation map into its bidual. This map preserves norms and identifies the space isometrically with its image in the bidual.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: J:X\to X^{**},\quad (Jx)(\zeta)=\zeta(x),\qquad \|Jx\|_{X^{**}}=\|x\|_X

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Weak Convergence in a Banach Space
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential weak convergence defined through all continuous linear functionals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U\) be a real Banach space. A sequence \((u_n)_{n=1}^{\infty}\subset U\) converges weakly to \(u\in U\), written \(u_n\rightharpoonup u\), if \(\lim_{n\to\infty}f(u_n)=f(u)\) for every \(f\in U^*\). The weak limit, when it exists, is unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sequence in a real Banach space converges weakly to u when every continuous linear functional converges on the sequence to its value at u. The weak limit is unique.
assumptions_latex: U\text{ is a real Banach space}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: u_n\rightharpoonup u\iff \forall f\in U^*:\ \lim_{n\to\infty}f(u_n)=f(u),\qquad \text{and the weak limit is unique}.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition through surjectivity of the canonical embedding into the bidual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A Banach space \(X\) is reflexive if its canonical embedding \(J_X:X\to X^{**}\), defined by \(\langle J_Xx,x^*\rangle_{X^{**},X^*}=\langle x^*,x\rangle_{X^*,X}\), is surjective. Equivalently, for every \(x^{**}\in X^{**}\) there exists \(x\in X\) such that \(\langle x^{**},x^*\rangle=\langle x^*,x\rangle\) for all \(x^*\in X^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Banach space is reflexive when every element of its bidual is evaluation at some element of the original space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: X\text{ is reflexive}\iff J_X:X\to X^{**}\text{ is surjective}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Weak Sequential Closedness, Relative Compactness, and Compactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definitions for a subset of a real Banach space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $M\subset U$, where $U$ is a real Banach space. The set $M$ is weakly sequentially closed if every sequence $(u_n)\subset M$ satisfying $u_n\rightharpoonup u$ has $u\in M$. It is weakly sequentially relatively compact if every sequence in $M$ has a weakly convergent subsequence. It is weakly sequentially compact if it is both weakly sequentially relatively compact and weakly sequentially closed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A subset of a real Banach space is weakly sequentially closed when it contains every weak limit of its sequences. It is weakly sequentially relatively compact when each of its sequences has a weakly convergent subsequence, and weakly sequentially compact when both properties hold.
assumptions_latex: U\text{ is a real Banach space}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M\text{ is weakly sequentially compact}\iff M\text{ is weakly sequentially relatively compact and weakly sequentially closed}

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: sequential Banach-Alaoglu for a separable predual
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential weak-star compactness on bounded dual sets when the predual is separable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
There exist \(x^*\in X^*\) and a subsequence \((x_{j_k}^*)\) such that
\[
x_{j_k}^*\stackrel{*}{\rightharpoonup}x^*,
\qquad
\langle x_{j_k}^*,x\rangle\to\langle x^*,x\rangle
\quad\text{for every }x\in X.
\]
Indeed, norm-bounded subsets of \(X^*\) are compact in \(\sigma(X^*,X)\); separability of \(X\) makes this topology metrizable on bounded subsets and therefore supplies subsequences. Without separability, weak-star compactness remains valid, but sequential compactness need not follow in this form.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bounded sequence in the dual of a separable Banach space has a weak-star convergent subsequence.
knowledge_statements.title: Weak-Star Compactness

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Critical BV Embedding Is Not Compact
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp endpoint boundary for BV-to-Lebesgue compactness in dimensions at least two.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(d\ge2\), the embedding \(BV(\Omega)\hookrightarrow L^{d/(d-1)}(\Omega)\) is generally not compact when \(\Omega\) contains a ball. Concentrating rescalings provide bounded BV sequences with no strongly convergent subsequence at the critical exponent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: BV compact embedding is sharp: concentration destroys compactness at the critical exponent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(BV(\Omega)\hookrightarrow L^{d/(d-1)}(\Omega)\) is not compact in general.
knowledge_statements.title: Critical BV Embedding Is Not Compact

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Normalization Is Necessary for Derivative-Only BV Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Escape along the additive-constant null direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A uniform bound on \(|Du_j|(\Omega)\) alone does not imply \(L^1\)-precompactness. On a finite-measure domain, the constants \(u_j\equiv j\) satisfy \(|Du_j|(\Omega)=0\) but are unbounded in \(L^1\). An \(L^1\) bound or a normalization controlling constants is therefore necessary for the standard BV compactness conclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Derivative variation does not control additive constants; an L1 bound or normalization is essential.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_j|Du_j|(\Omega)<\infty\) does not imply \(L^1\)-precompactness.
knowledge_statements.title: Normalization Is Necessary for Derivative-Only BV Bounds

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lebesgue-space compactness consequences of a uniform BV norm bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d\) be bounded with Lipschitz boundary. If \(d\ge2\), then \(BV(\Omega)\) embeds continuously into \(L^{d/(d-1)}(\Omega)\) and compactly into \(L^q(\Omega)\) for every \(1\le q<d/(d-1)\). If \(d=1\), bounded subsets of \(BV(\Omega)\) are relatively compact in every finite \(L^q(\Omega)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: BV bounds give compact convergence in every subcritical Lebesgue space, with only continuous embedding at the critical exponent in dimensions at least two.
assumptions_latex: \(\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d\) is bounded with Lipschitz boundary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(BV(\Omega)\Subset L^q(\Omega)\) for \(1\le q<d/(d-1)\) when \(d\ge2\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong \(L^1\) and derivative-measure compactness for uniformly bounded \(BV\) sequences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
There exist \(u\in BV(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)\) and a subsequence, not relabeled, such that
\[
u_j\to u\quad\text{strongly in }L^1(\Omega;\mathbb R^m),
\qquad
Du_j\stackrel{*}{\rightharpoonup}Du
\]
as finite vector-valued Radon measures. Moreover,
\[
|Du|(\Omega)\leq\liminf_{j\to\infty}|Du_j|(\Omega).
\]
Thus a uniform bound on the \(BV\) norm supplies the compactness needed for linear-growth variational problems, while retaining possible singular parts of the limiting derivative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform BV bounds yield strong L1 convergence along a subsequence, weak-star convergence of derivatives, and lower semicontinuity of total variation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Compactness and perimeter lower semicontinuity for sets of uniformly bounded perimeter
knowledge_statements.scope_note: BV compactness specialized to characteristic functions of measurable subsets of a bounded Lipschitz domain, including weak convergence of their distributional gradients in the stated test-function sense.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $D\subset\mathbb{R}^N$ be a bounded open domain with Lipschitz boundary, and let $(\Omega_n)$ be measurable subsets of $D$ such that there exists $c>0$ with $P_D(\Omega_n)\le c$ for all $n$. Then there exist a measurable set $\Omega\subset D$ and a subsequence $(\Omega_{n_k})$ such that $\chi_{\Omega_{n_k}}\to\chi_\Omega$ in $L^1(D)$ and $P_D(\Omega)\le\liminf_{k\to\infty}P_D(\Omega_{n_k})\le c$. Moreover, for every $\varphi\in\mathcal D^0(D;\mathbb{R}^N)$, $\langle\nabla\chi_{\Omega_{n_k}},\varphi\rangle\to\langle\nabla\chi_\Omega,\varphi\rangle$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In a bounded Lipschitz domain, a sequence of measurable sets with uniformly bounded relative perimeter has a subsequence whose characteristic functions converge in L1 to the characteristic function of a measurable set. The limit perimeter is no larger than the liminf, and the distributional gradients converge against every stated test function.
assumptions_latex: D\subset\mathbb{R}^N\text{ is bounded and open with Lipschitz boundary}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\Omega\subset D,\ \exists(n_k):\ \chi_{\Omega_{n_k}}\to\chi_\Omega\text{ in }L^1(D),\quad P_D(\Omega)\le\liminf_{k\to\infty}P_D(\Omega_{n_k})\le c,\quad \forall\varphi\in\mathcal D^0(D;\mathbb{R}^N),\ \langle\nabla\chi_{\Omega_{n_k}},\varphi\rangle\to\langle\nabla\chi_\Omega,\varphi\rangle.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fractional Sobolev embeddings for BV functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Both inclusions hold on bounded open Lipschitz domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $D\subset\mathbb{R}^N$ be a bounded open Lipschitz domain. Then
\[
BV(D)\subset W^{\varepsilon,1}(D)\qquad(0\leq\varepsilon<1),
\]
and
\[
BV(D)\cap L^\infty(D)\subset W^{\varepsilon,p}(D)
\qquad(1\leq p<\infty,\ 0\leq\varepsilon<1/p).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a bounded open Lipschitz domain, BV functions belong to every fractional W^{epsilon,1} space with epsilon below one; bounded BV functions belong to W^{epsilon,p} whenever p is finite and epsilon is below 1/p.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mass bounds alone do not preserve total mass under convergence on a noncompact space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the Dirac probabilities \(\delta_n\) on \(\mathbb R\), \(|\delta_n|(\mathbb R)=1\) and \(\delta_n\to0\) vaguely, but no subsequence converges narrowly in \(\mathcal P(\mathbb R)\). Uniform tightness prevents this escape of mass.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential weak-star compactness for uniformly bounded finite Radon measures on a compact metric space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
There exist \(\mu\in\mathcal M(K;\mathbb R^q)\) and a subsequence \((\mu_{j_k})\) such that
\[
\int_K\varphi\,d\mu_{j_k}\to\int_K\varphi\,d\mu
\quad\text{for every }\varphi\in C(K),
\]
componentwise. In addition,
\[
|\mu|(K)\leq\liminf_{k\to\infty}|\mu_{j_k}|(K).
\]
The metric assumption makes \(C(K)\) separable, so bounded weak-star compactness in its dual is sequential. This mechanism applies to distributional derivatives, fluxes, and concentration measures arising from energy-bounded sequences.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniformly bounded finite Radon measures on a compact metric space have a weak-star convergent subsequence, with lower semicontinuous total variation.
knowledge_statements.title: Measure-Valued Compactness

children.title: Trace Compactness Regimes
children.top_down_role: Boundary-trace behavior accompanying BV compactness.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: BV Weak-Star Convergence Does Not Preserve Traces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary layers show that ordinary BV weak-star convergence does not imply trace convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(\Omega=(0,1)\), let \(u_n(x)=\max\{1-nx,0\}\). Then \(u_n\to0\) in \(L^1(0,1)\), \(Du_n\stackrel{*}{\rightharpoonup}0\) in \(\mathcal M((0,1))\), and \(\sup_n|Du_n|((0,1))=1\), but \(Tu_n(0)=1\not\to0=T0(0)\). Trace continuity does hold under strict BV convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A BV boundary layer can vanish in the interior weak-star topology while retaining a nonzero trace; stronger convergence is needed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: u_n\to0\text{ BV weak-star, but }Tu_n(0)\not\to T0(0).
knowledge_statements.title: BV Weak-Star Convergence Does Not Preserve Traces

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compactness below, but generally not at, the critical Sobolev trace exponent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d\) be bounded Lipschitz, \(1<p<d\), and \(p_\partial^*=p(d-1)/(d-p)\). Then \(T:W^{1,p}(\Omega)\to L^q(\partial\Omega)\) is compact for \(1\le q<p_\partial^*\), while at \(q=p_\partial^*\) it is continuous but generally not compact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sobolev traces are compact in subcritical boundary spaces but generally lose compactness at the critical exponent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T:W^{1,p}(\Omega)\to L^q(\partial\Omega)\text{ is compact for }q<p_\partial^*\text{ and need not be compact at }q=p_\partial^*.
knowledge_statements.title: Critical Trace Exponent Boundary

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Trace Compactness at and Above the Interior Critical Index
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Completes the Sobolev trace regimes for \(p\ge d\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d\) is bounded Lipschitz, then for \(p=d>1\) the trace map \(W^{1,d}(\Omega)\to L^q(\partial\Omega)\) is compact for every finite \(q\). If \(p>d\), it is compact into \(C(\partial\Omega)\), and hence into every finite boundary Lebesgue space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At p equal to the dimension, traces are compact in every finite Lebesgue space; above the dimension, they are compact in continuous boundary functions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p=d\Rightarrow T:W^{1,d}(\Omega)\to L^q(\partial\Omega)\text{ compact for }q<\infty;\quad p>d\Rightarrow T:W^{1,p}(\Omega)\to C(\partial\Omega)\text{ compact}.
knowledge_statements.title: Trace Compactness at and Above the Interior Critical Index

assumptions_latex: \(\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d\) is a bounded Lipschitz domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The traces have a subsequence converging strongly in \(L^1(\partial\Omega;\mathbb R^m)\).

notation.meaning: Sobolev trace operator on the boundary of the domain.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compact trace convergence in a subcritical target space under superlinear Sobolev bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The trace operator
\[
T:W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)\to L^1(\partial\Omega;\mathbb R^m)
\]
is compact. Consequently, there exist a subsequence and \(g\in L^1(\partial\Omega;\mathbb R^m)\) such that
\[
Tu_{j_k}\to g\quad\text{strongly in }L^1(\partial\Omega;\mathbb R^m).
\]
If additionally \(u_{j_k}\rightharpoonup u\) in \(W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)\), continuity of the trace identifies \(g=Tu\). More generally, compactness holds in subcritical boundary Lebesgue spaces; the \(L^1\) formulation avoids endpoint distinctions among dimensions and exponents.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a bounded Lipschitz domain and p greater than one, bounded Sobolev sequences have strongly L1-convergent boundary traces along a subsequence.
knowledge_statements.title: Trace Compactness Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem fits the trace-compactness leaf and the L^1 target is subcritical for p>1, but the domain and exponent claim requires a specific trace-theorem locator.

children.title: Compact-Embedding Mechanisms
children.top_down_role: Strong compactness obtained from derivative control.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Critical Sobolev Exponent Is Not Compact
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp endpoint boundary of the subcritical Rellich embedding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(1<p<n\), the continuous embedding \(W^{1,p}_0(\Omega)\hookrightarrow L^{p^*}(\Omega)\), where \(p^*=np/(n-p)\), is generally not compact when \(\Omega\) contains a ball. Concentrating rescalings give bounded sequences with no strongly convergent subsequence in \(L^{p^*}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compact Sobolev embedding stops below the critical exponent because concentration destroys endpoint compactness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(W^{1,p}_0(\Omega)\hookrightarrow L^{p^*}(\Omega)\) is not compact in general.
knowledge_statements.title: Critical Sobolev Exponent Is Not Compact

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Critical and Supercritical Sobolev Compact Embeddings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rellich–Kondrachov regimes at and above the dimension exponent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n\) be bounded with Lipschitz boundary and let \((u_k)\) be bounded in \(W^{1,p}(\Omega)\). If \(p=n\), a subsequence converges strongly in \(L^q(\Omega)\) for every finite \(q\). If \(p>n\), then for every \(0\le\alpha<1-n/p\), a subsequence converges in \(C^{0,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At p equal to the dimension one has compactness in every finite Lebesgue space; above the dimension one has compact Hölder embeddings below the Morrey exponent.
assumptions_latex: \(\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n\) is bounded with Lipschitz boundary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p=n\Rightarrow u_{k_j}\to u\) in every finite \(L^q\); \(p>n\Rightarrow u_{k_j}\to u\) in \(C^{0,\alpha}\) for \(\alpha<1-n/p\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n\) be bounded with Lipschitz boundary and \(n\ge2\). Every bounded sequence in \(W^{1,1}(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)\) has a subsequence converging strongly in \(L^q(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)\) for every \(1\le q<n/(n-1)\). The limit belongs to \(BV(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)\) in general and need not belong to \(W^{1,1}\).

assumptions_latex: \(\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n\) is bounded with Lipschitz boundary.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rellich–Kondrachov compactness below the critical Sobolev exponent on bounded Lipschitz domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n\) be bounded with Lipschitz boundary, let \(1\le p<n\), and set \(p^*=np/(n-p)\). If \((u_k)\) is bounded in \(W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)\), then there exist \(u\in W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)\) and a subsequence \((u_{k_j})\) such that \(u_{k_j}\to u\) strongly in \(L^q(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)\) for every \(1\le q<p^*\). children.title: Concentration-Control Compactness Criteria
children.top_down_role: Compactness mechanisms preventing loss of mass or energy concentration.

children.title: Equiintegrability Criteria
children.top_down_role: Structural criteria yielding uniform integrability of varying families.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Power-bound criterion for equiintegrability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mu(\Omega)<\infty\), let \(q>1\), and suppose \(U\subset L^q(\Omega)\) is bounded. Then
\[\sup_{u\in U}\int_E|u|\,d\mu\le \Bigl(\sup_{u\in U}\|u\|_{L^q}\Bigr)\mu(E)^{1-1/q}\]
for every measurable \(E\subset\Omega\). Consequently, \(U\) is equiintegrable in \(L^1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every uniformly Lq-bounded family with q greater than one is equiintegrable in L1 on a finite measure space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U\) is equiintegrable in \(L^1(\Omega)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Higher-Integrability Sufficient Criterion

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak compactness characterization on a finite measure space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\Omega,\mathcal A,\mu)\) be a finite measure space. A subset \(U\subset L^1(\Omega)\) is relatively compact for \(\sigma(L^1,L^\infty)\) if and only if it is uniformly integrable, meaning under the convention of the immutable seed that it is \(L^1\)-bounded and its integrals are uniformly absolutely continuous with respect to \(\mu\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a finite measure space, equiintegrability is equivalent to relative weak compactness in L1.
assumptions_latex: \((\Omega,\mathcal A,\mu)\) is a finite measure space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U\) is relatively weakly compact in \(L^1\) if and only if \(U\) is uniformly integrable.

notation.meaning: Weak topology of L1 induced by L-infinity.

review_flags: terminology varies between equiintegrability and uniform integrability
knowledge_statements.title: Dunford–Pettis Criterion in L1

assumptions_latex: \((\Omega,\mathcal A,\mu)\) is a finite measure space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U\) is equiintegrable exactly when its integrals are uniformly small on sets of sufficiently small measure.

notation.meaning: A family of integrable vector-valued functions

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform absolute continuity criterion for finite-measure-domain \(L^1\) families.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A family \(U\subset L^1(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)\) is equiintegrable if and only if it is \(L^1\)-bounded and
\[
\forall\varepsilon>0\;\exists\delta>0\;\forall u\in U\;\forall E\in\mathcal A:\quad \mu(E)<\delta\Longrightarrow\int_E |u|\,d\mu<\varepsilon.
\]
On a finite measure space this condition prevents a uniformly positive amount of \(L^1\)-mass from being carried by sets whose measures vanish.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equiintegrability means uniform boundedness in integral and uniformly small mass on all sufficiently small measurable sets.
knowledge_statements.title: Equiintegrability Criteria

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the leaf and is a standard finite-measure characterization, but no cited source or locator establishes the intended convention for equiintegrability.

children.title: Concentration Control
children.top_down_role: Mechanisms preventing localization of mass or energy on small sets.

assumptions_latex: \((\Omega,\mathcal A,\mu)\) is a finite measure space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U\) is equiintegrable if and only if some superlinear convex gauge uniformly bounds \(\int_\Omega\Phi(|u|)\,d\mu\).

notation.meaning: Candidate family in the integrable space

knowledge_statements.scope_note: de la Vallée Poussin characterization of concentration control on finite measure spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The family \(U\subset L^1(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)\) is equiintegrable if and only if there exists an increasing convex function \(\Phi:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)\) satisfying \(\Phi(0)=0\), \(\lim_{t\to\infty}\Phi(t)/t=\infty\), and
\[
\sup_{u\in U}\int_\Omega \Phi(|u(x)|)\,d\mu(x)<\infty.
\]
The superlinear gauge penalizes large values uniformly and thereby excludes concentration of \(L^1\)-mass.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Concentration is excluded precisely when all functions admit a uniform integral bound under one convex superlinear gauge.
knowledge_statements.title: Concentration Control

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The de la Vallée Poussin characterization fits concentration control and the representation kind, but it has no source or inspectable locator.

children.title: Tightness Regimes
children.top_down_role: Control of escape in measure or spatial variables.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Practical sufficient condition preventing spatial escape.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S\) be a locally compact metric space and let \(V:S\to[0,+\infty]\) have compact sublevel sets. If a family \(\mathcal M\) of finite positive measures satisfies \(\sup_{\mu\in\mathcal M}\int_SV\,d\mu\le C<\infty\), then \(\mathcal M\) is tight. Quantitatively,
\[\sup_{\mu\in\mathcal M}\mu(\{V>R\})\le C/R\qquad(R>0).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A uniform moment bound for a coercive function forces a family of positive measures to be tight.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is a locally compact metric space.
\(\mathcal M\) is a family of finite positive measures with \(\sup_{\mu\in\mathcal M}\int V\,d\mu<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal M\) is tight.
knowledge_statements.title: Coercive-Moment Tightness Criterion

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Boundary Escape on a Bounded Open Domain
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of automatic tightness relative to compact subsets of an open bounded domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Omega=(0,1)\) and \(u_k=k\mathbf1_{(0,1/k)}\). Then \(\int_\Omega u_k\,dx=1\), but for every compact \(K\Subset\Omega\),
\[\int_{\Omega\setminus K}u_k\,dx=1\]
for all sufficiently large \(k\). Thus \(\{u_kdx:k\ge1\}\) is not tight as a family of measures on \(\Omega\), even though \(\Omega\) is bounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Boundedness of an open domain does not prevent mass from escaping toward its boundary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{u_kdx:k\ge1\}\) is not tight on \(\Omega\).

notation.meaning: Compact subset of the open domain.

knowledge_statements.title: Boundary Escape on a Bounded Open Domain

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Probability-measure form of the tightness–compactness equivalence on Polish spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) be a Polish space and let \(\mathcal P\) be a family of Borel probability measures on \(S\). Then \(\mathcal P\) is tight if and only if it is relatively compact for narrow convergence against bounded continuous functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For probability measures on a Polish space, tightness is equivalent to relative compactness for narrow convergence.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal P\) is a family of Borel probability measures on \(S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal P\) is tight if and only if it is relatively narrowly compact.
knowledge_statements.title: Prokhorov Tightness Criterion

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U\) is tight exactly when its \(L^1\)-mass is uniformly confined, up to arbitrary error, to one compact set.

notation.meaning: A compact subset of the spatial domain
Family whose spatial escape is tested

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spatial tightness criterion excluding loss of mass at infinity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A family \(U\subset L^1(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)\) is tight in the spatial variable when
\[
\forall\varepsilon>0\;\exists K\Subset\Omega\;\forall u\in U:\quad \int_{\Omega\setminus K}|u(x)|\,dx<\varepsilon.
\]
If \(U\) is also equiintegrable, then neither concentration on small sets nor escape of mass to spatial infinity can occur. On bounded domains, tightness is automatic when boundary leakage is not distinguished from mass inside the domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tightness requires the mass of every family member to lie uniformly, up to arbitrary error, in a common compact set.
knowledge_statements.title: Tightness Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed spatial-tightness condition fits the leaf, but the claim that tightness with K compactly contained in Omega is automatic on bounded domains is generally false: mass may concentrate arbitrarily near the boundary. A sourced boundary convention or correction is required.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Moment-Controlled Upgrade from Weak to Strong Narrow Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses convergence of a coercive radial moment to prevent escape and upgrade narrow convergence from the auxiliary weak Hilbert topology to the strong topology.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $X$ be the Hilbert space underlying $X_\varpi$, let $j:[0,+\infty)\to[0,+\infty)$ be continuous, strictly increasing, and surjective, and let $\mu_n,\mu\in\mathcal P(X)$. If $\mu_n\to\mu$ narrowly in $\mathcal P(X_\varpi)$ and $\int_X j(|x|)\,d\mu_n\to\int_X j(|x|)\,d\mu<+\infty$, then $\mu_n\to\mu$ narrowly in $\mathcal P(X)$ for the strong topology of $X$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Narrow convergence in the auxiliary weak Hilbert topology, together with convergence to a finite coercive radial moment, implies narrow convergence for the original strong Hilbert topology.
assumptions_latex: j:[0,+\infty)\to[0,+\infty)\text{ is continuous, strictly increasing, and surjective}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mu_n\rightharpoonup\mu\text{ narrowly in }\mathcal P(X).

children.title: Concentration Defects
children.top_down_role: Residual effects produced when concentration control fails.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Vanishing Defect and Strong Lp Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak-to-strong convergence when no total p-energy is lost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(1<p<\infty\), \(u_j\rightharpoonup u\) in \(L^p(\Omega)\), and \(\|u_j\|_{L^p}^p\to\|u\|_{L^p}^p\), then \(u_j\to u\) strongly in \(L^p(\Omega)\). In the energy-measure representation, vanishing defect together with convergence of total masses gives this norm convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weak convergence plus convergence of p-energy eliminates the defect and yields strong Lp convergence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(u_j\to u\) strongly in \(L^p(\Omega)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Vanishing Defect and Strong Lp Convergence

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Measure representation of energy retained beyond the weak-limit energy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(1<p<\infty\), let \(\Omega\) be bounded, and suppose \(u_jightharpoonup u\) in \(L^p(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)\). After passage to a subsequence, the energy measures converge weak-star on \(\overline\Omega\):
\[|u_j|^p\,dx\stackrel{*}{ightharpoonup}\mu=|u|^p\,dx+
u,\qquad 
u\ge0.\]
The nonnegative measure \(
u\) is the energy defect; its singular or atomic part records concentration invisible in \(u\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A weakly convergent Lp sequence may retain a nonnegative measure-valued energy defect beyond the energy of its weak limit.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|u_j|^pdx\stackrel{*}{\rightharpoonup}|u|^pdx+\nu\) along a subsequence, with \(\nu\ge0\).

notation.meaning: Weak-star limit of the energy measures.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(u_k\rightharpoonup0\) in \(L^p(0,1)\), while \(|u_k|^p\,dx\stackrel{*}{\rightharpoonup}\delta_0\) as measures and the energy densities are not equiintegrable.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical shrinking-support sequence exhibiting concentrated energy despite weak compactness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(1<p<\infty\), define \(u_k(x)=k^{1/p}\mathbf 1_{(0,1/k)}(x)\) on \((0,1)\). Then \(\|u_k\|_{L^p}=1\) and \(u_k\rightharpoonup0\) in \(L^p(0,1)\), but
\[
|u_k|^p\,dx=k\mathbf 1_{(0,1/k)}\,dx\stackrel{*}{\rightharpoonup}\delta_0
\]
as finite measures on \([0,1]\). Hence \((|u_k|^p)\) is not equiintegrable, and its limiting energy contains a concentration defect invisible in the weak limit \(u=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bounded weakly null sequence can concentrate all of its energy at one point, producing a nonzero defect measure.
knowledge_statements.title: Concentration Defects
