children.title: Admissible-Set Sequential Closure
children.top_down_role: Closure families for boundary, pointwise, differential, integral, and geometric constraints.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strong Closure Does Not Imply Weak Sequential Closure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Infinite-dimensional topology mismatch in admissibility passage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be an infinite-dimensional Hilbert space with orthonormal sequence \((e_j)\), and let \[A=\{u\in H:\|u\|=1\}.\] The sphere \(A\) is norm-closed, but \(e_j\rightharpoonup0\) while \(0\notin A\). Hence norm sequential closure alone does not preserve admissibility when compactness supplies only weak convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The unit sphere is strongly closed but loses feasibility along a weakly convergent orthonormal sequence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A\text{ is norm-closed but not weakly sequentially closed}.
knowledge_statements.title: Strong Closure Does Not Imply Weak Sequential Closure

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unified closure mechanism for boundary, differential, integral, and geometric constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G:(X,\tau)\to(Y,\sigma)\) be sequentially continuous and let \(C\subset Y\) be sequentially closed. Then \[A=G^{-1}(C)=\{u\in X\mid G(u)\in C\}\] is sequentially \(\tau\)-closed. Finitely many constraints are handled by the corresponding product map and product constraint set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constraint expressed as the preimage of a sequentially closed set under a sequentially continuous operator passes to direct-method limits.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is sequentially continuous for the specified convergence structures.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: G^{-1}(C)\text{ is sequentially closed}.
knowledge_statements.title: Continuous-Constraint Preimage Closure

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Closed Convex Constraints Are Weakly Sequentially Closed
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Core weak-closure regime for direct methods in Banach spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(X\) is a Banach space and \(A\subset X\) is norm-closed and convex, then \(A\) is weakly closed and therefore weakly sequentially closed. Thus \[u_j\rightharpoonup u,\quad u_j\in A\ \Longrightarrow\ u\in A.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Norm-closed convex feasible sets automatically survive weakly convergent direct-method subsequences.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is a norm-closed convex subset of a Banach space \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: u_j\rightharpoonup u\text{ and }u_j\in A\Rightarrow u\in A.
knowledge_statements.title: Closed Convex Constraints Are Weakly Sequentially Closed

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a topological space and \(A\subset X\).
\((u_k)\subset A\) converges to \(u\) in the topology used by the compactness argument.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The direct-method limit remains admissible precisely when \(A\) is sequentially closed for that convergence.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract closure condition matched to the convergence supplied by compactness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The admissible set \(A\subset X\) is sequentially closed for a specified convergence \(\tau\) if
\[
(u_k\in A\ \text{for every }k)\ \text{and}\ (u_k\to u\ \text{in }\tau)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad u\in A.
\]
Consequently, every \(\tau\)-convergent subsequence of an admissible minimizing sequence has an admissible limit. The topology \(\tau\) must be the same topology used in the compactness and lower-semicontinuity steps; closure in a stronger topology alone is insufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An admissible set passes to direct-method limits exactly when it is sequentially closed under the convergence produced by compactness.
knowledge_statements.title: Admissible-Set Sequential Closure

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The sequential-closure condition is mathematically appropriate for the leaf, but the record contains no evidence reference or standard-field rationale.

children.title: Lower-Semicontinuity Passage
children.top_down_role: Energy comparison between compactness limits and minimizing sequences.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Failure of the Energy Passage Without Lower Semicontinuity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compactness and feasibility alone do not ensure attainment when the energy is not lower semicontinuous.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A=[0,1]\), set \(F(0)=1\), and set \(F(x)=x\) for \(x>0\). Then \(u_n=1/n\to0\), \(F(u_n)\to0=\inf_A F\), and \(A\) is compact, but \(F(0)=1\); the infimum is not attained because \(F\) is not lower semicontinuous at \(0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A minimizing sequence can converge inside a compact feasible set without producing a minimizer when lower semicontinuity fails.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: u_n=1/n\to0,\quad F(u_n)\to\inf_A F=0,\quad F(0)=1,\quad\operatorname*{argmin}_A F=\varnothing.
knowledge_statements.title: Failure of the Energy Passage Without Lower Semicontinuity

assumptions_latex: \(A\) is sequentially closed for a convergence \(\tau\).
\((u_k)\subset A\) is minimizing and a subsequence satisfies \(u_{k_j}\to u\) in \(\tau\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(u\in A\) and \(F(u)=\inf_{v\in A}F(v)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The energy-comparison step in the abstract direct method.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((u_k)\subset A\) satisfy \(F(u_k)\to\inf_{v\in A}F(v)\), and suppose that \(u_{k_j}\to u\) in \(\tau\). Sequential closure gives \(u\in A\), while sequential lower semicontinuity gives
\[
F(u)\le\liminf_{j\to\infty}F(u_{k_j})=\inf_{v\in A}F(v).
\]
Since \(u\in A\), the reverse inequality follows from the definition of the infimum. Therefore \(F(u)=\inf_{v\in A}F(v)\), so the compactness limit is a minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sequential closure keeps the limit feasible, and lower semicontinuity makes its energy no larger than the minimizing-sequence limit.
knowledge_statements.title: Lower-Semicontinuity Passage

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The direct-method lower-semicontinuity passage is correctly categorized as a principle and is internally coherent, but no supporting source or locator is cited.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-dimensional compactness mechanism for derivative-coercive integrals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If one endpoint trace is prescribed, then \(\|u\|_{W^{1,p}(a,b)}\le C(1+\|u'\|_{L^p(a,b)})\), with the constant depending on the prescribed trace. Thus a lower bound by \(c|u'|^p-C\) yields bounded Sobolev sublevels.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixing one endpoint converts derivative control into control of the entire curve.
assumptions_latex: At least one endpoint trace is prescribed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sup_j\|u_j'\|_{L^p}<\infty\Rightarrow\sup_j\|u_j\|_{W^{1,p}}<\infty.
knowledge_statements.title: Endpoint Normalization Supplies Curve Coercivity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of full Sobolev coercivity for velocity-only energies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(F(u)=\int_a^b f(u')\,dt\) and the admissible class is invariant under \(u\mapsto u+c\), then \(F(u+c)=F(u)\) while \(\|u+c\|_{W^{1,p}}\to\infty\) as \(|c|\to\infty\). A trace, mean normalization, or coercive state term is needed for full-space coercivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Derivative growth cannot control additive translations of a curve.
assumptions_latex: The admissible class is invariant under additions of constants.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\text{ is not coercive in the full }W^{1,p}\text{ norm}.
knowledge_statements.title: Uncontrolled Translation Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural simplification for derivative densities of curves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite continuous \(f:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R\), Morrey quasiconvexity with respect to one-dimensional derivatives is equivalent to ordinary convexity of \(f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For curve derivatives, quasiconvexity and ordinary velocity convexity coincide.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R\) is finite and continuous.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\text{ is quasiconvex}\iff f\text{ is convex}.
knowledge_statements.title: One-Dimensional Quasiconvexity Equals Convexity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Autonomous Convex Tonelli Attainment for Curves
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-endpoint autonomous curve integral with coercive velocity growth.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(1<p<\infty\), \(I=(a,b)\), and
\[
A=\{u\in W^{1,p}(I;\mathbb R^m):u(a)=a_0,\ u(b)=b_0\}.
\]
If \(L:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R\) is convex, lower semicontinuous, and satisfies
\[
c|v|^p-C\le L(v)\le C(1+|v|^p),
\]
then \(F(u)=\int_I L(u'(t))dt\) attains its minimum on \(A\). If \(L\) is strictly convex, the minimizer is unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coercive convex velocity integral has a fixed-endpoint minimizing curve, unique under strict convexity.
assumptions_latex: \(1<p<\infty\) and both endpoint traces are fixed.
\(L\) is convex, lower semicontinuous, and has two-sided \(p\)-growth.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists u_*\in A:\ F(u_*)=\min_AF;\qquad L\text{ strictly convex}\Rightarrow u_*\text{ unique}.
knowledge_statements.title: Autonomous Convex Tonelli Attainment for Curves

assumptions_latex: \(1<p<\infty\), \(I=(a,b)\), and the endpoint-compatible class \(A\subset W^{1,p}(I;\mathbb R^m)\) is nonempty and weakly closed.
\(L:I\times\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb R^m\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is a normal integrand, convex in its last variable.
\(L(x,z,v)\ge c|v|^p-C(1+|z|^p)\), with boundary conditions or an added coercive term making the functional coercive on \(A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The functional \(F(u)=\int_I L(x,u(x),u'(x))\,dx\) attains its infimum on \(A\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coercive first-order Tonelli existence for Sobolev curves with convex velocity dependence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\subset W^{1,p}(I;\mathbb R^m)\) be nonempty and weakly closed. Suppose \(L\) is measurable in \(x\), lower semicontinuous in \((z,v)\), convex in \(v\), bounded below by \(c|v|^p-C(1+|z|^p)\) for constants \(c>0\) and \(C\ge0\), and such that \(F(u)=\int_I L(x,u,u')\,dx\) is coercive on \(A\). If \(F\) is proper on \(A\), then there exists \(u_*\in A\) satisfying \(F(u_*)=\inf_{u\in A}F(u)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proper coercive one-dimensional integral with lower-semicontinuous integrand convex in velocity attains its minimum on a weakly closed Sobolev class.
knowledge_statements.title: One-Dimensional Tonelli Theory

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem kind and local topic fit, but the exact lower-bound, coercivity, and lower-semicontinuity hypotheses require an authoritative Tonelli-theory source with a specific locator.

Then there exists a relatively open set \(\Omega\subset[S,T]\) of full measure such that \(\bar x\) is locally Lipschitz continuous on \(\Omega\).

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\Omega\subset[S,T]\text{ relatively open}:\ |[S,T]\setminus\Omega|=0,\quad \bar x\in\operatorname{Lip}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fixed-Endpoint Variational Problem on Absolutely Continuous Arcs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines arcs, admissibility, and global minimizers for the one-dimensional fixed-endpoint basic problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An arc on \([a,b]\) is an absolutely continuous map \(x:[a,b]\to\mathbb{R}^n\). The basic problem is
\[
\min\{J(x):x\in\mathrm{AC}([a,b];\mathbb{R}^n),\ x(a)=A,\ x(b)=B\}.
\]
An arc is admissible if it satisfies the endpoint constraints and \(J(x)\) is well defined and finite. An admissible arc \(x_*\) is a solution, or minimizer, if \(J(x_*)\leq J(x)\) for every admissible arc \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An arc is an absolutely continuous map from [a,b] to R^n. The basic problem minimizes J over arcs with prescribed endpoints A and B. An arc is admissible when it satisfies those constraints and J is well defined and finite. An admissible arc is a minimizer when its objective value is no greater than that of every admissible arc.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_*\text{ is a minimizer}\iff x_*\text{ is admissible and }J(x_*)\leq J(x)\quad\forall x\text{ admissible}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Tonelli Existence Theorem for Fixed-Endpoint Arcs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence for a first-order integral functional on absolutely continuous arcs with prescribed endpoints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let [S,T]\subset\mathbb{R},\ x_0,x_1\in\mathbb{R}^n, and L:[S,T]\times\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}. Consider minimizing \(\int_S^T L(t,x(t),\dot x(t))\,dt\) over \(x\in W^{1,1}([S,T];\mathbb{R}^n)\) satisfying \(x(S)=x_0\) and \(x(T)=x_1\). If \(L\) is continuous, \(v\mapsto L(t,x,v)\) is convex for every \(t\in[S,T]\) and \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and there exist \(c,d,\alpha>0\) such that \(L(t,x,v)\ge c|v|^{1+\alpha}-d\) for all \((t,x,v)\), then the problem has a minimizer in \(W^{1,1}([S,T];\mathbb{R}^n)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a continuous first-order Lagrangian that is convex in velocity and satisfies a uniform superlinear coercive lower bound, the fixed-endpoint integral problem over absolutely continuous arcs has a minimizer.
assumptions_latex: v\mapsto L(t,x,v)\text{ is convex for every }t\in[S,T],\ x\in\mathbb{R}^n
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname*{argmin}_{\substack{x\in W^{1,1}([S,T];\mathbb{R}^n)\\x(S)=x_0,\ x(T)=x_1}}\int_S^T L(t,x(t),\dot x(t))\,dt\ne\varnothing

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A nonsmooth sufficient condition imposed along a strong local minimizer of \((BP)\), with its smooth specialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\bar x\) be a strong local minimizer of \((BP)\), and assume the Tonelli existence hypotheses \((E1)\text{--}(E3)\). Suppose there are integrable functions \(c,\gamma\) such that, for a.e. \(t\in[S,T]\), \[\sup_{\xi\in P_x[\operatorname{co}\partial L](t)}|\xi|\le c(t)\inf_{\eta\in\partial_vL(t,\bar x(t),\dot{\bar x}(t))}|\eta|+\gamma(t),\] where \[P_x[\operatorname{co}\partial L](t)=\{\xi:(\xi,\eta)\in\operatorname{co}\partial L(t,\bar x(t),\dot{\bar x}(t))\text{ for some }\eta\in\mathbb R^n\}.\] Then \(\bar x\) is Lipschitz continuous. If \(L\) is smooth, the supplementary condition reduces to \[|L_x(t,\bar x(t),\dot{\bar x}(t))|\le c(t)|L_v(t,\bar x(t),\dot{\bar x}(t))|+\gamma(t)\quad\text{a.e.}\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strong local minimizer satisfying the Tonelli hypotheses is Lipschitz when the state components of the convexified subdifferential along the minimizer are controlled by the smallest velocity-subgradient norm plus an integrable remainder. For a smooth integrand, this becomes the corresponding inequality between the state and velocity gradients.
assumptions_latex: \(\bar x\) is a strong local minimizer of \((BP)\).
\(c,\gamma\in L^1([S,T])\) and the stated subgradient-growth inequality holds for a.e. \(t\in[S,T]\), evaluated along \((\bar x(t),\dot{\bar x}(t))\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x\in\operatorname{Lip}([S,T];\mathbb R^n)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bounded adjoint arcs imply bounded minimizing velocity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A local adjoint-boundedness criterion for regularity of a minimizer of the basic variational problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume the Tonelli existence hypotheses (E1)--(E3). Let \(\bar x\) minimize \((BP)\), let \(\mathcal S\) be its Tonelli set, and fix \(\bar t\in [S,T)\setminus\mathcal S\). Suppose there is \(k>0\) such that, for every \(t'\in(\bar t,T)\) with \([\bar t,t']\subset [S,T]\setminus\mathcal S\), there exists \(p\in W^{1,1}([\bar t,t'];\mathbb R^n)\) satisfying \[\dot p(t)\in\operatorname{co}\{q:(q,p(t))\in\partial L(t,\bar x(t),\dot{\bar x}(t))\}\quad\text{a.e.}\] and \(|p(t)|\le k\) for every \(t\in[\bar t,t']\). Then \(\dot{\bar x}\in L^\infty([\bar t,T];\mathbb R^n)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the Tonelli existence hypotheses, if uniformly bounded adjoint arcs satisfying the stated generalized Euler inclusion exist on every Tonelli-set-free interval beginning at bar t, then the minimizing velocity is essentially bounded from bar t to T.
assumptions_latex: \(\bar x\) is a minimizer of \((BP)\), with Tonelli set \(\mathcal S\), and \(\bar t\in[S,T)\setminus\mathcal S\).

\(\exists k>0\;\forall t'\in(\bar t,T)\) with \([\bar t,t']\subset[S,T]\setminus\mathcal S\), \(\exists p\in W^{1,1}([\bar t,t'];\mathbb R^n)\) satisfying the generalized adjoint inclusion a.e. and \(\|p\|_{L^\infty}\le k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\dot{\bar x}\in L^\infty([\bar t,T];\mathbb R^n)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Tonelli Existence Theorem for Coercive Convex Lagrangians
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence of an absolutely continuous minimizer for the associated one-dimensional fixed-endpoint variational problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(r>1\), and let \(\Lambda:[a,b]\times\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be continuous and convex in \(v\). If there exist constants \(\alpha>0\) and \(\beta\in\mathbb{R}\) such that
\[
\Lambda(t,x,v)\geq \alpha|v|^r+\beta
\quad\forall(t,x,v)\in[a,b]\times\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^n,
\]
then the associated basic fixed-endpoint problem \((P)\) admits a solution in \(\mathrm{AC}([a,b];\mathbb{R}^n)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the Lagrangian is continuous, convex in velocity, and uniformly bounded below by alpha times the r-th power of the velocity norm plus a constant, with r greater than one and alpha positive, then the associated fixed-endpoint variational problem has an absolutely continuous minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The basic fixed-endpoint problem }(P)\text{ admits a minimizer }x_*\in\mathrm{AC}([a,b];\mathbb{R}^n).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Everywhere extended differentiability in the scalar case
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar minimizers under strict velocity convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Assume \(\mathrm{(E1)}\)–\(\mathrm{(E3)}\). Suppose that for every \(t\in[S,T]\) and \(w\in\mathbb R\), \(L(\cdot,\bar x(t),w)\) is continuous at \(t\), that \(L(t,\bar x(t),\cdot)\) is strictly convex, and that \(n=1\). If \(\bar x\) is a minimizer, then for every \(\tau\in[S,T]\) the relative limit
\[
\lim_{\substack{t\to\tau\\t\in[S,T]}}\frac{\bar x(t)-\bar x(\tau)}{t-\tau}
\]
exists in the extended real line; it may be finite or infinite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In the scalar case, under the Tonelli hypotheses, time continuity, and strict convexity in velocity, a minimizer has an extended derivative at every point of the interval, with one-sided interpretation at endpoints.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exceptional-set, adjoint, and conditional smoothness conclusions for strong local minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Assume \(\mathrm{(E1)}\)–\(\mathrm{(E3)}\), let \(\bar x\) be a strong local minimizer, and let \(\mathcal S\) be its Tonelli set. Then \(\mathcal S\) is a possibly empty closed set of measure zero. For every closed interval \(I\subset[S,T]\setminus\mathcal S\), \(\bar x\) is Lipschitz on \(I\), and there exists \(p\in W^{1,1}(I;\mathbb R^n)\) such that for almost every \(t\in I\),
\[
\dot p(t)\in\operatorname{co}\{q:(q,p(t))\in\partial L(t,\bar x(t),\dot{\bar x}(t))\}
\]
and
\[
p(t)\cdot\dot{\bar x}(t)-L(t,\bar x(t),\dot{\bar x}(t))=\max_{v\in\mathbb R^n}\{p(t)\cdot v-L(t,\bar x(t),v)\}.
\]
If, additionally, \(L(\cdot,\bar x(t),w)\) is continuous at \(t\) for every \(t,w\), and \(L(t,\bar x(t),\cdot)\) is strictly convex for every \(t\), then \(\bar x\) is \(C^1\) on \([S,T]\setminus\mathcal S\). If further, for some integer \(r\ge2\), \(L\) is \(C^r\) near each \((t,\bar x(t),\dot{\bar x}(t))\) and \(L_{vv}(t,\bar x(t),\dot{\bar x}(t))\) is positive definite, then \(\bar x\) is \(C^r\) on \([S,T]\setminus\mathcal S\), with the stated one-sided interpretation at endpoints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Tonelli set of a strong local minimizer is closed and null. Away from it, the minimizer is Lipschitz and admits an adjoint satisfying a generalized Euler inclusion and a velocity-maximization identity. Additional time continuity and strict velocity convexity give continuous differentiability; additional smoothness and positive-definite velocity curvature give corresponding higher regularity.
assumptions_latex: \bar x\text{ is a strong local minimizer}
I\subset[S,T]\setminus\mathcal S\text{ is a closed interval}
\text{The }C^1\text{ conclusion additionally assumes time continuity along }\bar x\text{ and strict convexity in }v
\text{The }C^r\text{ conclusion additionally assumes local }C^r\text{ smoothness and }L_{vv}>0
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal S\text{ is closed and }|\mathcal S|=0;\quad \bar x|_I\in\operatorname{Lip}(I);\quad \exists p\in W^{1,1}(I;\mathbb R^n)\text{ satisfying the stated inclusion and maximization identity};\quad \text{the additional hypotheses imply }C^1\text{ or }C^r\text{ regularity}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Maximal Lipschitz region and Tonelli set
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exceptional-set representation for the failure of local Lipschitz regularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For an absolutely continuous \(\bar x:[S,T]\to\mathbb{R}^n\), let
\[
\Omega_{\max}(\bar x):=\bigcup\{\Omega\subset[S,T]:\Omega\text{ is relatively open and }\bar x\in\operatorname{Lip}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)\}.
\]
Then \(\Omega_{\max}(\bar x)\) is relatively open, has full measure, and \(\bar x\) is locally Lipschitz on it. The Tonelli set is
\[
\mathcal S:=[S,T]\setminus\Omega_{\max}(\bar x).
\]
Equivalently, \(\mathcal S\) consists of points at which the slopes of \(\bar x\) are unbounded in every vicinity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The maximal Lipschitz region is the union of all relatively open sets on which the curve is locally Lipschitz. Its complement is the Tonelli set, the exceptional set where slopes are unbounded in every neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Omega_{\max}(\bar x)\text{ is relatively open and full measure},\quad \mathcal S=[S,T]\setminus\Omega_{\max}(\bar x)

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential bounded-slope regularity using pairs that bracket the point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(y:[S,T]\to\mathbb R^n\) and \(\tau\in[S,T]\), \(\tau\) is a regular point of \(y\) if
\[
\liminf_{\substack{S\le s_i\le\tau\le t_i\le T\\s_i\to\tau,\ t_i\to\tau,\ s_i\ne t_i}}
\frac{\lVert y(t_i)-y(s_i)\rVert}{|t_i-s_i|}<+\infty.
\]
Equivalently, there exist sequences satisfying these bracketing and convergence conditions and a constant \(K>0\) such that \(\lVert y(t_i)-y(s_i)\rVert\le K|t_i-s_i|\) for all \(i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point is regular when it can be bracketed by convergent pairs of distinct times whose difference quotients remain uniformly bounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \tau\text{ is regular for }y\iff \exists K>0,\ (s_i),(t_i):\ S\le s_i\le\tau\le t_i\le T,\ s_i,t_i\to\tau,\ s_i\ne t_i,\ \lVert y(t_i)-y(s_i)\rVert\le K|t_i-s_i|

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Tonelli Existence Theorem for the Basic Variational Problem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded existence result for the one-dimensional basic variational problem (BP).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume that $L$ is bounded on bounded sets, $t\mapsto L(t,x,v)$ is measurable for every $(x,v)$, and $v\mapsto L(t,x,v)$ is convex for every $(t,x)$. For every $N>0$, suppose there is $k_N>0$ such that $|L(t,x,v)-L(t,x',v')|\le k_N|(x,v)-(x',v')|$ for all $(x,v),(x',v')\in NB$ and a.e. $t\in[S,T]$. Suppose also that there are $\alpha\ge0$ and a convex function $\theta:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$ satisfying $\lim_{r\to\infty}\theta(r)/r=+\infty$ and $L(t,x,v)\ge\theta(|v|)-\alpha|x|$ for all $(x,v)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^n$ and a.e. $t\in[S,T]$. Then $(BP)$ has a minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the integrand has the stated measurability, velocity convexity, bounded-set regularity, uniform local Lipschitz continuity, and superlinear coercivity properties, then the basic variational problem has a minimizer.
assumptions_latex: L\text{ is bounded on bounded sets}
t\mapsto L(t,x,v)\text{ is measurable for every }(x,v)
v\mapsto L(t,x,v)\text{ is convex for every }(t,x)
\forall N>0\;\exists k_N>0:\ |L(t,x,v)-L(t,x',v')|\le k_N|(x,v)-(x',v')|\quad\text{for all }(x,v),(x',v')\in NB\text{ and a.e. }t\in[S,T]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (BP)\text{ has a minimizer.}

children.title: Scalar Sobolev Existence
children.top_down_role: Scalar multidimensional existence under convex-gradient structures.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compactness condition for derivative-coercive scalar energies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a scalar admissible class has prescribed trace on a boundary portion of positive measure, or prescribed mean, then \(\|u\|_{W^{1,p}}\le C(1+\|\nabla u\|_{L^p})\). Consequently, a lower bound by \(c|\xi|^p-C\) yields bounded Sobolev sublevels.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A trace or mean normalization converts gradient control into full Sobolev coercivity.
assumptions_latex: The class removes additive constants by a trace or mean constraint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sup_jF(u_j)<\infty\Rightarrow (u_j)\text{ is bounded in }W^{1,p}(\Omega).
knowledge_statements.title: Scalar Poincare Normalization

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp lower-semicontinuity boundary for autonomous scalar gradient densities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite continuous scalar-gradient density in the standard \(p\)-growth regime, failure of convexity is failure of quasiconvexity and permits oscillatory sequences that violate sequential weak lower semicontinuity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonconvex scalar gradient density permits laminating oscillations and loses weak lower semicontinuity.
assumptions_latex: The density is finite, continuous, autonomous, and has standard \(p\)-growth.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\text{ nonconvex}\Rightarrow F\text{ is not sequentially weakly lower semicontinuous under suitable affine boundary data}.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex Scalar Gradient Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar multidimensional simplification distinguishing this leaf from vectorial theory.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite continuous scalar-gradient density \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), convexity, rank-one convexity, and quasiconvexity are equivalent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For scalar gradients, quasiconvexity reduces to ordinary convexity.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is finite and continuous.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\text{ convex}\iff f\text{ rank-one convex}\iff f\text{ quasiconvex}.
knowledge_statements.title: Scalar Quasiconvexity Equals Gradient Convexity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak lower semicontinuity with explicit control of state dependence and negative parts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(u_j\rightharpoonup u\) in \(W^{1,p}(\Omega)\), with \(u_j\to u\) strongly in a space controlling the state dependence. If \(f(x,s,\xi)\) is a normal integrand, lower semicontinuous in \((s,\xi)\), convex in \(\xi\), and its negative parts satisfy the required uniform-integrability lower bound, then \(\int_\Omega f(x,u,\nabla u)\,dx\le\liminf_j\int_\Omega f(x,u_j,\nabla u_j)\,dx\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convex gradient dependence yields weak lower semicontinuity when state dependence and negative parts are controlled.
assumptions_latex: The Sobolev compact embedding used controls the state variable.
The negative parts are uniformly integrable along the sequence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F(u)\le\liminf_{j\to\infty}F(u_j).
knowledge_statements.title: Scalar Convex-Gradient Weak Lower Semicontinuity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar autonomous existence with explicit normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(1<p<\infty\), let \(A\subset W^{1,p}(\Omega)\) be nonempty and weakly closed, and assume that \(A\) has fixed mean or fixed trace sufficient for a Poincare inequality. If \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is convex, lower semicontinuous, and satisfies
\[
c|\xi|^p-C\le f(\xi)\le C(1+|\xi|^p),
\]
then \(F(u)=\int_\Omega f(\nabla u)dx\) attains its infimum on \(A\). If \(f\) is strictly convex and \(A\) is convex, the minimizer is unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A normalized scalar Sobolev class admits a minimizer for a coercive convex gradient density, uniquely under strict convexity.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is nonempty, weakly closed, and satisfies a Poincare normalization.
\(f\) is convex, lower semicontinuous, and has two-sided \(p\)-growth.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists u_*\in A:\ F(u_*)=\min_AF;\qquad f\text{ strictly convex and }A\text{ convex}\Rightarrow u_*\text{ unique}.
knowledge_statements.title: Autonomous Scalar Convex-Gradient Attainment

assumptions_latex: \(\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n\) is bounded and Lipschitz, \(1<p<\infty\), and \(A\subset W^{1,p}(\Omega)\) is nonempty and weakly closed.
\(f:\Omega\times\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is a normal integrand and convex in its gradient variable.
\(F(u)=\int_\Omega f(x,u,\nabla u)\,dx\) is proper, bounded below, and coercive on \(A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exists \(u_*\in A\) such that \(F(u_*)=\inf_{u\in A}F(u)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar direct-method existence based on convexity in the gradient variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Assume that \(f\) is measurable in \(x\), lower semicontinuous in \((s,\xi)\), and convex in \(\xi\). If the functional
\[
F(u)=\int_\Omega f(x,u(x),\nabla u(x))\,dx
\]
is proper, bounded below, and coercive on the nonempty weakly closed set \(A\subset W^{1,p}(\Omega)\), then \(F\) is sequentially weakly lower semicontinuous along admissible sequences under the stated normal-integrand hypotheses, and there exists \(u_*\in A\) with \(F(u_*)=\inf_{u\in A}F(u)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convex gradient dependence, weak closure, coercivity, and lower semicontinuity yield a minimizer for a scalar Sobolev integral.
knowledge_statements.title: Scalar Sobolev Existence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The scalar existence theorem fits the leaf, but normal-integrand status, lower semicontinuity, and convexity in the gradient alone do not transparently supply the asserted weak lower semicontinuity without appropriate negative-part or growth hypotheses. A precise source is required.

children.title: Vectorial Quasiconvex Existence
children.top_down_role: Vectorial existence based on quasiconvex lower semicontinuity.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Normalization Required for Vectorial Gradient Coercivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correction of the additive-constant gap in derivative-only vectorial energies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A lower bound \(f(\xi)\ge c|\xi|^p-C\) controls \(\nabla u\) in \(L^p\), but controls \(u\) in \(W^{1,p}\) only after translations are removed by a prescribed trace, mean normalization, or coercive state term.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Gradient growth gives full Sobolev coercivity only when translations are fixed or penalized.
assumptions_latex: The admissible class satisfies a Poincare normalization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sup_jF(u_j)<\infty\Rightarrow (u_j)\text{ is bounded in }W^{1,p}.
knowledge_statements.title: Normalization Required for Vectorial Gradient Coercivity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Rank-One Convexity Is Insufficient in General
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Genuinely vectorial boundary between algebraic tests and quasiconvexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In matrix dimensions where rank-one convexity and quasiconvexity are known not to coincide, rank-one convexity does not guarantee quasiconvexity, sequential weak lower semicontinuity, or direct-method existence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convexity along rank-one lines does not rule out every genuinely vectorial microstructure.
assumptions_latex: The matrix dimension lies in a regime with known rank-one-convex but nonquasiconvex densities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{rank-one convexity}\not\Rightarrow\text{quasiconvexity}.
knowledge_statements.title: Rank-One Convexity Is Insufficient in General

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quasiconvexity Is Necessary for Autonomous Weak Lower Semicontinuity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessity under affine boundary tests for finite autonomous densities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a finite continuous density with standard \(p\)-growth defines a sequentially weakly lower-semicontinuous autonomous gradient integral under affine boundary data, then the density is quasiconvex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weak lower semicontinuity of an autonomous vectorial gradient integral forces every quasiconvexity test inequality.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is finite, continuous, and has standard \(p\)-growth.
Weak lower semicontinuity holds under fixed affine boundary data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\text{ is quasiconvex}.
knowledge_statements.title: Quasiconvexity Is Necessary for Autonomous Weak Lower Semicontinuity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Autonomous vectorial first-order integrals with quasiconvex density.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(1<p<\infty\). If \(f:\mathbb R^{m\times n}\to\mathbb R\) is continuous, quasiconvex, and satisfies \(|f(\xi)|\le C(1+|\xi|^p)\), then \(F(u)=\int_\Omega f(\nabla u)\,dx\) is sequentially weakly lower semicontinuous on \(W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuous quasiconvex vectorial density with p-growth generates a weakly lower-semicontinuous Sobolev integral.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is continuous, quasiconvex, and has two-sided \(p\)-growth.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: u_j\rightharpoonup u\text{ in }W^{1,p}\Rightarrow F(u)\le\liminf_jF(u_j).
knowledge_statements.title: Morrey Weak Lower Semicontinuity Theorem

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical vectorial gradient definition on a reference cube.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A finite density \(f:\mathbb R^{m\times n}\to\mathbb R\) is quasiconvex at \(\xi\) if
\[
f(\xi)\le \fint_Q f(\xi+\nabla\varphi(y))\,dy
\]
for every \(\varphi\in W^{1,\infty}_0(Q;\mathbb R^m)\). It is quasiconvex if this holds at every \(\xi\). For finite continuous densities, an equivalent definition uses any bounded Lipschitz reference domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A density is quasiconvex when no compactly supported gradient fluctuation lowers the energy of a constant gradient.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is finite; domain-independence additionally uses continuity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\text{ is quasiconvex}\iff \forall\xi,\varphi:\ f(\xi)\le\fint_Qf(\xi+\nabla\varphi)\,dy.
knowledge_statements.title: Morrey Quasiconvexity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Autonomous vectorial existence with explicit translation control.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(1<p<\infty\), let \(A\subset W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)\) be nonempty and weakly closed, and assume that a fixed trace or mean condition gives a Poincare inequality on \(A\). If \(f:\mathbb R^{m\times n}\to\mathbb R\) is continuous, quasiconvex, and satisfies
\[
c|\xi|^p-C\le f(\xi)\le C(1+|\xi|^p),
\]
then \(F(u)=\int_\Omega f(\nabla u)dx\) attains its infimum on \(A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quasiconvex lower semicontinuity plus normalized p-coercivity yields a vectorial Sobolev minimizer.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is nonempty, weakly closed, and satisfies a Poincare normalization.
\(f\) is continuous, quasiconvex, and has two-sided \(p\)-growth.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists u_*\in A:\ F(u_*)=\min_{u\in A}F(u).
knowledge_statements.title: Normalized Quasiconvex Direct-Method Attainment

assumptions_latex: \(\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n\) is bounded and Lipschitz, \(1<p<\infty\), and \(A\subset W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)\) is nonempty and weakly closed.
\(f:\mathbb R^{m\times n}\to\mathbb R\) is continuous, quasiconvex, and satisfies \(c|\xi|^p-C\le f(\xi)\le C(1+|\xi|^p)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exists \(u_*\in A\) satisfying \(F(u_*)=\inf_{u\in A}F(u)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Autonomous vectorial existence under quasiconvexity and two-sided \(p\)-growth.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \(f:\mathbb R^{m\times n}\to\mathbb R\) is continuous and quasiconvex, meaning that for every \(\xi\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and \(\varphi\in W^{1,\infty}_0((0,1)^n;\mathbb R^m)\),
\[
f(\xi)\le\int_{(0,1)^n}f(\xi+\nabla\varphi(y))\,dy.
\]
If \(f\) has two-sided \(p\)-growth and \(A\subset W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)\) is nonempty and weakly closed, then \(F(u)=\int_\Omega f(\nabla u)\,dx\) is coercive and sequentially weakly lower semicontinuous on \(A\). If proper, it attains its infimum on \(A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proper vectorial gradient integral with quasiconvex density and p-growth attains its minimum on a weakly closed Sobolev class.
knowledge_statements.title: Vectorial Quasiconvex Existence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Quasiconvexity and p-growth appropriately support weak lower semicontinuity, but gradient coercivity does not by itself make F coercive in the full W^{1,p} norm on an arbitrary weakly closed class because constants are uncontrolled. The exact existence regime needs correction and a source.

children.title: Polyconvex Elasticity Existence
children.top_down_role: Determinant-sensitive existence regimes in nonlinear elasticity.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical minors-based structure for nonlinear elastic energies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A density \(f:\mathbb R^{n\times n}\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is polyconvex if there is a convex lower-semicontinuous function \(g\) such that \(f(F)=g(M(F))\), where \(M(F)\) collects all minors of \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A density is polyconvex when it is convex as a function of all deformation-gradient minors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f=g\circ M\text{ for some convex lower-semicontinuous }g.

notation.meaning: Vector of all minors of the matrix F

knowledge_statements.title: Polyconvex Energy Density

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polyconvexity Is a Sufficient Quasiconvexity Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural relation to the vectorial quasiconvex sibling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For finite densities under the standard regularity convention, \(\text{convex}\Rightarrow\text{polyconvex}\Rightarrow\text{quasiconvex}\Rightarrow\text{rank-one convex}\). The reverse implications fail in general.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Polyconvexity is a tractable sufficient condition for quasiconvexity.
assumptions_latex: The density is finite and has the regularity required by the standard implication chain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\text{ polyconvex}\Rightarrow f\text{ quasiconvex}.
knowledge_statements.title: Polyconvexity Is a Sufficient Quasiconvexity Structure

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Weak Continuity of Minors Above the Critical Exponent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak-continuity mechanism used in the simplified supercritical polyconvex regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(u_j\rightharpoonup u\) in \(W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb R^n)\) and \(p>k\), then every \(k\)-th order minor of \(\nabla u_j\) converges weakly in \(L^{p/k}\) to the corresponding minor of \(\nabla u\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Above its critical integrability exponent, each gradient minor passes weakly to the limit.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M_k(\nabla u_j)\rightharpoonup M_k(\nabla u)\text{ in }L^{p/k}.

notation.meaning: Collection of kth-order minors of F

knowledge_statements.title: Weak Continuity of Minors Above the Critical Exponent

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Orientation-Preserving Polyconvex Attainment with a Determinant Barrier
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Supercritical polyconvex elasticity with a finite-energy orientation constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(p>n\), let \(A\subset W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb R^n)\) be nonempty and weakly closed with a trace normalization, and let \(W(F)=g(M(F))\), where \(g\) is convex and lower semicontinuous. Assume
\[
W(F)\ge c|F|^p-C,
\qquad W(F)=+\infty\ \text{when }\det F\le0,
\]
and that \(I(u)=\int_\Omega W(\nabla u)dx\) is proper on \(A\). Then \(I\) attains its infimum on \(A\), and every finite-energy minimizer satisfies \(\det\nabla u>0\) almost everywhere.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coercive polyconvex energy with an infinite orientation barrier admits a finite-energy orientation-preserving minimizer.
assumptions_latex: \(p>n\), and the weakly closed class has a trace normalization.
\(W=g\circ M\) with \(g\) convex and lower semicontinuous.
\(W\) is \(p\)-coercive and infinite when the determinant is nonpositive.
The functional is proper on the admissible class.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists u_*\in A:\ I(u_*)=\inf_AI,\qquad \det\nabla u_*>0\text{ a.e.}

notation.meaning: Vector of all minors of the deformation gradient

knowledge_statements.title: Orientation-Preserving Polyconvex Attainment with a Determinant Barrier

assumptions_latex: \(\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n\) is bounded and Lipschitz, \(p>n\), and \(A\subset W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb R^n)\) is nonempty and weakly closed.
\(f(\xi)=g(M(\xi))\), where \(M(\xi)\) lists all minors and \(g\) is convex and lower semicontinuous.
\(f(\xi)\ge c|\xi|^p-C\), and \(F(u)=\int_\Omega f(\nabla u)\,dx\) is proper on \(A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exists \(u_*\in A\) with \(F(u_*)=\inf_{u\in A}F(u)\).

notation.meaning: Vector of all minors, including the determinant

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simplified polyconvex existence regime with supercritical Sobolev exponent and weakly closed constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M(\xi)\) denote the vector of all minors of \(\xi\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), including \(\det\xi\). Suppose \(f(\xi)=g(M(\xi))\), where \(g\) is convex and lower semicontinuous, and suppose \(f(\xi)\ge c|\xi|^p-C\) with \(p>n\). Then the associated functional \(F(u)=\int_\Omega f(\nabla u)\,dx\) is sequentially weakly lower semicontinuous under the corresponding weak continuity of minors. Consequently, if \(A\subset W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb R^n)\) is nonempty and weakly closed and \(F\) is proper on \(A\), then \(F\) attains its infimum on \(A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coercive polyconvex elastic energy attains its minimum on a weakly closed deformation class when minors pass continuously to weak limits.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Perforated sequential laminates attain the relaxed multiple-load optimum
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimal-value equivalence and stress-preserving laminate replacement in homogenized elastic design.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the multiple-load objective \(J^*\) in (4.178),
\[
\min_{(\theta,A^*)\in\mathcal{CD}}J^*(\theta,A^*)
=
\min_{(\theta,A^*)\in\mathcal{LD}^+}J^*(\theta,A^*),
\]
where \(\mathcal{CD}\) is the class of composite designs and \(\mathcal{LD}^+\) is the class of perforated sequentially laminated designs. If \((\theta,A^*)\in\mathcal{CD}\) is a minimizer and \(\{\sigma_i\}\) minimizes the associated compliances, then there exists a sequential laminate \(\widetilde A^*\) such that \((\theta,\widetilde A^*)\in\mathcal{LD}^+\) is also a minimizer, the same \(\{\sigma_i\}\) are associated stresses, and
\[
A^{*-1}\sigma_i=\widetilde A^{*-1}\sigma_i\quad\text{for every load }i.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restricting the relaxed multiple-load elastic design problem from all composite designs to perforated sequential laminates does not change its optimal value. Every composite minimizer can be replaced by a sequential-laminate minimizer with the same density and associated stresses, and both effective tensors act identically on those stresses through their inverses.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min_{\mathcal{CD}}J^*=\min_{\mathcal{LD}^+}J^*,\qquad \exists\widetilde A^*:\ (\theta,\widetilde A^*)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\mathcal{LD}^+}J^*,\quad A^{*-1}\sigma_i=\widetilde A^{*-1}\sigma_i\ \forall i.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Representation and density minimizer for the multiple-load integrand
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded characterization of a reduced integrand in homogenized elastic design.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\{\tau_i\}_{i=1}^n\in(\mathcal M_N^s)^n\),
\[
g^n(\{\tau_i\},\theta)=\sum_{i=1}^n B^{-1}\tau_i:\tau_i+\frac{\theta}{1-\theta}g_n^*(\{\tau_i\}),
\]
where \(g_n^*\) is continuous, convex, positively homogeneous of degree two, and positive for \(\{\tau_i\}\neq0\). Thus \(g^n\) is continuous in \((\{\tau_i\},\theta)\) and separately strictly convex in the stress variables and in \(\theta\). The scalar minimization problem referenced as (4.173) has the unique minimizer
\[
\theta_{\{\tau_i\}}=\max\!\left\{0,1-\sqrt{\frac{g_n^*(\{\tau_i\})}{-\ell}}\right\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The multiple-load reduced integrand is the sum of the quadratic elastic stress energy and theta/(1−theta) times a continuous, convex, degree-two homogeneous function that is positive away from zero. The integrand is continuous and separately strictly convex, and the associated scalar density problem has the stated unique threshold-form minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: g^n(\{\tau_i\},\theta)=\sum_{i=1}^nB^{-1}\tau_i:\tau_i+\frac{\theta}{1-\theta}g_n^*(\{\tau_i\}),\qquad \theta_{\{\tau_i\}}=\max\left\{0,1-\sqrt{\frac{g_n^*(\{\tau_i\})}{-\ell}}\right\}.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generalized-growth existence in a reflexive Orlicz–Sobolev space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(W^{1,\Phi}(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)\) be reflexive, let \(A\) be nonempty and sequentially weakly closed, and suppose
\[
F(u)=\int_\Omega[\Phi(|\nabla u|)+V(x,u)]\,dx,
\]
where \(V\) is a convex lower-semicontinuous normal integrand with an integrable lower bound. If \(F\) is proper and a trace, mean, or state-coercive condition makes its sublevels bounded in \(W^{1,\Phi}\), then \(F\) attains its infimum on \(A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reflexive Orlicz growth, weak closure, lower semicontinuity, and normalized coercivity yield a minimizer.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is nonempty and sequentially weakly closed.
\(V\) is convex and lower semicontinuous in its state variable and has an integrable lower bound.
The functional is proper and has bounded sublevels.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists u_*\in A:\ F(u_*)=\inf_{u\in A}F(u).

knowledge_statements.title: Reflexive Orlicz–Sobolev Direct Method

assumptions_latex: \(\Phi\) and its conjugate \(\Phi^*\) are Young functions satisfying the \(\Delta_2\) condition, and \(W^{1,\Phi}(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)\) is reflexive.
\(A\subset W^{1,\Phi}(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)\) is nonempty and weakly closed.
\(f\) is a normal integrand, convex in its gradient variable, and \(F(u)=\int_\Omega f(x,u,\nabla u)\,dx\) is proper, weakly lower semicontinuous, and coercive on \(A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exists \(u_*\in A\) such that \(F(u_*)=\inf_{u\in A}F(u)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reflexive Orlicz–Sobolev extension permitting nonsmooth integrands and non-power growth.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Phi\) and \(\Phi^*\) satisfy \(\Delta_2\), so that \(W^{1,\Phi}(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)\) is reflexive. Let \(A\) be nonempty and weakly closed, and let \(f:\Omega\times\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb R^{m\times n}\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be a normal integrand, possibly nonsmooth, that is convex in its last variable. If
\[
F(u)=\int_\Omega f(x,u(x),\nabla u(x))\,dx
\]
is proper, sequentially weakly lower semicontinuous, and coercive in \(W^{1,\Phi}\) on \(A\), then there exists \(u_*\in A\) satisfying \(F(u_*)=\inf_{u\in A}F(u)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The direct method extends to reflexive Orlicz–Sobolev spaces for proper coercive weakly lower-semicontinuous integrals with nonsmooth generalized growth.
knowledge_statements.title: Generalized Tonelli–Morrey Regimes

knowledge_statements.title: Young-Measure Representation of Pure Oscillation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit bounded pure-oscillation family independent of the deferred gradient seed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix \(-1<\alpha<1\) and define
\[
A_\alpha:=\left\{z\in C([0,1]):\int_0^1z(x)\,dx=\alpha\right\},\qquad
J(z):=\int_0^1(z(x)^2-1)^2\,dx.
\]
Then \(\inf_{A_\alpha}J=0\), but the infimum is not attained. There are uniformly bounded minimizing sequences generating the homogeneous Young measure
\[
\frac{1+\alpha}{2}\delta_1+\frac{1-\alpha}{2}\delta_{-1},
\]
so the loss of attainment is purely oscillatory and has no concentration defect.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Continuous fields can mix the two preferred phases on finer scales and approach zero energy, although no continuous field with intermediate mean has zero energy.
assumptions_latex: The admissible fields are continuous and have prescribed mean \(\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \inf_{z\in A_\alpha}J(z)=0\quad\text{and}\quad\operatorname*{argmin}_{A_\alpha}J=\varnothing.

\[

\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
z_j\to z\ \text{in measure}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With concentration excluded, the Young measure is a point mass exactly when the sequence converges in measure.
assumptions_latex: \((z_j)\) is \(p\)-equiintegrable, converges weakly to \(z\), and generates \(\nu_x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \nu_x=\delta_{z(x)}\ \text{a.e.}\iff z_j\to z\ \text{in measure}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strong Relaxation by Shrinking Norm Neighborhoods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Metric-neighborhood and epigraph representations of the norm-lower-semicontinuous envelope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a normed space \(X\) and \(F:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), allowing the relaxed value to be \(-\infty\) when \(F\) is locally unbounded below,
\[\overline F^{\mathrm s}(x)=\sup_{\varepsilon>0}\inf_{\|y-x\|<\varepsilon}F(y)=\lim_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}\inf_{\|y-x\|<\varepsilon}F(y).\]
Equivalently,
\[\operatorname{epi}\overline F^{\mathrm s}=\overline{\operatorname{epi}F}\subset X\times\mathbb R.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong relaxation is obtained from infima on shrinking norm balls; equivalently, its epigraph is the closure of the original epigraph.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \overline F^{\mathrm s}(x)=\sup_{\varepsilon>0}\inf_{\|y-x\|<\varepsilon}F(y).
knowledge_statements.title: Strong Relaxation by Shrinking Norm Neighborhoods

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The functional \(\overline F^{\mathrm s}\) is the sequential norm-lower-semicontinuous envelope of \(F\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential relaxation for the norm topology of a Banach space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(x\in X\), the strong-topology relaxation of \(F\) is defined by \[\overline F^{\mathrm s}(x):=\inf\left\{\liminf_{n\to\infty}F(x_n):x_n\to x\text{ in norm}\right\}.\] It is the greatest sequentially norm-lower-semicontinuous functional not exceeding \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong relaxation assigns each point the least limiting energy obtainable along norm-convergent sequences. It is the largest sequentially norm-lower-semicontinuous minorant of the original functional.
knowledge_statements.title: Strong-Topology Relaxation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: The extraction evidently intends the final convergence to involve \(f_\rho^{**}\); this corrects the duplicated limit expression in the extracted sentence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \((H_1)\) or \((H_\infty)\), and for \(\rho>0\) define \(f_\rho(x,\xi)=f(x,\xi)\) when \(|\xi|\le\rho\) and \(f_\rho(x,\xi)=+\infty\) when \(|\xi|>\rho\). As \(\rho\to\infty\), for every fixed \(x\in\Omega\), \(f_\rho^{**}(x;\cdot)\) is continuous on its effective domain and converges to \(f^{**}(x;\cdot)\) uniformly on every compact subset. Moreover, for every \(\xi\in\mathbb R^n\), \(f_\rho^{**}(\cdot;\xi)\to f^{**}(\cdot;\xi)\) in \(L^1(\Omega)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under either stated integrand regime, biconjugating radial truncations produces convexified integrands that are continuous on their effective domains, converge locally uniformly in the gradient variable, and converge in L1 in the spatial variable at each fixed gradient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f_\rho^{**}(x;\cdot)\to f^{**}(x;\cdot)\text{ uniformly on compact subsets for each }x,\quad f_\rho^{**}(\cdot;\xi)\to f^{**}(\cdot;\xi)\text{ in }L^1(\Omega)\text{ for each }\xi.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sequential Representation on Weakly Metrizable Localizations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A precise regime in which relative weak relaxation is represented by weakly convergent sequences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\subset X\) carry a metrizable relative weak topology and let \(F_K:=F|_K\). For every \(x\in K\), the relative weak relaxation satisfies
\[\operatorname{cl}^{K}_wF_K(x)=\inf\left\{\liminf_{n\to\infty}F(x_n):x_n\in K,\ x_n\rightharpoonup x\right\}.\]
Thus the sequential and neighborhood formulas agree on weakly compact metrizable localizations, such as weakly compact subsets of a separable reflexive Banach space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a weakly metrizable localization, weak sequences fully represent the relative topological weak relaxation.
assumptions_latex: K\subset X\text{ has a metrizable relative weak topology}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{cl}^{K}_wF_K(x)=\inf_{\substack{x_n\in K\\x_n\rightharpoonup x}}\liminf_nF(x_n).

notation.meaning: Lower-semicontinuous envelope for the relative weak topology on \(K\)

knowledge_statements.title: Sequential Representation on Weakly Metrizable Localizations

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak-topology relaxation defined without assuming sequentiality or first countability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a Banach space \(X\), let \(\mathcal N_w(x)\) be the weak neighborhoods of \(x\). The topological weak relaxation is
\[\operatorname{cl}_wF(x):=\sup_{U\in\mathcal N_w(x)}\inf_{y\in U}F(y).\]
It is the greatest weakly lower-semicontinuous minorant of \(F\). On a nonsequential weak topology, this definition need not be represented by one application of an infimum over weakly convergent sequences.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The topology-correct weak relaxation is obtained from weak neighborhoods and is the greatest weakly lower-semicontinuous minorant.
assumptions_latex: X\text{ is a Banach space with its weak topology}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{cl}_wF(x)=\sup_{U\in\mathcal N_w(x)}\inf_{y\in U}F(y).
knowledge_statements.title: Topological Weak Lower-Semicontinuous Envelope

knowledge_statements.statement_title: One-Step Sequential Regularization Requires a Sequentiality Hypothesis
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limitation of identifying an unrestricted weak-sequence formula with the weak lower-semicontinuous envelope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define
\[F_1(x):=\inf\{\liminf_nF(x_n):x_n\rightharpoonup x\}.\]
Without a suitable sequentiality or metrizability hypothesis on the relevant weak topology, one cannot in general identify \(F_1\) with the topological weak lower-semicontinuous envelope or assert that one application of this operation produces the greatest sequentially weakly lower-semicontinuous minorant. A metrizable localization or an appropriate iterated sequential-closure construction is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On nonsequential weak topologies, a one-step infimum over weakly convergent sequences is not automatically the weak lower-semicontinuous envelope.
assumptions_latex: X\text{ carries a weak topology for which no sequentiality or metrizability hypothesis is imposed}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F_1\text{ cannot generally be identified with }\operatorname{cl}_wF\text{ without additional hypotheses}.
knowledge_statements.title: One-Step Sequential Regularization Requires a Sequentiality Hypothesis

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The functional \(\overline F^{\mathrm w}\) is the greatest sequentially weakly lower-semicontinuous functional satisfying \(\overline F^{\mathrm w}\le F\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential relaxation for the weak topology of a Banach space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The weak-topology relaxation of \(F\) is its sequential weakly lower-semicontinuous envelope, defined for every \(x\in X\) by \[\overline F^{\mathrm w}(x):=\inf\left\{\liminf_{n\to\infty}F(x_n):x_n\rightharpoonup x\right\}.\] Constant sequences give \(\overline F^{\mathrm w}\le F\). The envelope is sequentially weakly lower semicontinuous and dominates every sequentially weakly lower-semicontinuous functional \(G\) with \(G\le F\). A weakly convergent sequence whose energies approach the envelope value is a weak recovery sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weak relaxation assigns each point the least limiting energy achievable along weakly convergent sequences and is the largest weakly lower-semicontinuous minorant.
knowledge_statements.title: Weak-Topology Relaxation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind and local topic are appropriate, but the claimed identification of the one-step infimum-over-sequences formula with the greatest sequentially weakly lower-semicontinuous minorant needs a source or additional topological hypotheses. Weak topologies need not be first countable or sequential, so the usual metric diagonal argument is unavailable in this generality.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Weak Recovery Sequence with Energy and Gauge-Integral Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak recovery of a relaxed control with simultaneous convergence of the original energy and the auxiliary gauge integral.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: With \(\bar u,\bar p\), the measurable representation \((\bar f_i,\bar q_i)_{i=1}^{m+1}\), and \(\psi\) as fixed in the relaxation construction, there exists a sequence \(p_n\in L_m^1\) such that \(p_n\to\bar p\) in \(\sigma(L^1,L^\infty)\), \(\int_\Omega f(x,\bar u(x),p_n(x))\,dx\to\int_\Omega f^{**}(x,\bar u(x);\bar p(x))\,dx\), and \(\int_\Omega\psi(g(x,p_n(x)))\,dx\to\int_\Omega\sum_{i=1}^{m+1}\bar f_i(x)\psi(g(x,\bar q_i(x)))\,dx\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the data fixed by the preceding relaxation construction, there is a sequence of controls converging weakly to the relaxed control whose original energies converge to the biconjugate energy and whose gauge integrals converge to the corresponding finite-mixture value.
assumptions_latex: \bar u,\bar p,(\bar f_i,\bar q_i)_{i=1}^{m+1},\psi\text{ are the data fixed in the preceding relaxation construction.}

children.title: Relaxation Topology Comparison
children.top_down_role: Comparison of envelopes generated by different convergence topologies.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Topology-general comparison independent of sequentiality assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\tau_s\) be finer than \(\tau_w\) on \(X\), and let \(\operatorname{cl}_{\tau}F\) denote the greatest \(\tau\)-lower-semicontinuous minorant of \(F\). Then
\[\operatorname{cl}_{\tau_w}F\le \operatorname{cl}_{\tau_s}F\le F.\]
Moreover,
\[\operatorname{cl}_{\tau_w}F=\operatorname{cl}_{\tau_s}F\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \operatorname{cl}_{\tau_s}F\text{ is }\tau_w\text{-lower semicontinuous}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coarser topology yields a no-larger relaxed envelope; equality holds exactly when the finer-topology envelope is already lower semicontinuous for the coarser topology.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{cl}_{\tau_w}F\le\operatorname{cl}_{\tau_s}F\le F,\qquad \operatorname{cl}_{\tau_w}F=\operatorname{cl}_{\tau_s}F\Longleftrightarrow\operatorname{cl}_{\tau_s}F\text{ is }\tau_w\text{-lsc}.
knowledge_statements.title: Envelope Ordering for Nested Topologies

assumptions_latex: \(\overline F^{\mathrm s}\) and \(\overline F^{\mathrm w}\) denote the sequential strong and weak relaxations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(x\in X\), \(\overline F^{\mathrm w}(x)\le\overline F^{\mathrm s}(x)\le F(x)\).
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise ordering of sequential envelopes induced by topology strength.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Norm convergence implies weak convergence, so every sequence admissible in the definition of \(\overline F^{\mathrm s}(x)\) is admissible in the definition of \(\overline F^{\mathrm w}(x)\). Therefore \[\overline F^{\mathrm w}(x)\le\overline F^{\mathrm s}(x)\le F(x)\qquad(x\in X).\] Equality \(\overline F^{\mathrm w}=\overline F^{\mathrm s}\) holds whenever the strong relaxation is sequentially weakly lower semicontinuous. In particular, if \(F\) itself is sequentially weakly lower semicontinuous, then both relaxations equal \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Because norm convergence is stronger than weak convergence, weak relaxation can only lower energy further. The two envelopes coincide when the strong envelope is weakly lower semicontinuous.
knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation Topology Comparison

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The pointwise ordering is correct for the displayed sequence-based strong and weak relaxation formulas and the property role fits the comparison leaf. However, the record depends on the unresolved claim that the weak formula is the sequential weakly lower-semicontinuous envelope on every Banach space, and it cites no source establishing the intended convention or hypotheses.

children.title: Topology-Dependent Relaxation Gaps
children.top_down_role: Differences between relaxed values caused by topology choice.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: No-Gap Criterion by Weak Lower Semicontinuity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural sufficient condition excluding topology-dependent relaxation gaps under the sequential convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[\overline F^{\mathrm s}(x)=\inf_{x_n\to x}\liminf_nF(x_n),\qquad \overline F^{\mathrm w}(x)=\inf_{x_n\rightharpoonup x}\liminf_nF(x_n).\]
If \(\overline F^{\mathrm s}\) is sequentially weakly lower semicontinuous, then
\[\overline F^{\mathrm w}=\overline F^{\mathrm s}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sequential weak lower semicontinuity of the strong envelope rules out every strong–weak relaxation gap under the common sequential convention.
assumptions_latex: \overline F^{\mathrm s}\text{ is sequentially weakly lower semicontinuous}.
\overline F^{\mathrm s}\text{ and }\overline F^{\mathrm w}\text{ use the displayed sequential convention}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \overline F^{\mathrm w}=\overline F^{\mathrm s}.
knowledge_statements.title: No-Gap Criterion by Weak Lower Semicontinuity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Oscillatory Integral Producing a Strict Strong–Weak Gap
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete integral-functional separation on an infinite-dimensional Lebesgue space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X=L^4(0,1)\) and
\[F(u)=\int_0^1(u(t)^2-1)^2\,dt.\]
At \(u=0\), norm continuity gives \(\overline F^{\mathrm s}(0)=F(0)=1\). If \((r_n)\) is the Rademacher sequence, then \(|r_n|=1\), \(r_n\rightharpoonup0\) in \(L^4(0,1)\), and \(F(r_n)=0\). Since \(F\ge0\),
\[\overline F^{\mathrm w}(0)=0<1=\overline F^{\mathrm s}(0).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rapid ±1 oscillations converge weakly to zero with zero energy, whereas strong convergence to zero preserves energy one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \overline F^{\mathrm w}(0)=0<1=\overline F^{\mathrm s}(0).
knowledge_statements.title: Oscillatory Integral Producing a Strict Strong–Weak Gap

assumptions_latex: Both relaxation values are finite at the point under consideration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The topology-dependent gap \(\Delta(x):=\overline F^{\mathrm s}(x)-\overline F^{\mathrm w}(x)\) is nonnegative, and \(\Delta(x)>0\) exactly when weakly convergent sequences achieve a strictly smaller limiting energy than norm-convergent sequences.
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-valued pointwise gap between sequential strong and weak envelopes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[\Delta(x):=\overline F^{\mathrm s}(x)-\overline F^{\mathrm w}(x).\] The topology comparison gives \(\Delta(x)\ge0\). A strict topology-dependent relaxation gap occurs at \(x\) when \(\Delta(x)>0\). Equivalently, there is an energy level below \(\overline F^{\mathrm s}(x)\) approachable by a sequence converging weakly to \(x\), while no sequence converging strongly to \(x\) has a liminf energy below that level. Thus the additional weakly convergent microstructures or concentrations change the relaxed value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The weak envelope never exceeds the strong envelope. A positive difference records limiting structures visible under weak convergence but unavailable under norm convergence.
knowledge_statements.title: Topology-Dependent Relaxation Gaps

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The nonnegative pointwise difference fits the failure-boundary leaf, but the asserted equivalence between a positive difference and energy achieved by weak sequences requires precise interpretation of 'achieve' as an infimum of liminf values. It also depends on the unresolved weak-envelope convention and has no supporting citation.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the sequence-based relaxation \(\overline F\), \[\inf_{x\in X}\overline F(x)=\inf_{x\in X}F(x).\] Thus relaxation preserves the optimal value even when it changes the points at which that value is attained.

children.top_down_role: Existence of minimizers within enlarged or completed admissible classes.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a reflexive Banach space and \(\overline F:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper and sequentially weakly lower semicontinuous.
There exists \(c>\inf_{x\in X}\overline F(x)\) such that the nonempty sublevel set \(\{x\in X:\overline F(x)\le c\}\) is bounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exists \(\bar x\in X\) such that \(\overline F(\bar x)=\min_{x\in X}\overline F(x)\).

notation.meaning: A minimizer of the relaxed functional

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential weak direct-method attainment theorem on a reflexive Banach space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be reflexive and let \(\overline F\) be proper and sequentially weakly lower semicontinuous. If a nonempty sublevel set strictly above \(\inf_{x\in X}\overline F(x)\) is bounded, then there exists \(\bar x\in X\) such that \[\overline F(\bar x)=\min_{x\in X}\overline F(x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proper sequentially weakly lower-semicontinuous relaxed functional attains its infimum when a near-minimal sublevel is bounded in a reflexive Banach space.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Representation and density minimizer for the relaxed local energy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded characterization of the local relaxed density in the elastic shape problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The relaxed local energy satisfies \[g(\tau,\theta)=B^{-1}\tau:\tau+\frac{\theta}{1-\theta}g^*(\tau),\] where \(g^*\) is continuous, convex, positively homogeneous of degree two, and \(g^*(\tau)>0\) for \(\tau\ne0\). Thus \(g\colon(\tau,\theta)\mapsto\mathbb R_+\cup\{+\infty\}\) is continuous and separately strictly convex in \(\tau\) and \(\theta\). For each \(\tau\in\mathcal M_N^s\), the density subproblem has the unique solution \[\theta_\tau=\max\left\{0,1-\sqrt{\frac{g^*(\tau)}{-\ell}}\right\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The relaxed local energy splits into an elastic quadratic term and a density-weighted convex two-homogeneous stress term. It is separately strictly convex, and for each stress tensor its density minimizer is given explicitly by the stated threshold formula.
assumptions_latex: \(g^*\) is the stress-only function occurring in the relaxed formulation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: g(\tau,\theta)=B^{-1}\tau:\tau+\frac{\theta}{1-\theta}g^*(\tau),\qquad \operatorname*{argmin}_{\theta}g(\tau,\theta)=\left\{\max\left(0,1-\sqrt{g^*(\tau)/(-\ell)}\right)\right\}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Existence of a relaxed minimizer and sufficient conditions for no relaxation gap
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relaxed trajectory optimization with state constraints, endpoint constraints, and endpoint cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider the trajectory problem determined by $\Omega,F,X,C,$ and $g$. Assume: (i) $F$ is compact-valued and $\mathcal L\times\mathcal B^n$-measurable; (ii) for every $t\in[S,T]$, the graph of $F(t,\cdot)|_{X(t)}$ is closed; (iii) there exist $\alpha,\beta\in L^1([S,T])$ such that
\[
F(t,x)\subseteq(\alpha(t)|x|+\beta(t))B\quad\text{for all }(t,x)\in\operatorname{Gr}X;
\]
(iv) either $X(s)$ is bounded for some $s\in[S,T]$, or at least one endpoint projection
\[
C_0:=\{x_0:\exists x_1,
0(x_0,x_1)\in C\},\qquad C_1:=\{x_1:\exists x_0,
0(x_0,x_1)\in C\}
\]
is bounded; and the feasible ordinary-trajectory set $\mathcal R_F(X,C)$ is nonempty. Then the relaxed problem has a minimizer.

If additionally (a) some $k\in L^1([S,T])$ satisfies
\[
F(t,x)\subseteq F(t,x')+k(t)|x-x'|B\quad\text{for all }(t,x),(t,x')\in\Omega,
\]
(b) $g$ is continuous, and for some relaxed minimizer $\bar x$ and $\epsilon>0$, (c)
\[
\bar x(t)+\epsilon B\subseteq X(t)\quad\text{for all }t\in[S,T],
\]
and (d) either
\[
(\bar x(S)+\epsilon B)\times\{\bar x(T)\}\subseteq C
\]
or
\[
\{\bar x(S)\}\times(\bar x(T)+\epsilon B)\subseteq C,
\]
then
\[
\inf(P)_{\mathrm{relaxed}}=\inf(P).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compact-valued measurability, closed restricted graphs, integrable linear growth, a boundedness condition, and nonempty ordinary feasibility guarantee existence of a relaxed minimizer. If F is also integrably Lipschitz in the state, the cost is continuous, and a relaxed minimizer has uniform interior room in the state constraints and at one endpoint component of the endpoint constraint, then the relaxed and ordinary problems have equal infimum costs.
assumptions_latex: F\text{ is compact-valued and }\mathcal L\times\mathcal B^n\text{-measurable}
(\exists s\in[S,T]:X(s)\text{ is bounded})\ \lor\ C_0\text{ is bounded}\ \lor\ C_1\text{ is bounded}
\text{For the no-gap conclusion: }\exists k\in L^1\ \forall(t,x),(t,x')\in\Omega:\ F(t,x)\subseteq F(t,x')+k(t)|x-x'|B
\exists\bar x\text{ a relaxed minimizer},\ \exists\epsilon>0:\ \forall t,\ \bar x(t)+\epsilon B\subseteq X(t)
(\bar x(S)+\epsilon B)\times\{\bar x(T)\}\subseteq C\ \lor\ \{\bar x(S)\}\times(\bar x(T)+\epsilon B)\subseteq C
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (P)_{\mathrm{relaxed}}\text{ has a minimizer};\quad\text{under the additional assumptions, }\inf(P)_{\mathrm{relaxed}}=\inf(P)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quasiconvex relaxation of the stress-based optimal-shape problem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded relaxation theorem in the notation of the stress formulation and its relaxed problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The relaxed integrand is the quasiconvexification: \(QF\) is the quasiconvexification of \(F\). The relaxed problem admits a minimizer in \(\Sigma(\Omega)\); every minimizing sequence for the original problem has a subsequence converging weakly in \(L^2(\Omega;\mathcal M_N^s)\) to a relaxed minimizer; and every relaxed minimizer \(\tau\) is the weak \(L^2\)-limit of a minimizing sequence for the original problem. Moreover, \[\inf_{\tau\in\Sigma(\Omega)}\int_\Omega F(\tau)\,dx=\min_{\tau\in\Sigma(\Omega)}\int_\Omega QF(\tau)\,dx.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The quasiconvexified stress problem has a minimizer. Original minimizing sequences are weakly precompact toward relaxed minimizers, every relaxed minimizer has an original recovery sequence, and the original infimum equals the relaxed minimum.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) and \(QF\) are the integrands of the stated original and relaxed stress formulations over \(\Sigma(\Omega)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: QF=F^{qc},\quad \operatorname*{argmin}_{\Sigma(\Omega)}\int_\Omega QF\,dx\neq\varnothing,\quad \inf\int_\Omega F\,dx=\min\int_\Omega QF\,dx,\quad\text{with weak compactness and recovery in }L^2.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quasiconvex relaxation of the multiple-load stress problem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded relaxation theorem for finitely many load-associated stress fields.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the \(n\)-load stress problem, the quasiconvexified formulation is its relaxation: the relaxed problem has a minimizer in \(\Sigma^n(\Omega)\); every original minimizing sequence has a subsequence converging weakly in \(L^2(\Omega;\mathcal M_N^s)^n\) to a relaxed minimizer; and every relaxed minimizer \(\{\tau_i\}_{i=1}^n\) is the weak limit of an original minimizing sequence. Moreover, \[\inf_{\{\tau_i\}\in\Sigma^n(\Omega)}\int_\Omega F^n(\{\tau_i\})\,dx=\min_{\{\tau_i\}\in\Sigma^n(\Omega)}\int_\Omega QF^n(\{\tau_i\})\,dx.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For finitely many loads, the quasiconvexified stress problem attains its minimum, original minimizing sequences converge subsequentially to relaxed minimizers, every relaxed minimizer has a recovery sequence, and the original infimum equals the relaxed minimum.
assumptions_latex: \(F^n\) and \(QF^n\) are respectively the original and quasiconvexified multiple-load integrands.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname*{argmin}_{\Sigma^n(\Omega)}\int_\Omega QF^n\,dx\neq\varnothing,\quad \inf\int_\Omega F^n\,dx=\min\int_\Omega QF^n\,dx,\quad\text{with weak compactness and recovery in }L^2(\Omega;\mathcal M_N^s)^n.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Monotonicity and limiting behavior of the optimal-volume map
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded parameter-dependence property for possibly nonunique relaxed minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\ell\in\mathbb R^-\), let \[\Theta(\ell)=\int_\Omega(1-\theta_\ell)\,dx,\] where \(\theta_\ell\) is the optimal density associated with any possibly nonunique minimizer \(\tau_\ell\) of the relaxed problem; hence \(\Theta\) may be multivalued. Then \(\Theta\) is increasing in \(\ell\). If the surface load admits at least one admissible field \(\sigma\in\Sigma(\Omega)\) that is uniformly bounded on \(\Omega\), then \(\Theta(\ell)\to0\) as \(\ell\to-\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The material-deficit volume associated with relaxed optima increases with the negative parameter. Under existence of a uniformly bounded admissible stress field, it tends to zero as the parameter tends to minus infinity.
assumptions_latex: \(\theta_\ell\) is associated with an arbitrary minimizer \(\tau_\ell\) of the relaxed problem.
For the limiting assertion, \(\exists\sigma\in\Sigma(\Omega)\) uniformly bounded in \(\Omega\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \ell_1\le\ell_2\Longrightarrow \Theta(\ell_1)\le\Theta(\ell_2),\qquad \left[\exists\sigma\in\Sigma(\Omega)\cap L^\infty(\Omega)\right]\Longrightarrow\lim_{\ell\to-\infty}\Theta(\ell)=0.
