children.top_down_role: Minimizing objects admitted by relaxed formulations.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a metrizable topological space, \(F:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), and \(\overline F(x)=\inf\{\liminf_{n\to\infty}F(x_n):x_n\to x\}\).
The relaxed functional attains its minimum at \(\bar x\), and \(\inf_{x\in X}\overline F(x)=\inf_{x\in X}F(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A generalized minimizer is represented by the relaxed minimizer \(\bar x\) together with a recovery sequence \((x_n)\) satisfying \(x_n\to\bar x\) and \(F(x_n)\to\overline F(\bar x)\).

notation.meaning: Recovery sequence representing the generalized state

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition of a generalized minimizer as a relaxed minimizer represented by an original recovery sequence in a metrizable relaxation topology.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A generalized minimizer of \(F\) is represented by a point \(\bar x\in X\) satisfying \[\overline F(\bar x)=\min_{x\in X}\overline F(x)=\inf_{x\in X}F(x)\] and a recovery sequence \((x_n)\subset X\) satisfying \[x_n\to\bar x,\qquad F(x_n)\to\overline F(\bar x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A generalized minimizer consists of a relaxed minimizing state and a sequence of original states converging to it whose energies approach the relaxed minimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Generalized Minimizers

children.title: Relaxed Attainment Gaps
children.top_down_role: Residual failures of attainment or representation after relaxation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elementary example realizing a pointwise mismatch at every relaxed minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(X=\mathbb R\), define \[F(x)=\begin{cases}|x|,&x\ne0,\\1,&x=0.\end{cases}\] Its lower-semicontinuous relaxation is \(\overline F(x)=|x|\). Thus \(\inf F=0=\min\overline F\), the unique relaxed minimizer is \(0\), and \(F(0)=1>0=\overline F(0)\); consequently \(F\) does not attain its infimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Changing the value of the absolute-value function at zero from zero to one produces equal infima but only the relaxed functional attains the value.
assumptions_latex: \(X=\mathbb R\) has its usual topology and relaxation means the lower-semicontinuous envelope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\(\inf_XF=
ewcommand{\minrel}{\min_X\overline F}\minrel=0\), while \(\operatorname{argmin}F=\varnothing\) and \(\operatorname{argmin}\overline F=\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.title: Relaxed Attainment without Original Attainment

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Criterion for Original Nonattainment after Relaxation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact boundary between relaxed attainment and attainment by an original state when optimal values agree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\overline F\le F\) be a relaxation satisfying \(\inf_XF=\min_X\overline F=:m\), and set \(M_{\mathrm{rel}}:=\{x:\overline F(x)=m\}\). Then \[\operatorname{argmin}_X F\ne\varnothing\iff\exists x\in M_{\mathrm{rel}}\text{ such that }F(x)=\overline F(x).\] Hence the original problem is unattained exactly when \(F(x)>\overline F(x)\) for every \(x\in M_{\mathrm{rel}}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the relaxed and original optimal values agree, the original problem attains its infimum exactly when some relaxed minimizer has no pointwise relaxation mismatch.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{argmin}_X F\ne\varnothing\iff\exists x\in\operatorname{argmin}_X\overline F\text{ with }F(x)=\overline F(x)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Criterion for Original Nonattainment after Relaxation

assumptions_latex: \(F:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is bounded below, \(\overline F\) is its sequential relaxation, and \(\inf_{x\in X}\overline F(x)=\inf_{x\in X}F(x)\).
The relaxed functional has a minimizer \(\bar x\), and both \(F(\bar x)\) and \(\overline F(\bar x)\) are defined as extended-real values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A pointwise relaxed-attainment mismatch at \(\bar x\) occurs when \(\overline F(\bar x)=\inf_{x\in X}F(x)\) and \(F(\bar x)>\overline F(\bar x)\), including \(F(\bar x)=+\infty\).

notation.meaning: A minimizer of the relaxed functional
Pointwise relaxed-attainment gap when the difference is well defined

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise mismatch between relaxed attainment and the original energy at the same relaxed minimizing state; it does not by itself assert global nonattainment of the original problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A pointwise relaxed-attainment mismatch occurs at a relaxed minimizer \(\bar x\) when \[\overline F(\bar x)=\inf_{x\in X}F(x)\quad\text{and}\quad F(\bar x)>\overline F(\bar x).\] When the extended-real difference is well defined, it may be denoted by \[g(\bar x):=F(\bar x)-\overline F(\bar x).\] The case \(F(\bar x)=+\infty\) represents a relaxed minimizer outside the effective domain of the original functional.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pointwise relaxed-attainment mismatch occurs when a relaxed minimizer has the preserved optimal value but its original energy at that same state is larger or infinite. This alone does not rule out an original minimizer elsewhere.
knowledge_statements.title: Relaxed Attainment Gaps

children.title: Recovery-Sequence Methods
children.top_down_role: Approximation families realizing relaxed energies.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a metrizable topological space and \(F:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\).
\(\overline F\) is the sequential lower-semicontinuous envelope of \(F\): \(\overline F(x)=\inf\{\liminf_{j\to\infty}F(x_j):x_j\to x\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(x\in X\) with \(\overline F(x)<+\infty\), a recovery sequence realizes the relaxed value asymptotically.

notation.meaning: Original functional and its sequential relaxation
Recovery sequence converging to the prescribed state

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard recovery-sequence characterization of sequential relaxation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential recovery in the topology used to define relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A sequence \((x_j)_j\subset X\) is a recovery sequence for \(x\in X\) if \(x_j\to x\) and \(\limsup_{j\to\infty}F(x_j)\leq \overline F(x)\). Since the definition of \(\overline F\) gives \(\overline F(x)\leq\liminf_{j\to\infty}F(x_j)\), every recovery sequence satisfies \[\lim_{j\to\infty}F(x_j)=\overline F(x).\] The recovery-sequence method consists in constructing such a sequence for every \(x\) having finite relaxed energy; together with the corresponding lower-bound inequality, this identifies \(\overline F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A recovery sequence converges to a target state while its original energies converge to the relaxed energy, thereby furnishing the upper-bound half of a relaxation result.
knowledge_statements.title: Recovery-Sequence Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The recovery-sequence principle is mathematically standard and fits the terminal container, but no inspectable source with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Convex-Envelope Relaxation
children.top_down_role: Envelope regimes for state-dependent and scalar-gradient nonconvexity.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise convexification in a finite-dimensional gradient space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f:\mathbb R^d\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) bounded below and not identically \(+\infty\), \[Cf(\xi)=\inf\left\{\sum_{i=1}^{N}\lambda_i f(\xi_i):N<\infty,\ \lambda_i\geq0,\ \sum_i\lambda_i=1,\ \sum_i\lambda_i\xi_i=\xi\right\}.\] The lower-semicontinuous convex envelope is \(f^{**}=\operatorname{cl}Cf\); hence \(Cf=f^{**}\) whenever \(Cf\) is lower semicontinuous.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convexification minimizes energy over finite mixtures with prescribed barycenter, while biconjugation also takes lower-semicontinuous closure.
assumptions_latex: The gradient variable lies in \(\mathbb R^d\).
\(f\) is bounded below and not identically infinite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Cf\) has the finite-mixture formula and \(f^{**}=\operatorname{cl}Cf\).
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Mixture and Biconjugate Representations

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar-valued first-order energies with autonomous finite density.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(1<p<\infty\), let \(u:\Omega\to\mathbb R\), and let \(I(u)=\int_\Omega f(\nabla u)\,dx\), where \(f:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) is continuous with standard \(p\)-growth and coercivity. Then \(I\) is sequentially weakly lower semicontinuous on \(W^{1,p}\) exactly when \(f\) is convex, and its sequential weak relaxation is \(\overline I(u)=\int_\Omega f^{**}(\nabla u)\,dx\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For autonomous scalar-gradient energies, convexity is the weak lower-semicontinuity condition and biconjugate convexification gives relaxation.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is finite and continuous with standard \(p\)-growth and coercivity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(I\text{ is weakly l.s.c.}\iff f\text{ is convex},\qquad \overline I(u)=\int_\Omega f^{**}(\nabla u)\,dx.\)
knowledge_statements.title: Autonomous Scalar-Gradient Relaxation

assumptions_latex: \(\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d\) is bounded and open, \(1<p<\infty\), and \(u\in W^{1,p}(\Omega)\).
\(f:\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^d\to[0,+\infty)\) is continuous and satisfies standard \(p\)-growth and coercivity bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The weakly lower-semicontinuous relaxation is obtained by convexifying the scalar gradient variable.

notation.meaning: Lower-semicontinuous convex envelope in the gradient variable

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: scalar-gradient relaxation by convexification under standard growth hypotheses
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar-valued Sobolev maps; convexification acts only on the gradient variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(I(u)=\int_\Omega f(u(x),\nabla u(x))\,dx\). Under hypotheses ensuring locality and excluding additional relaxation in the state variable, the sequential weak-\(W^{1,p}\) lower-semicontinuous envelope is \[\overline I(u)=\int_\Omega f^{**}(u(x),\nabla u(x))\,dx,\] where \[f^{**}(s,\xi)=\sup\{a\cdot\xi+b:a\cdot\eta+b\leq f(s,\eta)\text{ for every }\eta\in\mathbb R^d\}.\] Thus \(f^{**}(s,\cdot)\) is the greatest lower-semicontinuous convex function bounded above by \(f(s,\cdot)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For scalar Sobolev maps, relaxation replaces a nonconvex gradient density by its lower-semicontinuous convex envelope, subject to suitable growth and state-dependence assumptions.
knowledge_statements.title: Convex-Envelope Relaxation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits scalar-gradient relaxation, but continuity and generic p-growth alone do not establish the stated state-dependent formula. A source must specify hypotheses preventing additional relaxation in the state variable.

children.title: Quasiconvex-Envelope Relaxation
children.top_down_role: Relaxation of vectorial gradient energies.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Genuinely vectorial matrix spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Every finite quasiconvex density is rank-one convex, but the converse fails in general: finite rank-one convex functions on \(\mathbb R^{3\times2}\) exist that are not quasiconvex. Thus replacing \(Qf\) by \(Rf\) is not an exact vectorial relaxation rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rank-one convexity is necessary but not sufficient for vectorial weak lower semicontinuity.
assumptions_latex: The matrix space is genuinely vectorial; a classical counterexample exists in \(\mathbb R^{3\times2}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{quasiconvex}\Rightarrow\text{rank-one convex}\), but the converse is false in general.
knowledge_statements.title: Rank-One Convexity Is Not Sufficient

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Autonomous vectorial first-order integral energies in the reflexive Sobolev regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(1<p<\infty\), let \(\Omega\) be bounded and Lipschitz, and let \(f:\mathbb R^{m\times d}\to\mathbb R\) be continuous with standard \(p\)-growth and coercivity. Then \(I(u)=\int_\Omega f(\nabla u)\,dx\) is sequentially weakly lower semicontinuous on \(W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)\) if and only if \(f\) is quasiconvex: for every \(A\), bounded Lipschitz test domain \(D\), and \(\varphi\in W^{1,\infty}_0(D;\mathbb R^m)\), \[f(A)\leq |D|^{-1}\int_D f(A+\nabla\varphi)\,dx.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Morrey quasiconvexity is the exact weak lower-semicontinuity condition for standard autonomous vectorial gradient energies.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is finite and continuous with standard \(p\)-growth and coercivity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(I\text{ is sequentially weakly l.s.c.}\iff f\text{ is quasiconvex}.\)
knowledge_statements.title: Morrey Quasiconvexity Criterion

For \(I(u)=\int_\Omega f(
abla u(x))\,dx\), its sequential weak-\(W^{1,p}\) lower-semicontinuous envelope is \[\overline I(u)=\int_\Omega Qf(

children.title: Rank-One Convex Envelopes
children.top_down_role: Envelope constructions based on rank-one convexity.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Affine Covariance of the Rank-One Convex Envelope
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility of the envelope with positive scaling and affine perturbations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(a>0\) and \(\ell(A)=\langle C,A\rangle+c\) is affine, then
\[R(af+\ell)=aRf+\ell.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive rescaling and addition of an affine function commute with rank-one convexification.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R(af+\ell)=aRf+\ell.
knowledge_statements.title: Affine Covariance of the Rank-One Convex Envelope

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order-theoretic properties intrinsic to the rank-one convex-envelope operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For extended-real functions \(f,h\) admitting rank-one-convex minorants,
\[Rf\le f,\qquad f\le h\Rightarrow Rf\le Rh,\qquad R(Rf)=Rf.\]
Moreover, \(Rf=f\) if and only if \(f\) is rank-one convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rank-one convexification is order preserving and idempotent, lies below the original density, and fixes exactly the rank-one convex functions.
assumptions_latex: f,h:\mathbb R^{m\times d}\to(-\infty,+\infty]\text{ admit rank-one-convex minorants}.
f\le h\text{ for the monotonicity assertion}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Rf\le f,\quad f\le h\Rightarrow Rf\le Rh,\quad R^2f=Rf,\quad Rf=f\Longleftrightarrow f\text{ is rank-one convex}.
knowledge_statements.title: Rank-One Envelope Operator Laws

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^{m\times d}\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is bounded below by an affine function.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R f\) is the largest rank-one convex minorant of \(f\).

notation.meaning: Rank-one convex envelope of the density

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: order-theoretic definition of the rank-one convex envelope
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise envelope on finite-dimensional matrix space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A function \(g:\mathbb R^{m\times d}\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is rank-one convex if, whenever \(\operatorname{rank}(A-B)\leq1\), \[g(tA+(1-t)B)\leq t g(A)+(1-t)g(B)\qquad(0\leq t\leq1).\] The rank-one convex envelope of \(f\) is \[Rf(A)=\sup\{g(A):g\leq f\text{ and }g\text{ is rank-one convex}\}.\] Consequently, \(Rf\leq f\), \(Rf\) is rank-one convex when the supremum retains rank-one convexity, and every rank-one convex minorant \(g\) of \(f\) satisfies \(g\leq Rf\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The rank-one convex envelope is the greatest minorant convex along every affine line whose direction has rank at most one.
knowledge_statements.title: Rank-One Convex Envelopes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the exact leaf and is essentially standard, although the pointwise supremum of rank-one-convex minorants is itself rank-one convex, making the qualification about retaining convexity unnecessary. No inspectable citation is supplied.

children.title: Lamination Envelopes
children.top_down_role: Envelope constructions generated by laminate microstructures.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite iterated rank-one laminates, without closure by weak limits.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mu=\sum_{i=1}^N\lambda_i\delta_{A_i}\) be represented by a finite binary tree whose internal nodes are barycentric rank-one splits and whose root is \(A\). Then \(\mu\) is an admissible finite laminate with barycenter \(A\), and \[Lf(A)\leq\sum_{i=1}^N\lambda_i f(A_i).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite rank-one splitting tree certifies laminate admissibility and an upper bound on the envelope.
assumptions_latex: Every internal split joins rank-one-compatible children.
Leaf weights are nonnegative and sum to one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar\mu=A,\qquad Lf(A)\leq\int f\,d\mu.\)
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Laminate Upper Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A single compatible two-phase split.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(A=tB+(1-t)C\), \(t\in[0,1]\), and \(\operatorname{rank}(B-C)\leq1\), then \(t\delta_B+(1-t)\delta_C\) is a finite laminate with barycenter \(A\), and \(Lf(A)\leq t f(B)+(1-t)f(C)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A single rank-one split gives an admissible two-phase laminate and an explicit envelope upper bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Lf(A)\leq tf(B)+(1-t)f(C)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Elementary Rank-One Mixing Bound

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The lamination envelope is the infimum of averages of \(f\) over finite-order laminates with prescribed barycenter.

notation.meaning: Set of finite-order laminate probability measures

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: finite laminate representation of lamination relaxation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-order laminate convention; closure variants require separate specification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal L\) be the smallest class of finitely supported probability measures containing every Dirac mass and closed under replacing an atom \(\lambda\delta_A\) by \(\lambda[t\delta_B+(1-t)\delta_C]\) whenever \(A=tB+(1-t)C\) and \(\operatorname{rank}(B-C)\leq1\). The finite-lamination envelope is \[Lf(A)=\inf\left\{\int f(B)\,d\mu(B):\mu\in\mathcal L,\ \bar\mu=A\right\}.\] It records energies attainable by iterated rank-one splittings while preserving the macroscopic matrix \(A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The lamination envelope minimizes the average density over finite iterated rank-one splittings whose barycenter equals the prescribed macroscopic matrix.
knowledge_statements.title: Lamination Envelopes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-laminate representation fits the leaf, but the finite-order convention requires a source. The record also incorrectly lists its own node as a prerequisite.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Optimal Nonlocal Bounds for Two-Phase Effective Conductivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives universal upper and lower energy bounds over the homogenized-tensor class and identifies finite-rank sequential laminates as optimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every $\xi\in\mathcal M_N$ and every $A^*\in G_\theta$,
\[
A^*:\xi^t\xi\le B:\xi^t\xi+\theta\min_{\eta\in\mathcal M_N}\left[2\xi:\eta+(B-A)^{-1}:\eta^t\eta-(1-\theta)h(\eta)\right],
\]
where
\[
h(\eta)=\min_{k\in\mathbb Z^N,\,k\ne0}\frac{|\eta k|^2}{Bk\cdot k},
\]
and
\[
A^*:\xi^t\xi\ge A:\xi^t\xi+(1-\theta)\max_{\eta\in\mathcal M_N}\left[2\xi:\eta-(B-A)^{-1}:\eta^t\eta-\theta g(\eta)\right],
\]
where
\[
g(\eta)=\max_{k\in\mathbb Z^N,\,k\ne0}\frac{|\eta k|^2}{Ak\cdot k}.
\]
Both bounds are optimal pointwise in $\xi$, and equality can always be attained by a rank-$N$ sequential laminate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every effective conductivity tensor in G_theta satisfies the stated nonlocal upper and lower quadratic-energy bounds. Each bound is pointwise optimal for every test matrix xi, and a rank-N sequential laminate can attain it.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The displayed upper and lower bounds hold for every }A^*\in G_\theta;\text{ both are optimal, and each is attainable by a rank-}N\text{ sequential laminate.}

children.title: Finite-Order Lamination Hierarchy
children.top_down_role: Envelope levels indexed by finite lamination depth.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nested maximum-depth convention allowing unchanged branches.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[(Tg)(A)=\inf\{t g(B)+(1-t)g(C):t\in[0,1],\ A=tB+(1-t)C,\ \operatorname{rank}(B-C)\leq1\}.\] With \(L_0f=f\) and \(L_{k+1}f=T(L_kf)\), degenerate choices \(B=C=A\) give \(L_{k+1}f\leq L_kf\). Moreover, \(L_kf(A)\) is the infimum over rank-one binary splitting trees of depth at most \(k\) and barycenter \(A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each hierarchy level permits one additional binary rank-one mixing generation, with unchanged branches ensuring nestedness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_{k+1}f=T(L_kf)\leq L_kf\).
knowledge_statements.title: Recursive Rank-One Splitting Operator

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary-tree maximum-depth convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Every laminate produced by a binary splitting tree of depth at most \(k\) has at most \(2^k\) terminal atoms. Its labeled splitting tree is a finite certificate of order-\(k\) admissibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An order-k binary laminate uses at most 2^k phases, and its tree certifies admissibility.
assumptions_latex: Lamination order is maximum binary-tree depth.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|\operatorname{supp}\mu|\leq2^k\) for every order-\(k\) laminate \(\mu\).
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Depth Support Bound

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The envelopes decrease with lamination order and converge pointwise to the finite-lamination envelope.

notation.meaning: Laminates obtainable using at most k generations of rank-one splitting

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: monotone hierarchy generated by bounded-depth rank-one splitting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hierarchy indexed by the maximum number of successive splitting generations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Set \(\mathcal L_0(A)=\{\delta_A\}\), and obtain \(\mathcal L_{k+1}(A)\) from measures in \(\mathcal L_k(A)\) by one further generation of rank-one splittings, always preserving barycenter \(A\). Define \[L_kf(A)=\inf_{\mu\in\mathcal L_k(A)}\int f(B)\,d\mu(B).\] Then \[f(A)=L_0f(A)\geq L_1f(A)\geq L_2f(A)\geq\cdots,\qquad L_\infty f(A)=\inf_{k\geq0}L_kf(A).\] Thus increasing lamination order enlarges the admissible microstructures and cannot increase the envelope value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Allowing more generations of rank-one splitting yields a decreasing sequence of envelopes whose infimum is the finite-lamination envelope.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Order Lamination Hierarchy

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property fits the hierarchy leaf, but “one further generation” does not explicitly make the classes nested, which is needed for the monotonicity claim. The lamination-order convention needs a source.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence and inverse-tensor representation for a rank-p sequential laminate with matrix B and core A.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $(e_i)_{i=1}^p$ be unit vectors, let $\theta\in[0,1]$, and let $m_i\geq0$ satisfy $\sum_{i=1}^p m_i=1$. Then there exists a rank-$p$ sequential laminate $A_p^*$ with matrix $B$, core $A$, respective proportions $1-\theta$ and $\theta$, and lamination directions $(e_i)_{i=1}^p$, such that
\[
\theta(A_p^*-B)^{-1}=(A-B)^{-1}+(1-\theta)\sum_{i=1}^p m_i\frac{e_i\otimes e_i}{Be_i\cdot e_i}.
\]
The numbers $(m_i)_{i=1}^p$ are called the lamination parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Given unit lamination directions, a volume fraction, and nonnegative weights summing to one, there exists a rank-p sequential laminate with matrix B and core A satisfying the stated inverse effective-tensor formula. The weights are its lamination parameters.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists A_p^*:\quad \theta(A_p^*-B)^{-1}=(A-B)^{-1}+(1-\theta)\sum_{i=1}^p m_i\frac{e_i\otimes e_i}{Be_i\cdot e_i}.

children.title: Envelope Separation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Settings where rank-one and lamination envelopes differ.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strict separation in a genuinely vectorial matrix space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: There exists a finite rank-one convex function \(g:\mathbb R^{3\times2}\to\mathbb R\) that is not quasiconvex. Consequently, for some \(A\), \(Qg(A)<g(A)=Rg(A)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In 3-by-2 matrix space, the quasiconvex envelope can be strictly smaller than the rank-one convex envelope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists g,A:\ Qg(A)<Rg(A)=g(A)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Vectorial Rank-One–Quasiconvex Separation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matrix spaces in which every segment is rank-one.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(m=1\) or \(d=1\), every difference in \(\mathbb R^{m\times d}\) has rank at most one. Hence rank-one convexity equals convexity; for finite continuous densities under standard growth, quasiconvexity also equals convexity. Therefore \(Cf=Qf=Rf\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When either matrix dimension is one, convex, quasiconvex, and rank-one convex envelopes coincide.
assumptions_latex: For the quasiconvex equivalence, the density is finite and satisfies standard regularity and growth assumptions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Cf=Qf=Rf\).
knowledge_statements.title: Scalar and One-Dimensional Collapse

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite-Laminate Convention Collapses to the Rank-One Convex Envelope
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Clarifies the convention-sensitive relation between finite-lamination and rank-one convex envelopes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Lf(A)\) be the infimum of \(\int f\,d\mu\) over all finite iterated rank-one laminates with barycenter \(A\), and let \(Rf\) be the greatest rank-one convex minorant of \(f\). Under this finite-laminate convention, \(Lf=Rf\). Thus any claimed separation between these two symbols must use a different closure, order, or admissible-microstructure convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With all finite iterated rank-one splittings allowed, the lamination envelope equals the rank-one convex envelope; separation requires a different convention.
assumptions_latex: \(Lf\) ranges over all finite iterated rank-one laminates.
\(Rf\) is the greatest rank-one convex minorant of \(f\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Lf=Rf\).
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Laminate Convention Collapses to the Rank-One Convex Envelope

assumptions_latex: \(m,d\geq2\) and \(f:\mathbb R^{m\times d}\to\mathbb R\) is a finite density for which the indicated envelopes are defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Strict envelope gaps may occur in genuinely vectorial dimensions; scalar or one-dimensional settings collapse the convexity notions.

notation.meaning: Convex, quasiconvex, rank-one convex, and lamination envelopes

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: hierarchy follows from convexity implications and admissible microstructure classes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Qualitative boundary between scalar collapse and genuinely vectorial separation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Because every convex function is quasiconvex and every quasiconvex function is rank-one convex, the corresponding greatest-minorant envelopes satisfy \[Cf\leq Qf\leq Rf\leq f.\] A finite-lamination envelope based only on iterated rank-one splittings need not equal \(Qf\), and strict gaps between envelope levels can occur when \(m,d\geq2\). By contrast, if \(m=1\) or \(d=1\), every matrix difference has rank at most one, so rank-one convexity is ordinary convexity and \(Rf=Cf\); under the standard finite-growth setting, quasiconvexity also reduces to convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Envelope notions coincide in scalar or one-dimensional gradient settings but can separate in genuinely vectorial matrix spaces, where rank-one tests do not capture all gradient oscillations.
knowledge_statements.title: Envelope Separation Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The scalar-collapse discussion fits the failure-boundary container, but strict vectorial separation and the relation of the chosen lamination envelope to the other envelopes require cited examples and precise dimensional and regularity hypotheses.

children.title: Cell-Formula Representations
children.top_down_role: Local variational representations of relaxed densities.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Periodic alternative under finite continuous growth hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(Y=(0,1)^d\), a finite continuous density with standard \(p\)-growth satisfies \[Qf(A)=\inf\left\{\int_Y f(A+\nabla\varphi(y))\,dy:\varphi\in W^{1,p}_{\mathrm{per}}(Y;\mathbb R^m),\ \int_Y\varphi\,dy=0\right\}.\] The zero-mean condition only fixes the additive constant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The quasiconvex cell value can equivalently be computed using periodic zero-mean fluctuations.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is finite and continuous with standard \(p\)-growth.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Qf(A)=\inf_{\varphi\in W^{1,p}_{\mathrm{per}}(Y),\ \int_Y\varphi=0}\int_Yf(A+\nabla\varphi)\,dy\).

notation.meaning: Periodic Sobolev perturbations on the reference cell

knowledge_statements.title: Periodic Cell Representation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Autonomous finite continuous densities with standard growth.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\subset\mathbb R^d\) be a bounded Lipschitz domain and let \(f:\mathbb R^{m\times d}\to[0,+\infty)\) be continuous with standard \(p\)-growth. Then \(\mathcal Z_Df(A)=|D|^{-1}\inf_{\varphi\in W^{1,p}_0(D;\mathbb R^m)}\int_D f(A+\nabla\varphi)\,dx\) is independent of the chosen bounded Lipschitz test domain and equals \(Qf(A)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The normalized Dirichlet cell value is independent of the bounded Lipschitz reference cell and represents the quasiconvex envelope.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is finite and continuous with standard \(p\)-growth.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal Z_Df(A)=Qf(A)\) for every \(A\).
knowledge_statements.title: Cell-Domain Invariance

assumptions_latex: \(Y=(0,1)^d\), and \(f:\mathbb R^{m\times d}\to[0,+\infty)\) is continuous with standard \(p\)-growth.
Zero-boundary perturbations are taken in \(W^{1,p}_0(Y;\mathbb R^m)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The relaxed homogeneous density is represented by a local cell minimization over microscopic perturbations.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard Dirichlet cell formula for quasiconvexification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Homogeneous first-order density; the formula uses one reference cell.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times d}\), define \[f_{\mathrm{cell}}(A)=\inf_{\varphi\in W^{1,p}_0(Y;\mathbb R^m)}\int_Y f(A+\nabla\varphi(y))\,dy.\] The affine boundary condition is encoded by \(Ay+\varphi(y)=Ay\) on \(\partial Y\), while the average gradient remains \(A\). Under hypotheses for which the one-cell formula represents quasiconvexification, \(f_{\mathrm{cell}}=Qf\), and the relaxed functional is \[\overline I(u)=\int_\Omega f_{\mathrm{cell}}(\nabla u(x))\,dx.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relaxed density can be computed locally by minimizing microscopic energy on a reference cell subject to an affine macroscopic boundary condition.
knowledge_statements.title: Cell-Formula Representations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cell representation fits the leaf, but equality of the one-cell formula with Qf, including the use of W^{1,p}_0 rather than another test class, requires a source with exact hypotheses.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(\Omega=(0,1)\), let \[z_j(x)=\mathbf 1_{[0,1/2)}(\{jx\}),\] where \(\{\cdot\}\) denotes fractional part. Then \((z_j)\) generates the homogeneous Young measure \[\nu_x=\tfrac12\delta_0+\tfrac12\delta_1\quad\text{for a.e. }x,\] and \(z_j\rightharpoonup\tfrac12\) in every finite \(L^p\), but \(z_j\) does not converge in measure to \(1/2\).

children.title: Generalized Young Measures
children.top_down_role: Joint representations of oscillation and concentration.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduction of a generalized Young measure to the classical no-concentration regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If an \(L^1\)-bounded generating sequence \((z_j)\) is equiintegrable, then its generalized Young measure satisfies \(\lambda=0\), so the representation reduces to the classical fibers \((\nu_x)\). Conversely, \(\lambda\ne0\) certifies failure of equiintegrability along the generating subsequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equiintegrable sequences have no concentration component, while a nonzero concentration measure detects loss of equiintegrability.
assumptions_latex: \((z_j)\subset L^1(\Omega;\mathbb R^N)\) generates \((\nu_x,\lambda,\nu_x^\infty)\) in a fixed generalized Young-measure framework.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((z_j)\text{ equiintegrable}\Rightarrow\lambda=0\), and \(\lambda\ne0\Rightarrow(z_j)\text{ is not equiintegrable}\).
knowledge_statements.title: Equiintegrability Eliminates Concentration

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical concentrating sequence requiring a nonzero concentration measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(\Omega=(0,1)\), let \(z_j=j\mathbf 1_{(0,1/j)}\). Then \(\|z_j\|_{L^1}=1\), \(z_j\to0\) in measure, and the classical oscillation fibers are \(\nu_x=\delta_0\) almost everywhere. Nevertheless, \[z_j\,dx\stackrel{*}{\rightharpoonup}\delta_0\] as measures on \([0,1]\); in the generalized representation this mass is recorded by \(\lambda=\delta_0\) and positive concentration direction \(\nu_0^\infty=\delta_1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A unit amount of mass concentrated into shrinking intervals disappears from classical fibers but is retained by the generalized concentration component.
assumptions_latex: \(\Omega=(0,1)\), with generalized Young measures allowed to record boundary concentration on \(\overline\Omega\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The sequence has classical fibers \(\delta_0\) but a nonzero concentration measure \(\lambda=\delta_0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Concentration Invisible to Classical Fibers

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear-growth representation separating oscillation from concentration magnitude and direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A generalized Young measure on \(\Omega\) is a triple \((
u_x,\lambda,
u_x^\infty)\), where \((
u_x)_{x\in\Omega}\) is a weakly measurable family of probability measures on \(\mathbb R^N\), \(\lambda\) is a finite positive Radon measure on \(\overline\Omega\), and \((

u_x,gangle\,dx+\langle

assumptions_latex: \(\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d\) is bounded and open, and \((z_j)_j\) is bounded in \(L^1(\Omega;\mathbb R^N)\) but need not be equiintegrable.

children.title: Measure-Valued Minimizers
children.top_down_role: Generalized minimizers represented by parameterized measures.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elementary pointwise example showing strict improvement by non-Dirac fibers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f(t)=(t^2-1)^2\), impose barycenter zero. The Dirac state \(\delta_0\) has energy \(f(0)=1\), whereas \[\mu=\tfrac12\delta_{-1}+\tfrac12\delta_1\] has barycenter zero and energy \(\int f\,d\mu=0\). Thus measure-valued mixing strictly improves upon the ordinary state with the same barycenter.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A symmetric mixture of the two wells has zero energy, while the ordinary zero state has positive energy.
assumptions_latex: The only pointwise constraint is that the probability measure have barycenter zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\int f\,d(\tfrac12\delta_{-1}+\tfrac12\delta_1)=0<1=f(0)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex Density Benefits from Mixing

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Barycentric Convexification and Affine Dual Form
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise measure-valued relaxation under a prescribed barycenter, without differential constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^N\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and bounded below by an affine function. Under the moment and tightness conditions needed to define the expressions, \[f^{**}(z)=\inf_{\substack{\mu\in\mathcal P(\mathbb R^N)\\\int\lambda\,d\mu=z}}\int f(\lambda)\,d\mu(\lambda)=\sup_{\substack{a\in\mathbb R^N,\ b\in\mathbb R\\a\cdot\lambda+b\le f(\lambda)\ \forall\lambda}}(a\cdot z+b).\] Thus optimal non-Dirac fibers represent convex mixtures, while affine minorants give the dual value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Expected-energy minimization over probability measures with fixed barycenter produces the lower-semicontinuous convex envelope, equivalently the supremum of affine minorants.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper and bounded below by an affine function.
The probability measures have the moments required for their barycenters and energies.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The barycentrically constrained measure problem and its affine-minorant dual both have value \(f^{**}(z)\).

The admissible class is preserved by fiberwise barycentric replacement.

For \(
u=(
u_x)_{x\in\Omega}\in\mathcal A\), define the averaged energy \[\mathcal I(
u)=\int_\Omega\int_{\mathbb R^N}f(\lambda)\,d
u_x(\lambda)\,dx.\] A measure-valued minimizer is an element \(
u^*\in\mathcal A\) satisfying \[\mathcal I(

children.title: Lavrentiev Gap Phenomena
children.top_down_role: Discrepancies between infima over nested admissible regularity classes.

children.title: Regularity-Class Gaps
children.top_down_role: Gaps among Sobolev, Lipschitz, smooth, and related admissible classes.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical one-dimensional gap between absolutely continuous and Lipschitz competitors with identical endpoints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F(u)=\int_0^1 (u(x)^3-x)^2|u'(x)|^6\,dx\), with \(u(0)=0\) and \(u(1)=1\), the absolutely continuous map \(u(x)=x^{1/3}\) has zero energy, whereas the infimum over admissible Lipschitz maps is strictly positive. Thus \(\inf_{AC}F=0<\inf_{W^{1,\infty}}F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Manià's functional has zero energy at a non-Lipschitz absolutely continuous map but a positive Lipschitz infimum.
assumptions_latex: Competitors are absolutely continuous on \([0,1]\) with \(u(0)=0\) and \(u(1)=1\).
The stricter class is \(W^{1,\infty}(0,1)\) with the same endpoints.
knowledge_statements.title: Manià's Lavrentiev Example

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Admissible classes differing only in regularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(Y_2\subset Y_1\subset X\), then \(\inf_XF\leq\inf_{Y_1}F\leq\inf_{Y_2}F\). Strengthening the regularity requirement therefore cannot decrease the variational value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Variational values increase monotonically as the admissible regularity class becomes smaller.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_XF\leq\inf_{Y_1}F\leq\inf_{Y_2}F\).
knowledge_statements.title: Nested-Class Value Monotonicity

assumptions_latex: \\(\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^d\) is bounded and open, and \\(1\le p<\infty\).
\\(F(u)=\int_\Omega f(x,u(x),\nabla u(x))\,dx\) is defined on an admissible class \\(X\subset W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^m)\).
\\(Y\subset X\) is a stricter admissible class, such as Lipschitz or smooth maps satisfying the same constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \\(\inf_{u\in X}F(u)<\inf_{u\in Y}F(u)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a Lavrentiev gap between nested Sobolev and more regular admissible classes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A regularity-class gap for \\(F\) between \\(X\) and \\(Y\subset X\) occurs when
\\[\inf_{u\in X}F(u)<\inf_{u\in Y}F(u).\]
The infimum of the empty set is understood as \\(+\infty\). The definition compares classes carrying identical boundary and side constraints; only their regularity differs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A regularity-class gap occurs when minimizing over a stricter Lipschitz or smooth class gives a strictly larger value than minimizing over the containing Sobolev class.
knowledge_statements.title: Regularity-Class Gaps

children.title: Boundary-Approximation Gaps
children.top_down_role: Failure of energy-preserving approximation under boundary restrictions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Trace-Preserving Recovery Is Sufficient for No Gap
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient recovery condition excluding a boundary-approximation gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If every \(u\in X_g\) with \(F(u)<+\infty\) admits \(u_n\in Y_g\) with the same prescribed trace, \(u_n\to u\), and \(\limsup_nF(u_n)\le F(u)\), then \(\inf_{X_g}F=\inf_{Y_g}F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Trace-preserving energy-recovery sequences for all finite-energy Sobolev competitors rule out the gap.
assumptions_latex: Every finite-energy point of \(X_g\) admits a trace-preserving recovery sequence in \(Y_g\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \inf_{u\in X_g}F(u)=\inf_{u\in Y_g}F(u).
knowledge_statements.title: Trace-Preserving Recovery Is Sufficient for No Gap

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Norm Density Alone Does Not Ensure Energy Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinction between trace-preserving topological density and recovery of energy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Even when \(Y_g\) is dense in \(X_g\), equality of infima does not follow without suitable upper recovery of the energy along approximating sequences. The relevant sufficient property is \(u_n\to u\) together with \(\limsup_nF(u_n)\le F(u)\), not convergence alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Trace-preserving norm density does not by itself exclude a boundary gap.
assumptions_latex: \(Y_g\) is dense in \(X_g\) in the chosen topology.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \overline{Y_g}=X_g\centernot\Rightarrow\inf_{X_g}F=\inf_{Y_g}F\text{ without energy control}.
knowledge_statements.title: Norm Density Alone Does Not Ensure Energy Recovery

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representation of the gap through regular exact-trace competitors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(\overline F_{Y_g}(u)=\inf\{\liminf_{n\to\infty}F(u_n):u_n\in Y_g,\ u_n\to u\}\). Then \(\inf_{X_g}\overline F_{Y_g}=\inf_{Y_g}F\). Hence a boundary-approximation gap is equivalent to \(\inf_{X_g}F<\inf_{X_g}\overline F_{Y_g}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The boundary gap is the difference between the Sobolev infimum and the infimum of the relaxation generated by regular exact-trace competitors.
assumptions_latex: A sequential relaxation topology is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \inf_{Y_g}F=\inf_{X_g}\overline F_{Y_g}.

notation.meaning: Sequential relaxation envelope generated by regular exact-trace competitors

knowledge_statements.title: Boundary-Restricted Relaxation Envelope

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical one-dimensional integral-energy gap with identical endpoint data in the Sobolev and Lipschitz classes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[F(u)=\int_0^1 (u(x)^3-x)^2|u'(x)|^6\,dx,\qquad u(0)=0,\quad u(1)=1.\]
The map \(u_*(x)=x^{1/3}\) belongs to \(W^{1,1}(0,1)\), satisfies the endpoint data, and has \(F(u_*)=0\). By the Manià gap phenomenon, Lipschitz competitors satisfying the same endpoint data have infimum strictly above zero. Hence
\[\inf_{\substack{u\in W^{1,1}(0,1)\\u(0)=0,\,u(1)=1}}F(u)=0<\inf_{\substack{u\in W^{1,\infty}(0,1)\\u(0)=0,\,u(1)=1}}F(u).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Manià's integral has zero energy at the singular Sobolev map x^(1/3), while exact-boundary Lipschitz competitors have a strictly positive infimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \inf_{u\in X_g}F(u)=0<\inf_{u\in Y_g}F(u).
knowledge_statements.title: Manià Exact-Boundary Lavrentiev Gap
Boundary-Approximation Gaps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a value gap between Sobolev and more regular competitors subject to identical exact trace constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A boundary-approximation gap occurs when
\[\inf_{u\in X_g}F(u)<\inf_{u\in Y_g}F(u).\]
Here both classes carry the same prescribed trace, while \(Y_g\) imposes additional regularity. Energy-recovery density of \(Y_g\) in \(X_g\) would preclude this strict inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A boundary-approximation gap occurs when regular competitors satisfying the exact prescribed boundary data have a strictly larger infimum than Sobolev competitors with the same trace.
assumptions_latex: \(\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^d\) is a bounded Lipschitz domain, \(1\le p<\infty\), and \(g\) is admissible trace data.
\(Y_g\subset X_g\) is a class of more regular competitors satisfying the same trace condition exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{u\in X_g}F(u)<\inf_{u\in Y_g}F(u)\).

notation.meaning: More regular competitors with trace g

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Builder example is not an integral-energy example and therefore does not complete this integral-variational leaf.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The proposed construction assigns \(F(u_0)=0\) and \(F(u)=1\) otherwise on an arbitrary metric space with a dense proper subset. It proves only an abstract discontinuous-functional fact and does not exhibit an integral functional, a Sobolev trace class, or a boundary-induced approximation obstruction.

children.title: Gap Nonoccurrence Regimes
children.top_down_role: Structural settings in which regular approximation preserves variational values.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nested admissible classes with finite full-class infimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y\subset X\) and \(\alpha=\inf_{u\in X}F(u)\in\mathbb R\). Then \(\inf_YF=\inf_XF\) if and only if for every \(\varepsilon>0\) there exists \(v_\varepsilon\in Y\) with \(F(v_\varepsilon)\leq\alpha+\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: There is no gap exactly when the regular class contains competitors arbitrarily close to the full-class infimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_YF=\inf_XF\iff(\forall\varepsilon>0)(\exists v_\varepsilon\in Y)\ F(v_\varepsilon)\leq\inf_XF+\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.title: Value-Level Certificate for Gap Nonoccurrence

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sobolev classes for which approximation preserves every side constraint; boundary-sensitive approximation belongs to the boundary-gap sibling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subset W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)\), let \(Y\subset X\) be strongly \(W^{1,p}\)-dense in \(X\), and let \(F(u)=\int_\Omega f(x,u,\nabla u)\,dx\). If \(f\) is Carathéodory, finite, and satisfies \(|f(x,s,A)|\leq C(1+|s|^p+|A|^p)\), then \(F\) is continuous along strongly convergent \(W^{1,p}\) sequences and \(\inf_YF=\inf_XF\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong Sobolev density excludes a gap when the energy is continuous for strong Sobolev convergence.
assumptions_latex: \(Y\) is strongly dense in \(X\) while preserving all constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{v\in Y}F(v)=\inf_{u\in X}F(u)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Strong-Density Nonoccurrence Regime

assumptions_latex: \\(Y\subset X\) are nonempty admissible classes for \\(F:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\).
For every \\(u\in X\) there exists \\((u_k)\subset Y\) with \\(u_k\to u\) in the chosen admissible topology.
Every such recovery sequence can be chosen so that \\(\limsup_k F(u_k)\le F(u)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \\(\inf_{v\in Y}F(v)=\inf_{u\in X}F(u)\).
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A general recovery-density criterion excluding Lavrentiev gaps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Because \\(Y\subset X\), one has \\(\inf_XF\le\inf_YF\). If every \\(u\in X\) has a recovery sequence \\((u_k)\subset Y\) satisfying \\(\limsup_kF(u_k)\le F(u)\), then
\\[\inf_{v\in Y}F(v)=\inf_{u\in X}F(u).\]
Thus energy-recovery density of the regular class is sufficient for nonoccurrence of a regularity-class gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: No gap occurs when every admissible competitor can be approximated by regular competitors whose limiting energy does not exceed its energy.
knowledge_statements.title: Gap Nonoccurrence Regimes

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C_n(t)=\operatorname{epi}f_n(t,\cdot)\subset\mathbb R^{d+1}\) be nonempty measurable closed-valued multifunctions. children.title: Dual Convergence Failures

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A nonconvex remote negative well disappears in the primal epi-limit but changes the dual epi-limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(n\ge1\), define \(f_n:\mathbb R\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) by
\[f_n(0)=0,\qquad f_n(n)=-n,\qquad f_n(x)=+\infty\quad(x\notin\{0,n\}).\]
Then \(f_n\xrightarrow{e}\delta_{\{0\}}\), whereas
\[f_n^*(y)=\max\{0,n(y+1)\}\xrightarrow{e}\delta_{(-\infty,-1]}(y),\]
which differs from \(\delta_{\{0\}}^*(y)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A remote nonconvex negative well vanishes from the primal epi-limit but produces a different epi-limit for the conjugates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f_n\xrightarrow{e}\delta_{\{0\}}\) but \(f_n^*\not\xrightarrow{e}\delta_{\{0\}}^*\).

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \\(f_n\xrightarrow{e}\delta_{\{0\}}\), but \\(f_n^*\) does not epi-converge to \\(\delta_{\{0\}}^*=0\).

The proper lower-semicontinuous, nonconvex functions \\(f_n\) satisfy \\(f_n\xrightarrow{e}\delta_{\{0\}}\). Their conjugates are
\\[f_n^*(y)=\max\{0,ny+n^2\}.\]
Hence \\(f_n^*(y)\to+\infty\) for every fixed \\(y\in\mathbb{R}\), whereas \\(\delta_{\{0\}}^*(y)=0\). Thus conjugation need not preserve epigraphical convergence without convexity-compatible hypotheses.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Measurable Selection Criterion for Recovery Multifunctions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Kuratowski–Ryll-Nardzewski-type selection condition used in pointwise recovery constructions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((T,\Sigma,\mu)\) be a complete finite measure space and \(X\) a Polish space. Suppose each \(R_n:T\rightrightarrows X\) has nonempty closed values and is weakly measurable, meaning \(\{t:R_n(t)\cap O\ne\varnothing\}\in\Sigma\) for every open \(O\subset X\). Then \(R_n\) admits a measurable selector \(u_n\). If membership also implies \(d(u_n(t),u(t))\le\varepsilon_n(t)\) and \(f_n(t,u_n(t))\le f(t,u(t))+\varepsilon_n(t)\), where \(\varepsilon_n\ge0\) and \(\|\varepsilon_n\|_{L^1}\to0\), then \(u_n\to u\) in measure and \(\limsup_n I_n(u_n)\le I(u)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weakly measurable nonempty closed recovery sets in a Polish space admit measurable selectors; integrably vanishing distance and energy errors produce integral recovery.
assumptions_latex: \((T,\Sigma,\mu)\) is complete and finite and \(X\) is Polish.
Each \(R_n\) is weakly measurable with nonempty closed values.
The pointwise distance and energy estimates hold with \(\varepsilon_n\to0\) in \(L^1\), and the displayed integrals are well defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists u_n\text{ measurable}:u_n(t)\in R_n(t)\ \text{a.e.},\quad u_n\to u\text{ in measure},\quad\limsup_nI_n(u_n)\le I(u).
knowledge_statements.title: Measurable Selection Criterion for Recovery Multifunctions

assumptions_latex: \((T,\Sigma,\mu)\) is a complete finite measure space and \(X\) is Polish.
Each \(f_n:T\times X\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) is a normal integrand, and \(u:T\to X\) is measurable with \(f(\cdot,u(\cdot))\in L^1(\mu)\).
There are measurable \(\varepsilon_n\ge0\) with \(\|\varepsilon_n\|_{L^1}\to0\), and the multifunctions \(R_n(t)\) below have nonempty measurable graphs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any measurable selections \(u_n(t)\in R_n(t)\) satisfy \(u_n\to u\) in measure and \(\limsup_n I_n(u_n)\le I(u)\).

notation.meaning: Integral functionals of the approximating and limit integrands

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: measurable-selection recovery criterion for integral epilimits
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient measurable-selection criterion for constructing an upper-epilimit recovery sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[R_n(t):=\{y\in X:d(y,u(t))\le\varepsilon_n(t),\ f_n(t,y)\le f(t,u(t))+\varepsilon_n(t)\}.\] By measurable selection, choose a measurable \(u_n\) with \(u_n(t)\in R_n(t)\) almost everywhere. Then \(d(u_n,u)\to0\) in measure. Moreover, integration of the defining inequality gives \[I_n(u_n)\le I(u)+\|\varepsilon_n\|_{L^1},\qquad \limsup_{n\to\infty}I_n(u_n)\le I(u).\] Thus measurable pointwise recovery selections yield a recovery sequence for the integral functional.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Measurable pointwise selections that approach the target and incur integrably vanishing excess form an upper-epilimit recovery sequence.
knowledge_statements.title: Measurable Recovery Selections

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The measurable-selection conclusion depends on precise graph measurability, closed-value, and selection-theorem hypotheses that are not sourced. The statement also contains proof-style derivation and does not fully introduce the limit integrand f.

children.title: Recovery Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Obstructions to measurable or variational recovery.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Integral-functional example where exact low-energy choices cannot approach the target state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\) be a one-point probability space and identify measurable fields with \(\mathbb R\). Define \(f_n(t,x)=0\) for \(x=1\) and \(+\infty\) otherwise, while \(f(t,x)=0\) for \(x=0\) and \(+\infty\) otherwise. At the target \(u=0\), every sequence with finite approximating energy satisfies \(u_n=1\), so it cannot converge to \(u\). Hence no recovery sequence exists despite exact pointwise energy minimization for every \(n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact low-energy choices may remain separated from the target topology, preventing recovery even when there is no integration error.
assumptions_latex: The ambient topology is the usual topology of \(\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: I(0)=0,\qquad u_n\to0\Longrightarrow\limsup_nI_n(u_n)=+\infty.
knowledge_statements.title: Topology Mismatch Obstructs Recovery

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonempty pointwise recovery sets having no admissible measurable selector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T=(0,1)\) carry the Lebesgue sigma-algebra and let \(A\subset T\) be non-Lebesgue-measurable. Define \(R(t)=\{1\}\) for \(t\in A\) and \(R(t)=\{0\}\) otherwise. Every pointwise selector equals \(\mathbf1_A\), so no Lebesgue-measurable selector exists, even up to an almost-everywhere modification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recovery sets can be nonempty everywhere but admit no measurable selector when their graph encodes a nonmeasurable set.
assumptions_latex: Admissible recovery fields must be Lebesgue measurable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R(t)\ne\varnothing\ \forall t,\qquad\nexists u\text{ measurable with }u(t)\in R(t)\ \text{a.e.}
knowledge_statements.title: Measurability Obstruction to Pointwise Recovery
Recovery Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concentration failure caused by absence of domination or uniform integrability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T=(0,1)\), \(f_n(t,x)=n\mathbf 1_{(0,1/n)}(t)\), and \(f(t,x)=0\). Then \(f_n(t,x)\to f(t,x)\) for every \((t,x)\in T\times\mathbb R\), whereas for every measurable \(u_n:T\to\mathbb R\), \[I_n(u_n)=\int_0^1 f_n(t,u_n(t))\,dt=1\] and \(I(u)=0\). Hence no sequence satisfies \(\limsup_{n\to\infty}I_n(u_n)\le I(u)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The integrands converge pointwise to zero, but their integrals remain one for every decision sequence, so pointwise recovery alone does not yield an integral recovery sequence.
assumptions_latex: \(T=(0,1)\) has Lebesgue measure, \(X=\mathbb R\), and the integrands are independent of the decision variable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Pointwise integrand convergence does not imply \(\limsup_{n\to\infty}I_n(u_n)\le I(u)\) without suitable integral control.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: elementary concentration counterexample to interchange of pointwise convergence and integration

children.title: Equicoercive Integral Families
children.top_down_role: Uniform compactness structures accompanying functional convergence.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard integral-functional condition producing uniform compactness in strong \(L^p\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d\) be bounded with Lipschitz boundary and \(1<p<\infty\). On an admissible class having a common trace condition or normalization, define \(F_n(u)=\int_\Omega f_n(x,u,\nabla u)\,dx\). If \(f_n(x,z,\xi)\ge c|\xi|^p-C\) almost everywhere with \(c>0\) and \(C\ge0\) independent of \(n\), and a uniform Poincare inequality controls \(u\), then every uniformly energy-bounded sequence is bounded in \(W^{1,p}(\Omega)\) and relatively compact in \(L^p(\Omega)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform gradient p-growth plus common Poincare control yields Sobolev boundedness and strong-Lp equicoercivity.
assumptions_latex: The common admissible class satisfies a uniform Poincare inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sup_nF_n(u_n)<\infty\Longrightarrow (u_n)\text{ is relatively compact in }L^p(\Omega).

notation.meaning: Integral functionals on the common Sobolev class

knowledge_statements.title: Sobolev Growth Criterion for Equicoercivity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational consequence of equicoercivity for variationally convergent integral families.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \((F_n)\) is equicoercive on a metric space \(X\) and \(\sup_nF_n(u_n)<+\infty\), then \((u_n)\) has a convergent subsequence. Consequently, approximate minimizers satisfying \(F_n(u_n)\le\inf_XF_n+o(1)\) are relatively compact whenever \(\sup_n\inf_XF_n<+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equicoercivity makes bounded-energy sequences, including bounded-value approximate minimizers, precompact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists n_k\uparrow\infty,\ u\in X:\ u_{n_k}\to u.
knowledge_statements.title: Compactness of Bounded-Energy Sequences
Equicoercive Integral Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform compact containment of bounded-energy sublevels for a family of integral functionals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A family \((F_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}\) is equicoercive on a topological space \(X\) if, for every \(c\in\mathbb R\), there exists a compact set \(K_c\subset X\) such that \[\{u\in X:F_n(u)\le c\}\subset K_c\qquad\text{for every }n\in\mathbb N.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A family is equicoercive when, at every finite energy level, one compact set contains the corresponding sublevel of every functional in the family.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a topological space and \(F_n:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) for every \(n\in\mathbb N\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(c\in\mathbb R\), the union \(\bigcup_{n\in\mathbb N}\{u\in X:F_n(u)\le c\}\) is contained in a compact subset of \(X\).
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: Integral Limit Representation
children.top_down_role: Conditions under which a variational limit retains a local integral form.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary structural conditions for a nonnegative localized functional to admit a pointwise integral density.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(F(u,A)=\int_A f(t,u(t))\,d\mu(t)\) with \(f\ge0\), then for every \(u\), \(A\mapsto F(u,A)\) is a countably additive measure absolutely continuous with respect to \(\mu\). Moreover, if \(u=v\) almost everywhere on \(A\), then \(F(u,A)=F(v,A)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative pointwise integral representation forces absolute continuity and countable additivity in the set variable and locality in the state.
assumptions_latex: \(f:T\times\mathbb R^m\to[0,+\infty]\) is measurable enough for the integrals to be defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F(u,\cdot)\ll\mu,\qquad u=v\ \mu\text{-a.e. on }A\Longrightarrow F(u,A)=F(v,A).
knowledge_statements.title: Necessary Locality and Measure Conditions

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Qualified density uniqueness; continuity replaces the builder's invalid lower-semicontinuity dense-set claim.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) and \(g\) have finite integrable constant sections at every \(q\in\mathbb Q^m\), and suppose \(f(t,\cdot)\) and \(g(t,\cdot)\) are continuous for almost every \(t\). If \(\int_A f(t,q)\,d\mu=\int_A g(t,q)\,d\mu\) for every \(A\in\Sigma\) and \(q\in\mathbb Q^m\), then there is one full-measure set on which \(f(t,z)=g(t,z)\) for every \(z\in\mathbb R^m\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Localized equality on rational constant fields identifies continuous fiber densities almost everywhere.
assumptions_latex: For every \(q\in\mathbb Q^m\), the sections \(f(\cdot,q)\) and \(g(\cdot,q)\) are finite and integrable.
The fibers of both integrands are continuous almost everywhere.
The localized integral identities hold for every measurable set and rational constant field.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f(t,z)=g(t,z)\quad\text{for almost every }t\text{ and every }z\in\mathbb R^m.
knowledge_statements.title: Uniqueness Under Almost-Everywhere Fiber Continuity

assumptions_latex: \((T,\Sigma,\mu)\) is a finite measure space, \(1\le p<\infty\), and \(F:L^p(T;\mathbb R^m)\times\Sigma\to[0,+\infty]\).
For each \(u\), the map \(A\mapsto F(u,A)\) is a finite measure absolutely continuous with respect to \(\mu\); \(F\) is local and strongly lower semicontinuous in \(u\).
There exist \(a\in L^1_+(\mu)\) and \(C>0\) such that \(F(u,A)\le\int_A(a+C|u|^p)\,d\mu\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There is a measurable lower-semicontinuous density \(f\) representing \(F\) by integration, uniquely up to \(\mu\)-null sets on values probed by \(L^p\).
review_flags: exact representation theorem and hypotheses need source verification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A finite-measure, zeroth-order local representation; gradient-dependent versions require different hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the stated locality, measure, lower-semicontinuity, and growth hypotheses, there exists a normal integrand \(f:T\times\mathbb R^m\to[0,+\infty]\) such that, for every \(u\in L^p(T;\mathbb R^m)\) and \(A\in\Sigma\), \[F(u,A)=\int_A f(t,u(t))\,d\mu(t).\] In particular, the variational limit retains a local integral form rather than acquiring a nonlocal dependence on \(u\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local lower-semicontinuous limit with measure structure and p-growth admits representation by a measurable pointwise density.
knowledge_statements.title: Integral Limit Representation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The existence of a normal-integrand representation and the stated uniqueness qualification require an exact integral-representation theorem. The supplied hypotheses may need additional structural or continuity conditions, so the mathematical version cannot be validated from standard-field rationale alone.

children.title: Stability of Integral Minimization
children.top_down_role: Consequences of variational convergence for values and solution mappings.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Chapter 7.E and 7.J: Convergence in Minimization; Solution Estimates

children.title: Optimal-Value Stability
children.top_down_role: Convergence and semicontinuity of infimal values.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proper epi-limit with nonconvergent infimal values caused by loss of compactness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(\mathbb R\), define \[F_n(x)=\min\{x^2,-1+(x-n)^2\}.\] Then \(F_n\) epiconverges to \(F(x)=x^2\), while \[\inf F_n=-1\quad\text{for every }n,\qquad \inf F=0.\] Thus epiconvergence without compactness of near-minimizers does not ensure optimal-value convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lower well moving to infinity disappears from the epi-limit while continuing to determine every prelimit optimal value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F_n\xrightarrow{e}x^2\text{ but }\inf F_n=-1\not\to0=\inf F.
knowledge_statements.title: Escaping Wells Destroy Value Convergence

knowledge_statements.scope_note: The value inequality supplied without compactness assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(F_n\) epiconverges to \(F\), then recovery sequences imply \[\limsup_{n\to\infty}\inf_XF_n\le F(x)\quad(x\in X),\] and hence \[\limsup_{n\to\infty}\inf_XF_n\le\inf_XF.\] The reverse inequality is not automatic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Epiconvergence alone supplies the upper bound on infimal values; compactness of near-minimizers is needed for the reverse bound.
assumptions_latex: \(F_n\) epiconverges to \(F\) on a metrizable space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \limsup_n\inf_XF_n\le\inf_XF.
knowledge_statements.title: One-Sided Optimal-Value Bound Under Epiconvergence

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential compactness formulation of optimal-value stability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_n\) epiconverge to a proper \(F\), let \(m_n=\inf_XF_n\in\mathbb R\) eventually, and assume \((m_n)\) is bounded above. Suppose that for every sequence \(\varepsilon_n\downarrow0\), every choice \(x_n\) satisfying \(F_n(x_n)\le m_n+\varepsilon_n\) has a convergent subsequence. Then \[\lim_{n\to\infty}m_n=\inf_XF.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Epiconvergence yields convergence of optimal values when finite almost-minimizers cannot escape.
assumptions_latex: \(m_n=\inf_XF_n\) is finite eventually and bounded above.
Every vanishing-error almost-minimizing sequence is sequentially precompact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \inf_XF_n\to\inf_XF.
knowledge_statements.title: Value Convergence from Compact Almost-Minimizers

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is metrizable, \(F_n:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) epiconverges to a proper functional \(F\).
The family \((F_n)\) is equicoercive and \(\inf_XF_n<+\infty\) eventually.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The optimal values converge: \(\lim_n\inf_XF_n=\inf_XF\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: fundamental theorem of epiconvergence under equicoercivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global value convergence under epiconvergence and equicoercivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m_n:=\inf_XF_n\) and \(m:=\inf_XF\). The epiliminf inequality and equicoercivity give \(m\le\liminf_nm_n\). If \(x\) minimizes \(F\), or approximates its infimum arbitrarily closely, an epigraphical recovery sequence gives \(\limsup_nm_n\le F(x)\); taking the infimum over such \(x\) yields \(\limsup_nm_n\le m\). Therefore \[\lim_{n\to\infty}m_n=m.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Epiconvergence plus equicoercivity forces convergence of the infimal values of the integral functionals.
knowledge_statements.title: Optimal-Value Stability

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This is a theorem in the correct leaf, but no inspectable source is supplied for the precise topological and equicoercivity hypotheses. The statement also includes a proof outline, which must be removed from a sourced replacement.

children.title: Minimizer Accuracy Stability Regimes
children.top_down_role: Outer-limit behavior of exact and near-minimizing sequences.

children.title: Exact-Minimizer Stability
children.top_down_role: Outer-limit behavior of sequences of exact minimizers.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Outer stability of global exact minimizers, without inner recovery of every limiting minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be metrizable, let \(F_n\xrightarrow{e}F\), suppose \(m_n:=\min_XF_n\to m:=\min_XF\in\mathbb R\), and let \(x_n\in\operatorname{argmin}F_n\). If \((x_n)\) is relatively compact, then every cluster point of \((x_n)\) belongs to \(\operatorname{argmin}F\), and \(F_n(x_n)=m_n\to m\). Equicoercivity is a standard sufficient condition for relative compactness and, in the usual fundamental theorem, for convergence of minima.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every cluster point of a relatively compact sequence of exact prelimit minimizers is a limiting minimizer, and the attained values converge with the minimum values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Limsup}\{x_n\}\subseteq\operatorname{argmin}F\quad\text{and}\quad F_n(x_n)\to\min_XF.\)
knowledge_statements.title: Exact-Minimizer Outer Stability

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is metrizable, \(F_n\) epiconverges to proper \(F\), and \((F_n)\) is equicoercive.
Each \(x_n\) is an exact minimizer of \(F_n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every cluster point of \((x_n)\) belongs to \(\operatorname{argmin}F\), and \(F_n(x_n)\to\min F\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: outer stability of exact minimizers under epiconvergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Outer stability of global exact minimizers; it does not guarantee recovery of every limit minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Equicoercivity makes \((x_n)\) relatively compact. For any subsequence with \(x_{n_k}\to\bar x\), the epiliminf inequality and optimal-value convergence imply \[F(\bar x)\le\liminf_{k\to\infty}F_{n_k}(x_{n_k})=\lim_{k\to\infty}\min_XF_{n_k}=\min_XF.\] Hence \(\bar x\in\operatorname{argmin}F\). Moreover, the full sequence of minimum values satisfies \(F_n(x_n)=\min_XF_n\to\min_XF\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every cluster point of exact minimizers is a limit minimizer, and their attained values converge to the limiting minimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact-Minimizer Stability

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The outer-stability theorem is standard and appropriately classified, but its precise hypotheses and attainment consequences lack an inspectable source. The statement contains proof text.

children.title: Approximate-Minimizer Stability
children.top_down_role: Outer-limit behavior of near-minimizers with vanishing or controlled errors.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Outer stability and value convergence for global approximate minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be metrizable, let \(F_n\xrightarrow{e}F\), suppose \(m_n:=\inf_XF_n\to m:=\min_XF\in\mathbb R\), and let \((x_n)\) be relatively compact. If \(\varepsilon_n\to0\) and \(F_n(x_n)\le m_n+\varepsilon_n\), then every cluster point of \((x_n)\) lies in \(\operatorname{argmin}F\), and \(F_n(x_n)\to m\). Equicoercivity together with the displayed uniform level bound is a standard sufficient condition for the required relative compactness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relatively compact vanishing-error minimizers have only limiting minimizers as cluster points, and their objective values converge to the limiting minimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Limsup}\{x_n\}\subseteq\operatorname{argmin}F\quad\text{and}\quad F_n(x_n)\to\min_XF.\)
knowledge_statements.title: Vanishing-Error Approximate-Minimizer Stability

assumptions_latex: \(F_n:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) epiconverges to proper \(F\), the family is equicoercive, and \(X\) is metrizable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every cluster point of \((x_n)\) minimizes \(F\), and \(F_n(x_n)\to\min_XF\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: approximate-minimizer extension of the fundamental epiconvergence theorem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Outer stability for globally approximate minimizers with vanishing error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Optimal-value convergence gives \(\inf_XF_n\to\inf_XF\). Thus \[\limsup_{n\to\infty}F_n(x_n)\le\inf_XF.\] Equicoercivity supplies cluster points. If \(x_{n_k}\to\bar x\), the epiliminf inequality yields \[F(\bar x)\le\liminf_{k\to\infty}F_{n_k}(x_{n_k})\le\inf_XF,\] so \(\bar x\in\operatorname{argmin}F\). The same inequalities show \(F_n(x_n)\to\min_XF\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Vanishing-error minimizers inherit exact outer stability under epiconvergence and equicoercivity.
knowledge_statements.title: Approximate-Minimizer Stability

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The vanishing-error minimizer theorem fits the leaf, but no source verifies the exact extended-real and attainment hypotheses. The statement also presents a proof outline.

children.title: Accuracy-Regime Transitions
children.top_down_role: Dependence of stability on the scale and decay of optimization error.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp transition from exact limiting minimality to positive-tolerance limiting minimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_n\xrightarrow{e}F\) on a metrizable space, suppose \(m_n:=\inf_XF_n\to m:=\inf_XF\in\mathbb R\), and let \(\varepsilon_n\to\varepsilon\in[0,+\infty)\). If \(F_n(x_n)\le m_n+\varepsilon_n\), then every cluster point \(\bar x\) of \((x_n)\) satisfies \(F(\bar x)\le m+\varepsilon\). Thus \(\varepsilon=0\) yields exact limiting minimality, whereas \(\varepsilon>0\) yields only limiting \(\varepsilon\)-minimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Vanishing errors force cluster points to be exact minimizers; a positive limiting error guarantees only membership in the corresponding limiting tolerance set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{n_k}\to\bar x\implies F(\bar x)\le\inf_XF+\varepsilon.\)
knowledge_statements.title: Limiting-Accuracy Transition
Accuracy-Regime Transitions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transition from guaranteed exact-minimizer stability to fixed-tolerance stability as optimization errors cease to vanish.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be metrizable, let \(F_n:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) epiconverge to a proper functional \(F:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}\), and suppose \((F_n)\) is equicoercive with \(\inf_XF_n\to\inf_XF\). If \(\varepsilon_n\to\varepsilon\in[0,+\infty)\) and \(F_n(x_n)\le\inf_XF_n+\varepsilon_n\), then every cluster point \(\bar x\) of \((x_n)\) satisfies \[F(\bar x)\le\inf_XF+\varepsilon.\] Thus \(\varepsilon=0\) guarantees exact-minimizer stability, whereas \(\varepsilon>0\) guarantees only membership in the limiting \(\varepsilon\)-minimizer set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero limiting optimization error guarantees exact-minimizer stability; a positive limiting error guarantees only limiting epsilon-minimality.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is metrizable, \(F_n:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) epiconverges to proper \(F:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}\), and \((F_n)\) is equicoercive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every cluster point \(\bar x\) satisfies \(F(\bar x)\le\inf_XF+\varepsilon\); when \(\varepsilon=0\), every cluster point minimizes \(F\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: limiting-error transition for approximate minimizers

children.title: Outer-Stability Failures
children.top_down_role: Loss of minimizer containment under inadequate compactness or value control.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Escape of Exact Minimizers Without Equicoercivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of precompactness despite epi-convergence to a coercive limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(x)=x^2\) on \(\mathbb R\) and define \(F_n(n)=-1\) and \(F_n(x)=x^2\) for \(x\ne n\). Then each \(F_n\) is lower semicontinuous and \(F_n\xrightarrow{e}F\), but \(\operatorname{argmin}F_n=\{n\}\). Hence the exact minimizers have no convergent subsequence although \(\operatorname{argmin}F=\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An escaping minimizing well leaves the epi-limit unchanged while forcing every exact minimizer to escape.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_n\xrightarrow{e}F\), but \(\operatorname{argmin}F_n=\{n\}\) is not relatively compact.
knowledge_statements.title: Escape of Exact Minimizers Without Equicoercivity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fixed Accuracy Does Not Give Exact Outer Stability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of exact limiting minimality when approximation errors do not vanish.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_n=F\) on \(\mathbb R\), where \(F(x)=x^2\), and take \(x_n=1\). Then \(F_n\xrightarrow{e}F\), the family is equicoercive, and \(F_n(x_n)=\inf F_n+1\), but \(x_n\to1\notin\operatorname{argmin}F=\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even for a constant coercive objective sequence, fixed-error approximate minimizers can converge outside the exact limiting argmin.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_n(x_n)\le\inf F_n+1\), but \(1\notin\operatorname{argmin}F\).
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed Accuracy Does Not Give Exact Outer Stability
Outer-Stability Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of outer exact-minimizer stability when approximation errors do not vanish.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\mathbb R\), \(F_n=F\) for every \(n\), and \(F(x)=x^2\). The family is equicoercive and epiconverges to \(F\), with \(\operatorname{argmin}F=\{0\}\). For \(x_n=1\), \[F_n(x_n)=1=\inf_{x\in\mathbb R}F_n(x)+1,\] but \(x_n\to1\notin\operatorname{argmin}F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the constant coercive functional x squared, fixed-error approximate minimizers can converge outside the exact minimizer set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Although \(F_n\) epiconverges to \(F\), the cluster point \(1\) is not in \(\operatorname{argmin}F=\{0\}\).

notation.meaning: Constant functional sequence and its limit
