children.top_down_role: Invariant-integral certificates associated with extremal fields.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strict form of the invariant-integral comparison.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the Hilbert identity \[J[y]-J[\bar y]=\int_a^bE(t,y(t),y'(t))\,dt,\] suppose \(E\ge0\) on the comparison tube and \(E(t,x,v)=0\) only for \(v=q(t,x)\). Equality of actions then forces \(y'=q(t,y)\) almost everywhere. If the field ODE has a unique trajectory from the prescribed initial endpoint, every distinct admissible equal-endpoint competitor satisfies \(J[y]>J[\bar y]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict positivity of excess away from the field slope, plus uniqueness of the field trajectory, yields strict minimality.
assumptions_latex: The Hilbert identity holds for the comparison class.
The field ODE has a unique trajectory from the prescribed initial endpoint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: y\ne\bar y\Longrightarrow J[y]>J[\bar y].
knowledge_statements.title: Strict Hilbert-Excess Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Closedness Does Not Ensure Global Path Independence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Topological boundary for global Hilbert invariance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On a nonsimply-connected field tube, \(d\omega=0\) gives local exactness but does not force all periods \(\oint_\gamma\omega\) to vanish. Consequently the Hilbert integral can depend on the homotopy class of a path with fixed endpoints. Global endpoint invariance requires exactness, vanishing periods, or restriction to an appropriate simply connected region.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed Hilbert form is locally invariant, but global endpoint invariance can fail on a multiply connected tube.
assumptions_latex: \(\omega\) is closed on a possibly nonsimply-connected field tube.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d\omega=0\not\Rightarrow\int_\gamma\omega\text{ depends globally only on the endpoints.}
knowledge_statements.title: Closedness Does Not Ensure Global Path Independence

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Extremal Fields Generate a Closed Hilbert Form
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local invariance result underlying the Hilbert integral certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q(t,x)\) be the slope of a sufficiently smooth regular field of Euler–Lagrange extremals and set \(p(t,x)=L_v(t,x,q(t,x))\). Then the Hilbert form \[\omega=\bigl(L(t,x,q)-p\cdot q\bigr)\,dt+p\cdot dx\] is closed. Its integral is invariant under endpoint-fixed homotopies within the field tube; on a simply connected tube, \(\omega=dS\) for a potential \(S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Hilbert one-form of a regular extremal field is closed and is globally exact on a simply connected field tube.
assumptions_latex: \(L\) and the regular extremal field are sufficiently differentiable.
Simple connectivity is assumed only for global exactness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d\omega=0,\qquad \omega=dS\text{ on a simply connected tube.}
knowledge_statements.title: Extremal Fields Generate a Closed Hilbert Form

assumptions_latex: \(L\in C^1(U\times\mathbb R^m)\), where \(U\subset\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^m\) is a simply connected tube.
\(q\in C^1(U;\mathbb R^m)\), and the Hilbert one-form \(\omega\) displayed below is exact on \(U\).
The reference arc satisfies \(\bar y'(t)=q(t,\bar y(t))\), and \(E(t,x,v)\ge 0\) on the comparison domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[J[y]-J[\bar y]=\int_a^b E(t,y(t),y'(t))\,dt\ge 0.\]

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical first-order Hilbert integral on a simply connected extremal-field tube.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(y:[a,b]\to\mathbb R^m\) be piecewise \(C^1\), with graph in \(U\), and have the same endpoints as \(\bar y\). Define
\[\omega=\bigl(L(t,x,q)-L_v(t,x,q)\cdot q(t,x)\bigr)\,dt+L_v(t,x,q)\cdot dx.\]
Exactness makes \(\int_y\omega\) depend only on the endpoints. Since \(\bar y'=q(t,\bar y)\), one has \(J[\bar y]=\int_{\bar y}\omega=\int_y\omega\). Consequently,
\[J[y]-J[\bar y]=\int_a^b\!\bigl[L(t,y,y')-L(t,y,q)-L_v(t,y,q)\cdot(y'-q)\bigr]dt=\int_a^b E(t,y,y')\,dt.\]
Thus nonnegativity of \(E\) certifies minimality among these competitors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact Hilbert integral has the same value on equal-endpoint arcs; subtracting it from the action yields the nonnegative Weierstrass excess, certifying minimality.
knowledge_statements.title: Hilbert Invariant-Integral Family

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Hilbert invariant integral associated with a variational field
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the Hilbert invariant integral and states its exactness, path independence, and reduction on field trajectories.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R\subset\mathbb{R}^{n+1}\) be simply connected, and let \(y_i'=\psi_i(x,y)\), \(i=1,\ldots,n\), define a field for \(\int_a^b F(x,y,y')\,dx\). Write \(p_i=F_{y_i'}(x,y,\psi(x,y))\) and \(H=\sum_{i=1}^n p_i\psi_i-F(x,y,\psi(x,y))\). If \(\partial p_i/\partial y_k=\partial p_k/\partial y_i\) for all \(i,k\) and \(\partial H/\partial y_i=-\partial p_i/\partial x\) for all \(i\), then the one-form \(\omega=-H\,dx+\sum_{i=1}^n p_i\,dy_i\) is exact. Its line integral \(\int_\Gamma\omega\), called Hilbert's invariant integral, depends only on the endpoints of \(\Gamma\). If \(\Gamma\) is a field trajectory, so that \(dy_i=\psi_i(x,y)\,dx\), then \(\int_\Gamma\omega=\int_\Gamma F(x,y,y')\,dx\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In a simply connected region, the self-adjointness and consistency conditions of a variational field make the associated Hilbert one-form exact. Its integral is path independent and, on a field trajectory, reduces to the original variational integral.
assumptions_latex: y_i'=\psi_i(x,y),\quad i=1,\ldots,n,\text{ defines a field for }\int_a^b F(x,y,y')\,dx
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: -H\,dx+\sum_{i=1}^n p_i\,dy_i=dg\text{ for some }g;\quad \int_\Gamma\left(-H\,dx+\sum_{i=1}^n p_i\,dy_i\right)\text{ is path independent and equals }\int_\Gamma F\,dx\text{ when }\Gamma\text{ is a field trajectory}.

children.title: Calibration Methods
children.top_down_role: Comparison-field certificates for global or strong minimality.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact uniqueness condition supplementing non-strict calibrated minimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \[J[u]-J[\bar u]=\int_\Omega(F-\Phi)(x,u,\nabla u)\,dx,\qquad F-\Phi\ge0.\] If saturation \((F-\Phi)(x,u,
abla u)=0\) almost everywhere forces \(u=\bar u\) almost everywhere within \(\mathcal A\), then \(\bar u\) is the unique global minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A calibration proves uniqueness when only the calibrated map can have zero calibration gap.
assumptions_latex: The calibration integral is invariant on \(\mathcal A\).
The calibration gap is measurable and nonnegative.
Its almost-everywhere saturation set identifies \(\bar u\) uniquely in \(\mathcal A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: u\ne\bar u\text{ in }\mathcal A\Longrightarrow J[u]>J[\bar u].
knowledge_statements.title: Strict Calibration Gap Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Null-Lagrangian realization of an abstract integral calibration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G:\overline\Omega\times\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R^n\) be \(C^1\) and define \[\Phi(x,z,P)=\operatorname{div}_xG(x,z)+D_zG(x,z):P.\] Then \(\Phi(x,u,\nabla u)=\operatorname{div}(G(x,u(x)))\), so \[\int_\Omega\Phi(x,u,\nabla u)\,dx=\int_{\partial\Omega}G(x,u)\cdot n\,dS.\] This integral is invariant on a class with common trace. If \(\Phi\le F\) on the admissible jets and equality holds along \(\bar u\), then \(\bar u\) is a global minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A total-divergence minorant is a calibration because its integral is fixed by the boundary trace.
assumptions_latex: The competitors have a common trace and the chain rule and divergence theorem apply.
\(\Phi\le F\) on admissible jets, with equality almost everywhere along \(\bar u\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: J[u]\ge J[\bar u]\quad\forall u\in\mathcal A.
knowledge_statements.title: Divergence Calibration Representation

assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A\) is a class of admissible maps with fixed boundary data, and \(J[u]=\int_\Omega F(x,u(x),\nabla u(x))\,dx\).
A measurable integrand \(\Phi\) satisfies \(\int_\Omega\Phi(x,u,\nabla u)\,dx=C\) for every \(u\in\mathcal A\).
\(\Phi(x,z,\xi)\le F(x,z,\xi)\) on the admissible state-gradient set, with equality almost everywhere along \((\bar u,\nabla\bar u)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[J[u]\ge C=J[\bar u]\quad\text{for every }u\in\mathcal A.\]

notation.meaning: Admissible comparison class with prescribed boundary data.
Calibration integrand whose integral is invariant on the comparison class.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract integral calibration covering comparison fields and null-Lagrangian certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A calibration for \(\bar u\in\mathcal A\) is an integrand \(\Phi\) whose integral is invariant on \(\mathcal A\), lies pointwise below the energy density, and saturates that bound on \(\bar u\). For every \(u\in\mathcal A\),
\[J[u]=\int_\Omega F(x,u,\nabla u)\,dx\ge\int_\Omega\Phi(x,u,\nabla u)\,dx=C.\]
Saturation gives
\[J[\bar u]=\int_\Omega F(x,\bar u,\nabla\bar u)\,dx=\int_\Omega\Phi(x,\bar u,\nabla\bar u)\,dx=C.\]
Hence \(J[u]\ge J[\bar u]\) throughout \(\mathcal A\); strict domination away from the calibrated state yields the corresponding strict-minimality conclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A calibration is an invariant comparison integral lying below the energy and touching it on the reference map; integration then certifies global minimality.
knowledge_statements.title: Calibration Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A calibration certificate is the correct content_kind for this leaf, and the non-strict global-minimality implication follows formally from invariant integral, domination, and saturation. Nevertheless, no relevant source or inspectable locator is supplied. In addition, the domains of \(\Omega\), \(z\), and \(\xi\), the measure and regularity setting, and the admissible state-gradient set are not defined; the final strict-minimality claim also lacks a precise quantified strictness condition ensuring a strict integral gap for every distinct competitor. An authoritative calibration or null-Lagrangian source and a fully specified formulation are required.
